relationships.What evidence establishes: Securities lending involves collateralised temporary borrowing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Zero counterparty risk or guaranteed collateral sufficiency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Mark-to-market and recall risk remain.

relationships.Category: Securities lending, temporary title and market inventory
relationships.Conversion input: Prime-broker balance sheet and lender network
relationships.Conversion output: Borrowed securities and leveraged market access
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Prime brokers convert institutional custody and lender networks into tradable inventory for hedge funds
relationships.What evidence establishes: Prime brokers provide securities lending and financing services to investment funds.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Control of every fund position or guaranteed recall availability.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Inventory and terms change with market conditions.

relationships.Category: Securities lending, temporary title and market inventory
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Recall rights preserve the lender's ability to regain possession for sale, voting or settlement
relationships.What evidence establishes: OFR notes securities-lending contracts often allow lender recall.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Immediate return without settlement risk in every condition.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Borrowers may need to source replacement securities.

relationships.Conversion input: Accounts, securities prices and settlement systems
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A single collateral agent can become critical infrastructure for a large funding market
relationships.What evidence establishes: Federal Reserve sources identify BNY as the tri-party repo clearing and collateral-management bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership of all repo collateral or credit guarantee of all trades.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: BNY provides infrastructure while counterparties retain contract risk.

relationships.Conversion input: Security data, haircuts and account instructions
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Collateral agents convert legal eligibility and market values into operationally usable secured positions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Collateral platforms value, allocate and optimise securities across transactions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of borrower performance or elimination of wrong-way risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Agent processes depend on accurate data and legal arrangements.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Dealers rely on custody infrastructure to transform inventories into secured funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: BNY provides tri-party settlement and collateral services.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: BNY acting as the economic lender in every trade.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The cash lender and borrower remain principal counterparties.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Amount / scale: Approximately 801,000 private retirement plans within wider EBSA coverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Public authority turns benefit law into plan governance and enforcement
relationships.What evidence establishes: EBSA administers and enforces ERISA standards for covered private plans.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of investment performance or coverage of public pension plans.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: ERISA coverage and exemptions vary by plan and transaction.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: An employer converts compensation policy into a long-duration balance-sheet and trust obligation
relationships.What evidence establishes: Defined-benefit plans promise benefits under plan formulas and funding rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Full funding at every date or unlimited sponsor solvency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Funding status and benefit protections vary.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Edge type: Plan establishment, contributions and menu design
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The sponsor converts compensation into a participant-directed savings platform
relationships.What evidence establishes: Sponsors establish defined-contribution plans and select service structures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Sponsor guarantee of account value or every investment outcome.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Participant elections and fiduciary duties remain separate.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Payroll infrastructure converts current income into long-duration financial claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: 401(k) plans receive participant salary deferrals and may receive employer contributions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed return or unrestricted access before retirement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Tax, vesting and withdrawal rules apply.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Edge type: Loyalty, prudence, diversification and expense duties
relationships.Conversion output: Mandated decision process for participant benefit
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fiduciary law constrains delegated financial power
relationships.What evidence establishes: ERISA fiduciaries must act solely in participant interests, prudently and with reasonable expenses.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Positive returns or immunity from all losses.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Duties are process- and context-dependent.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Edge type: Legal holding and authorised transaction execution
relationships.Conversion output: Assets held in trust and operationally administered
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Trust structure separates plan assets from ordinary sponsor property
relationships.What evidence establishes: Plan assets are generally held in trust and administered for participants.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Trustee discretion over every investment decision.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Named fiduciary, trustee and investment-manager powers vary.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Recordkeeping turns pooled custody positions into participant-level claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: Recordkeepers maintain participant account information and process plan activity.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership of plan assets or fiduciary investment authority in every arrangement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Service contracts determine discretion and liability.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Plan design converts non-decision into market exposure
relationships.What evidence establishes: QDIA rules permit qualifying default investments subject to notice and other conditions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Participant endorsement or guarantee of suitability for every person.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Participants can opt out and fiduciaries must prudently select the option.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A glide path automates long-term allocation choices
relationships.What evidence establishes: Target-date products are recognised QDIA forms and adjust asset mix over time.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed principal, sufficient income or identical glide paths.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Design assumptions and fees differ.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Amount / scale: About 22,000 covered single-employer plans in FY2025
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Premiums pool private plan-failure risk into a statutory insurance programme
relationships.What evidence establishes: PBGC operates insurance programmes funded in part by covered-plan premiums.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Full taxpayer funding or coverage of defined-contribution plans.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Programme finances and legal coverage differ by plan type.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Amount / scale: FY2025: more than $6.4 billion paid to nearly 926,000 retirees in single-employer plans
relationships.Conversion output: Monthly benefit up to legal limits
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The public corporation converts a failed private pension promise into a limited insured claim
relationships.What evidence establishes: PBGC pays covered benefits subject to statutory limits after qualifying plan failures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Payment of every promised benefit or rescue of plan sponsors and shareholders.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Limits, phase-ins and plan status matter.

relationships.Conversion output: Illiquid ownership exposure and expected returns
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A long-duration public liability supports delegated private-company ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: CalPERS maintains and reviews a large private-equity programme.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Control of every portfolio company or guaranteed excess return.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Returns, fees, valuations and pacing require programme-level review.

relationships.Amount / scale: June 2025 review reported $49 billion commitments, $19 billion NAV and $31 billion unfunded
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Pension savings are converted into directly negotiated loans through specialist managers
relationships.What evidence establishes: CalPERS reported private-debt commitments, NAV and unfunded commitments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Immediate cash deployment or guaranteed realised returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commitment, NAV and called capital are different measures.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: A national pension pool supplies long-duration capital to non-bank credit markets
relationships.What evidence establishes: CPP Investments reports credit and private-credit investment activity.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Canadian government direction of each loan or guarantee of returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Statutory independence and portfolio governance must be preserved.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Edge type: Proposed prudence safe harbour for asset-allocation funds with alternative assets
relationships.Conversion output: Framework for evaluating private-market exposure in plan menus
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Proposed fiduciary process standards create a possible regulated gate for private-market access to retirement menus
relationships.What evidence establishes: DOL proposed a rule addressing fiduciary selection of diversified options containing alternative assets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A final rule, mandatory allocation or proof that private assets improve outcomes.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Proposal may change, be withdrawn, litigated or adopted differently.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fund shares aggregate dispersed savings into scalable securities ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: Mutual funds issue redeemable pooled interests under the Investment Company Act.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct ownership of each portfolio security.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Share class, fees and redemption mechanics differ.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: An advisory contract converts beneficial capital into delegated investment authority
relationships.What evidence establishes: Registered funds commonly delegate portfolio management to advisers under contracts.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Adviser beneficial ownership of fund assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fund board, law and mandate constrain the adviser.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Independent governance creates an internal accountability interface within pooled funds
relationships.What evidence establishes: Fund boards have statutory and governance duties over advisers and operations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Day-to-day portfolio selection by independent directors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Board effectiveness depends on information, independence and resources.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion output: Segregated custody records and completed settlement
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Custody infrastructure converts trades into protected recorded positions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bank custodians provide settlement, safekeeping and reporting.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership or investment discretion over all assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Contract and fiduciary status vary.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Edge type: Account records, issuance, redemption and distributions
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Transfer agents operationalise the legal register and shareholder cash flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: Transfer agents record ownership changes and process distributions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Investment management or beneficial ownership of fund assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Omnibus and street-name structures can place detailed records at intermediaries.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Mandatory reporting turns private portfolio operations into supervisory information
relationships.What evidence establishes: Covered funds file Form N-PORT information with the SEC.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Real-time public transparency of every field or absence of reporting lags.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Public availability and confidentiality vary by field and period.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Annual reporting makes fund architecture legible to supervisors
relationships.What evidence establishes: Registered funds file census information on Form N-CEN.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Audit of every operational fact by filing alone.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Filings depend on accurate reporting and definitions.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Disclosure converts delegated stewardship into an auditable dataset
relationships.What evidence establishes: Registered management investment companies disclose proxy-voting records.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Proof that votes caused corporate outcomes or reflect every beneficial owner’s preference.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Lending, abstention and mandate details matter.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Asset-management mandates can convert dispersed ownership into recurring governance interfaces
relationships.What evidence establishes: Advisers may exercise proxy authority under client or fund mandates and must disclose records or policies where required.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership, guaranteed vote control or uniform preferences across clients.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Clients can retain or limit voting authority.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fund-share voting converts beneficial interest into governance selection
relationships.What evidence establishes: Registered funds have boards with shareholder and statutory governance roles.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct control of daily portfolio decisions by each shareholder.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Voting structures and adviser influence vary.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion output: Cash payment funded from liquidity, sales or borrowing
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Open-end structure converts portfolio ownership into a liquidity promise
relationships.What evidence establishes: Open-end mutual funds issue redeemable shares based on NAV.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Underlying-asset liquidity or guaranteed same-day settlement in all circumstances.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fees, gates and settlement terms vary by fund and law.

relationships.Category: Registered funds, delegated management and liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Valuation governance converts illiquid observations into official fund NAVs
relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 2a-5 permits board oversight of a valuation designee under defined conditions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Objective certainty of private-asset values.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Models, inputs and conflicts remain material.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: AP agreements connect underlying assets to primary-market ETF supply
relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 6c-11 ETFs issue creation units to authorised participants for baskets and cash balancing amounts.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Retail investor direct creation right or guaranteed AP activity.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: AP participation is contractual and economic.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Redemption converts fund shares back into underlying portfolio claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: ETFs redeem creation units with authorised participants through baskets or cash.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Retail redemption directly with the ETF.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Custom baskets and foreign settlement can change timing.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Dealer balance sheets convert primary-market arbitrage capacity into secondary-market execution
relationships.What evidence establishes: ETF shares trade on exchanges through market intermediaries.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed two-sided liquidity at all times.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Spreads widen when underlying markets or dealer capacity are stressed.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Central infrastructure reduces bilateral operational complexity
relationships.What evidence establishes: NSCC automates ETF creation and redemption for eligible instruments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Economic guarantee of the ETF or every underlying asset.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligibility and member access remain bounded.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Licensing converts benchmark intellectual property into investable products
relationships.What evidence establishes: Index providers license benchmarks for use in funds and financial products.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Index-provider ownership of fund assets or guarantee of tracking performance.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Active ETFs and self-indexed products differ.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Exchange trading transfers fund-share ownership without necessarily changing fund assets
relationships.What evidence establishes: Retail and institutional investors trade ETF shares in secondary markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct ownership of basket assets or direct fund cash inflow on every trade.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Only creations and redemptions change shares outstanding.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Arbitrage incentives can align ETF price and NAV
relationships.What evidence establishes: The ETF framework relies on creation-redemption and market arbitrage to support price alignment.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Perfect alignment or a legal duty to arbitrage every discrepancy.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Transaction costs and market closures can interrupt the mechanism.

relationships.Category: ETF creation, redemption and market liquidity
relationships.Conversion input: Portfolio holdings, tax lots and liquidity needs
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Controlled basket discretion can manage tax, liquidity and tracking considerations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 6c-11 permits custom baskets under written policies and procedures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unlimited adviser discretion or freedom from conflicts.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Policies, board oversight and documentation are required.

relationships.Category: Retirement claims, fiduciary governance and pension backstops
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Target-date vehicles transmit participant savings into index funds and ETFs
relationships.What evidence establishes: Target-date funds commonly use pooled underlying strategies and rebalancing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Exclusive use of passive funds or identical implementation across providers.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Holdings and glide paths must be verified fund by fund.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The depository model centralises registered title while downstream ledgers record investors
relationships.What evidence establishes: Many DTC-eligible securities are registered in the nominee name Cede & Co.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Cede beneficial ownership of the economic interests.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Direct registration and other structures also exist.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: DTC converts central record ownership into transferable intermediary positions
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC records participant positions and processes book-entry transfers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ultimate beneficial-owner records at DTC.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Participants maintain their own customer records.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Broker and custodian books connect depository positions to end investors
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC participants record investor beneficial interests on their books.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Issuer visibility into every end owner or direct registered status.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Omnibus chains can include several intermediary levels.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Edge type: Exercise of registered-holder rights through intermediaries
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Intermediation converts end-owner rights into instructions executed by the nominee
relationships.What evidence establishes: A beneficial owner may need Cede & Co., through its participant, to assert appraisal or similar rights.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Cede independent economic discretion over customer interests.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Deadlines and documentary chains can create friction.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Custody infrastructure makes delegated portfolios operationally durable
relationships.What evidence establishes: Custody services include settlement, safekeeping and reporting.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Investment ownership or independent authority to change mandates.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Custody and fiduciary roles may be combined or separate.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Transfer agents convert market transfers into recognised issuer records
relationships.What evidence establishes: Transfer agents maintain security-holder records and process ownership changes and distributions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial-owner identification through all street-name layers.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Issuer, depository and intermediary records require reconciliation.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The depository routes corporate actions across the holding chain
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC processes distributions and corporate actions for participants.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Final delivery to every beneficial owner without intermediary action.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Participants must pass information and payments downstream.

relationships.Category: Custody, intermediated ownership and corporate-action chains
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Custody and advisory mandates separate economic exposure from governance execution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Beneficial owners may delegate proxy voting to advisers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Transfer of beneficial ownership or uniform owner preferences.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Mandate terms and securities lending can limit voting availability.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: A specialised governance body converts rules and discretion into benchmark membership
relationships.What evidence establishes: S&P methodologies identify index committees that maintain indices and apply policies.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ownership of index constituents or guaranteed passive flows.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Committee discretion is bounded by methodology and governance.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Benchmark licensing converts classification into commercial product infrastructure
relationships.What evidence establishes: S&P DJI provides benchmarks and methodologies used in investable products.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Management of every licensed product or responsibility for product returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Licence and implementation are distinct.

relationships.What evidence establishes: FTSE Russell publishes governance and methodologies for licensed benchmarks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic control over all licensee trading.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Licensees choose products and replication methods.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Index data becomes a reusable allocation and performance-measurement interface
relationships.What evidence establishes: MSCI indices are licensed and used by institutional products.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ownership of investor assets or guarantee of tracking.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The existing V1 sources should be supplemented with current methodology files.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fund sponsors convert benchmark weights into portfolio construction rules
relationships.What evidence establishes: Index-tracking products use benchmark methodologies and licences.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Exact replication or mechanical trading at one instant.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Sampling, buffers and implementation discretion can reduce immediate flow.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Consultation creates a formal feedback channel between asset owners and benchmark governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: FTSE Russell uses consultations and external committees in index governance.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: User veto or proof that every comment changes a methodology.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Final authority remains within the provider’s governance structure.

relationships.Conversion mechanism: Formal consultation makes benchmark changes contestable and documented
relationships.What evidence establishes: S&P DJI published consultation results and described committee monitoring.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Consensus among respondents or permanent methodology.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Index policy can change after future consultations.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: LP agreements convert long-duration savings into contingent private-market funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private-fund investors purchase interests and commit capital to adviser-managed vehicles.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Immediate full investment, liquidity or management control.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Terms vary widely by partnership agreement.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The partnership structure concentrates operational control in the GP
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private funds are managed by advisers and controlling general partners under fund documents.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unlimited discretion or beneficial ownership of all LP capital.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: LP agreements, law and advisory duties constrain powers.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion output: Ownership, board rights and restructuring authority
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Private funds convert pooled commitments into concentrated company control rights
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private equity funds acquire portfolio-company interests and exercise contractual governance rights.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform control, operating success or criminal motive.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Minority, growth and co-investment structures differ from buyouts.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fund scale becomes revenue before investment gains are realised
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private-fund documents allocate management fees to advisers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Alignment of every fee with investor returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fee bases and offsets vary.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The distribution waterfall converts successful exits into GP compensation
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private-fund economics commonly include performance-linked carried interest.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed carry or equivalence between gross and net returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Hurdles, clawbacks and taxation vary.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Edge type: Form ADV and Form PF reporting
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Regulatory reporting partially illuminates otherwise private capital pools
relationships.What evidence establishes: SEC-registered private-fund advisers file Form ADV and qualifying advisers file Form PF.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete coverage of all private funds or public disclosure of confidential Form PF details.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Thresholds and exemptions create data gaps.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Banks convert future capital calls into present acquisition and expense funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: Fund-level financing against commitments is a recognised private-market practice and bank exposure channel.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Improved underlying performance or absence of leverage risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Facility details are often private and require contract-level evidence.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Investor obligations become collateral supporting fund-level borrowing
relationships.What evidence establishes: Subscription facilities are generally supported by uncalled commitments and call rights.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct borrower status of every LP or lender ownership of LP assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Notice, exclusion and concentration rules vary.

relationships.Category: Private funds, delegated ownership and fund-level leverage
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Fund assets become collateral for borrowing after much capital has been deployed
relationships.What evidence establishes: NAV facilities are used as fund-level liquidity instruments in private markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Objective portfolio value or equal treatment of all stakeholders.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Valuation and structural subordination are central risks.

relationships.Edge type: Strategic partnership for defined-contribution private-market exposure
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Alternative managers seek to convert retirement default flows into private-market capital
relationships.What evidence establishes: Blue Owl and Voya announced a partnership aimed at bringing private-market investments to defined-contribution plans.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Actual plan adoption, performance benefit or final regulatory approval.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commercial announcement and fiduciary selection are separate.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Long-duration commitments support illiquid direct loans
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private credit funds pool investor capital for direct lending.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Immediate deployment or guaranteed yield.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commitment, NAV and cash flow are distinct.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Non-bank funds convert institutional capital into borrower financing
relationships.What evidence establishes: BIS and Federal Reserve sources define private credit as non-bank, often directly negotiated business lending.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Absence of default risk, bank involvement or public-market exposure.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Definitions and deal structures vary.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Conversion output: Loan selection, pricing and workout decisions
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Delegated underwriting concentrates information and control in the manager
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private-fund advisers manage private credit portfolios and report certain information under Form PF or ADV.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership of assets or accurate valuation in every case.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Manager incentives and valuation policies require review.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Operating revenue is converted into contractual fund cash flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private credit loans create borrower payment obligations, often at floating rates.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Capacity to pay through every cycle.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: PIK can defer rather than resolve stress.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Amount / scale: Riskier private-firm debt about 10% of total nonfinancial business debt in May 2026 report
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Official monitoring makes the expanding non-bank credit layer legible
relationships.What evidence establishes: The May 2026 FSR reports continued growth in leveraged loans and private credit and identifies PIK use as a stress signal.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A forecast of imminent crisis or complete measurement of the sector.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Data remain fragmented and valuation is less frequent than public markets.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Amount / scale: Bank commitments to NBFIs reached $2.6 trillion in 2025 Q4; private equity, BDCs and private credit were the largest category
relationships.Conversion output: Assessment of non-bank leverage and spillovers
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Bank balance sheets remain upstream funding nodes for market-based finance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Federal Reserve reports identify rapid bank exposure growth to NBFIs and large commitments to PE, BDCs and private credit.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Full drawdown, loss or direct funding of every underlying loan.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commitments, outstandings and collateral vary.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Amount / scale: $49 billion commitments reported in June 2025 review
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Public retirement savings become non-bank corporate credit
relationships.What evidence establishes: CalPERS reports a dedicated private-debt programme and commitments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed performance or direct CalPERS underwriting of every loan.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: External and internal management must be separated.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Amount / scale: Apollo reported more than $300 billion of 2025 origination activity across its platform
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A large alternative manager channels retirement and institutional capital into private lending
relationships.What evidence establishes: Apollo reports an integrated asset-management and retirement-services platform with large origination activity.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Every origination being private credit or risk-free alignment between Athene and fund investors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Business lines and balance sheets must be separated.

relationships.Category: Private credit and non-bank corporate lending
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A listed closed-end structure links public shareholders to private-company credit
relationships.What evidence establishes: Federal Reserve and SEC materials identify BDCs as important private-credit providers and NBFI exposures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Bank-deposit protection, daily redemption or absence of leverage.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: BDC regulation and individual portfolio quality vary.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Banks convert acquisition or refinancing needs into distributable institutional loans
relationships.What evidence establishes: Leveraged loans are arranged and distributed to institutional investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Bank retention of all credit risk or borrower solvency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Underwriting and distribution exposures vary.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: CLO demand converts securitisation funding into leveraged-loan market capacity
relationships.What evidence establishes: Federal Reserve research identifies CLOs as major buyers of leveraged loans.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: CLO ownership of every leveraged loan or elimination of bank exposure.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Other funds, banks and insurers also hold loans.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Manager expertise and discretion shape the risk behind fixed tranche claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO structures employ managers to select and manage loan collateral subject to documents.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unrestricted trading or identical incentives across tranches.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reinvestment tests and eligibility criteria constrain the manager.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Edge type: Purchase of senior and mezzanine notes
relationships.Conversion output: Priority debt claim on collateral cash flows
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Tranching attracts investors with different risk tolerances
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLOs issue rated debt tranches to institutional investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Government guarantee or zero loss for senior tranches.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Ratings and structural protections are conditional.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Equity capital absorbs early losses in exchange for residual upside
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO equity is subordinate to debt claims and receives residual cash flows.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unlimited control or guaranteed high return.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Cash diversion tests can suspend equity distributions.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Contractual priority converts common collateral into differentiated risk claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO indentures specify payment priority and collateral tests.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of collateral credit risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Defaults and manager actions can erode protection.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The residual tranche receives cash only after senior claims and structural tests
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO equity receives residual cash after fees, debt and tests.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Stable or guaranteed distribution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Overcollateralisation failures can divert cash.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Edge type: Account control, test calculation and waterfall administration
relationships.Conversion mechanism: The trustee operationalises indenture priority and investor protections
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO trustees administer accounts, reporting and payment mechanics under transaction documents.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Independent investment management or guarantee of collateral performance.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Trustee duties are contractual and often ministerial.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Ratings compress complex default and waterfall assumptions into reusable risk categories
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLO debt tranches commonly receive ratings used by institutional investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of repayment or statement about CLO equity.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Ratings are opinions and can change.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Rating methodologies influence eligibility and capital treatment for structured-credit investors
relationships.What evidence establishes: Moody’s is a major structured-credit rating agency.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed performance or single-agency consensus.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Agency methodologies and ratings can diverge.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Conversion mechanism: A third rating framework provides additional classification and market access
relationships.What evidence establishes: Fitch rates structured-credit tranches and publishes methodologies.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of model risk or guaranteed recovery.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Ratings must be mapped to exact transactions.

relationships.Category: CLOs, leveraged loans and structured-credit waterfalls
relationships.Edge type: Monitoring bank credit to CLOs and structured vehicles
relationships.Amount / scale: Bank credit growth was strong for CLO and related vehicle categories in 2025
relationships.Conversion mechanism: Official analysis connects securitisation vehicles back to bank funding and systemic risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: Federal Reserve reports track bank exposure growth to CLOs, ABS and other NBFIs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Imminent failure or identical risk across all vehicles.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commitments, warehouses and final securities holdings must be separated.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Issuers use registration statements and prospectuses to conduct registered offerings.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: SEC approval of investment merit or guaranteed completion of the offering.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Review intensity and form depend on issuer and offering type.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporation Finance administers issuer disclosure and offering rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Certification of business quality, valuation or future returns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: A filing may become effective without every business risk being resolved.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Traditional public offerings commonly use investment banks and underwriting arrangements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent bank ownership or control of the issuer.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Mandates and economics differ across firm-commitment, best-efforts and direct-listing transactions.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Underwriting syndicates distribute securities subject to offering contracts and Regulation M.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unified long-term investment interest or control of investor allocations after settlement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Syndicate roles and stabilization activities must be transaction-specific.

relationships.Conversion output: Order book and proposed pricing range
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bookbuilding gathers investor demand before pricing and allocation.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Binding demand at the indicated quantity or a neutral allocation algorithm.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Order books can include strategic, non-binding or revised indications.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Syndicates sell and allocate public-offering securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal allocation, permanent holdings or absence of stabilization-related constraints.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Allocation policies and customer categories are generally not fully public.

relationships.Conversion output: Issuer capital and investor securities claim
relationships.What evidence establishes: Registered offerings can raise capital from public investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That gross offering size equals net usable proceeds or guarantees productive investment.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Underwriting discounts, expenses and selling-shareholder proceeds must be separated.

relationships.What evidence establishes: NYSE requires an application and continued compliance for listing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Endorsement of the security's investment quality.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Listing and continued-listing standards are distinct.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Nasdaq operates a formal listing-application and qualification process.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of liquidity, valuation or corporate performance.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Different Nasdaq tiers have different quantitative standards.

relationships.What evidence establishes: NYSE grants listing and trading access subject to its rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Exchange ownership of the issuer or immunity from suspension or delisting.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Exchange rules and SEC oversight remain separate authority layers.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Nasdaq lists and trades qualifying issuer securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Nasdaq beneficial ownership of listed companies.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Listing services, trading systems and index businesses must remain distinct.

relationships.What evidence establishes: NYSE assigns DMMs defined responsibilities in listed securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: DMM ownership of the issuer or exclusive control of all trading.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Other exchanges and off-exchange venues also trade the same security.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Retail investors ordinarily submit orders through broker-dealers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct control over venue selection when the order is non-directed.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Directed orders and special routing instructions must be identified separately.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Institutional clients use broker-dealers and execution services to access markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Identical routing, anonymity or execution method across all institutional orders.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Algorithms, ATSs, blocks and direct market access vary.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Brokers route customer orders among exchanges, ATSs and market centers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every order is routed solely by price or solely by payment.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Routing logic may consider execution quality, likelihood, fees, rebates and size.

relationships.Edge type: Pays for or economically rewards order flow
relationships.Conversion input: Execution revenue and customer flow value
relationships.What evidence establishes: Payment for order flow and related inducements are regulated and disclosed arrangements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic best-execution failure or customer harm.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Execution-quality comparison is required before drawing outcome conclusions.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Retail brokers disclose routing venues and material economic arrangements under Rule 606.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A specific current routing share without the current broker report or inferior execution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Named broker-quarter data must be refreshed from the FINRA repository.

relationships.Edge type: Routes customer orders across market centers
relationships.What evidence establishes: Large retail brokers must evaluate and disclose routing practices.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Any fixed current venue share without the current filing.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Affiliates, directed orders and asset classes must be separated.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Broker-dealers are subject to best-execution review and routing disclosure.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed price improvement on every trade.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Execution quality must be evaluated by order type and prevailing market.

relationships.Conversion input: Broker routing data and supervisory procedures
relationships.What evidence establishes: FINRA Rule 5310 and related oversight apply to member firms.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That FINRA chooses each venue for the broker.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: SEC rules and FINRA rules operate as distinct but overlapping layers.

relationships.What evidence establishes: FINRA requires central submission of public Rule 606(a) reports.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete order-level auditability from the public report.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reports are aggregated and exclude some directed or institutional detail.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 605 requires defined execution-quality disclosures and was amended.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A complete welfare measure or identical compliance timing across all entities before August 2026.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: New definitions and reporting fields require implementation checks.

relationships.Actor A: SEC Division of Trading and Markets
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SEC administers federal order-routing and execution-disclosure rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That staff selects individual customer execution venues.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: SRO implementation and firm supervision remain separate.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Margin accounts allow broker credit subject to collateral and firm rights.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unlimited credit or protection from forced liquidation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Regulation T, house margin and security-specific requirements can differ.

relationships.Edge type: Provides assigned liquidity and auction participation
relationships.What evidence establishes: DMMs have defined NYSE obligations and roles.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Exclusive trading rights or riskless execution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Their performance and assigned security panels change over time.

relationships.Edge type: Operates listing, auction and continuous-trading venue
relationships.Amount / scale: Thousands of listed and U.S. securities
relationships.What evidence establishes: NYSE operates a national securities exchange and auction mechanisms.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That NYSE executes all trades in NYSE-listed securities.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Off-exchange and competing-exchange trading remain material.

relationships.Edge type: Registers and governs electronic market makers
relationships.What evidence establishes: Nasdaq operates an electronic market with member liquidity providers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: One market maker controlling the full Nasdaq market.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Specific market-maker obligations depend on Nasdaq rules and registration.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Cboe operates multiple U.S. equities exchanges and related data products.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unified order book or identical rules across every Cboe venue.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Each exchange remains a separate regulated market.

relationships.What evidence establishes: IEX operates an SEC-registered national securities exchange.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Dominance of U.S. equity volume or immunity from routing economics.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Its market design differs from other exchanges and should be mapped directly.

relationships.What evidence establishes: ATSs match securities orders under a broker-dealer and Regulation ATS framework.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Absence of regulation or complete public pre-trade transparency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Venue protocols, conflicts and fair-access obligations differ.

relationships.Edge type: Requires Form ATS-N and supervises Regulation ATS
relationships.What evidence establishes: NMS stock ATSs file public operational disclosures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: SEC endorsement of venue quality or complete disclosure of every algorithm.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Confidential exhibits and later amendments require review.

relationships.Edge type: Publishes ATS and non-ATS volume transparency
relationships.What evidence establishes: FINRA publishes delayed aggregate off-exchange equity volume.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Real-time order-level transparency or beneficial-owner identification.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Publication lags and aggregation rules affect interpretation.

relationships.Amount / scale: Company describes itself as a leading U.S. retail destination
relationships.Conversion input: Retail order flow and firm capital
relationships.What evidence establishes: Citadel Securities provides U.S. retail execution and exchange market making.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Control of all retail orders or the ability to set any security price.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Company claims about rank require independent routing-share verification.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Citadel Securities operates a NYSE DMM business.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ownership or control of assigned issuers.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Assignments and market shares must be dated.

relationships.Edge type: Provides market making and execution services
relationships.What evidence establishes: Virtu reports market-making and execution-services businesses.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every trade is retail internalisation or profitable.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Business segments and asset classes must be separated.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Jane Street describes itself as a global trading and liquidity provider.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Specific current U.S. equity market share without venue or regulatory data.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Private firms disclose less detail than public companies.

relationships.Conversion output: Customer fill, possible price improvement and dealer inventory
relationships.What evidence establishes: Wholesalers may execute retail orders as principal.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed improvement, zero conflict or direct customer selection of the wholesaler.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The retail broker remains responsible for routing and customer relationship.

relationships.Edge type: Approves national-exchange registration and rule filings
relationships.What evidence establishes: 24X received approval and opened as a national securities exchange.

relationships.What evidence establishes: 24X operates defined extended trading sessions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform overnight liquidity or completed 23/5 implementation for all phases.

relationships.Actor A: SIP consolidated quotation and trade feed
relationships.What evidence establishes: Extended-hours exchange operation depends on NMS data-plan and intermarket infrastructure.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That current SIP operating hours already satisfy every proposed overnight phase.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The relevant rule filings and technical readiness must be updated.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Exchanges contribute core market data to NMS plan processors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That SIPs receive every proprietary order-book event.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Exact data content and protected-status rules are defined by NMS plans and Regulation NMS.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.What evidence establishes: FINRA is a central reporting channel for off-exchange equity activity.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Real-time publication of all ATS identities or order-level subscriber data.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Public transparency datasets and SIP reporting are separate outputs.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.What evidence establishes: SIPs disseminate consolidated core market information.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal latency, depth or cost for all users.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Investors often consume the feed through brokers and vendors.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Creates and licenses proprietary market data
relationships.What evidence establishes: Exchanges offer proprietary data and connectivity products.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed trading advantage or absence of substitutes.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Feed content, speed and fees differ by exchange.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Provides venue-specific depth and order events
relationships.What evidence establishes: Institutional users can subscribe to proprietary exchange feeds.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Knowledge of hidden ATS orders, customer identity or guaranteed profits.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Latency and co-location effects need measurement.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SEC approves and oversees national market system plans.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct operation of every processor or determination of each quote.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Plan participants retain governance and operational roles.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Proposes rescission of trade-through and locked/crossed provisions
relationships.What evidence establishes: In June 2026 the SEC proposed amendments affecting Regulation NMS trade-through and locked/crossed rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Final adoption, effective date or the direction of market-quality effects.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Proposal status must remain separate from current law.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Reports customer and proprietary order events
relationships.Conversion input: Order, route, modification and account identifiers
relationships.What evidence establishes: Broker-dealers report defined NMS order events to CAT.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Public release of named customer trading records.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Data scope and exemptions continue to evolve.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Reports exchange order and execution events
relationships.What evidence establishes: SRO participants contribute CAT data under the NMS plan.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That CAT replaces every other exchange audit trail or public market data feed.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The 2026 concept release considers the continuing role of CAT and other audit trails.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.What evidence establishes: CAT is intended to support regulatory tracking and analysis across NMS securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unrestricted access by private actors or automatic enforcement conclusions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access controls, purpose limitations and auditability remain critical.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Conversion output: Accepted, rejected and corrected CAT records
relationships.What evidence establishes: FINRA CAT operates core industry-member reporting functions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: FINRA ownership of customer securities or use of data outside authorised purposes.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: CAT NMS LLC governance and FINRA operational roles should remain distinct.

relationships.Category: Market data, price transparency and surveillance
relationships.Edge type: Orders cost, governance and privacy changes and seeks comment
relationships.Conversion output: Modified plan obligations and concept review
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SEC approved cost reductions, changed PII requirements and opened a broad 2026 CAT review.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Termination of CAT or resolution of all privacy concerns.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Final outcomes of the concept release remain open.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Amount / scale: Virtually all broker-to-broker U.S. equity trades according to DTCC
relationships.What evidence establishes: NSCC clears and nets a very large share of eligible U.S. equity transactions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: NSCC execution of the original trade or elimination of member default risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligibility and exclusions must be mapped by product and transaction.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: NSCC acts as central counterparty and nets eligible transactions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Zero margin, zero liquidity demand or public guarantee of all member losses.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Default resources and loss allocation sit in separate rulebook layers.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: NSCC and DTC operate linked clearing and settlement functions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That the two legal entities are interchangeable or have identical risk roles.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: NSCC is CCP; DTC is central securities depository and settlement system.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC records participant positions and settles securities movements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ultimate beneficial-owner identification or economic ownership by DTC.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Participants maintain downstream customer and custody records.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Appears as registered holder for deposited securities
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cede acts as DTC's nominee record holder for deposited securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ultimate beneficial ownership or unilateral voting control over every deposited share.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Voting and corporate actions flow through participant and beneficial-owner instructions.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Meets margin, clearing and net settlement obligations
relationships.Conversion input: Member capital, collateral and trade obligations
relationships.Conversion output: CCP risk resources and settlement performance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Clearing members are responsible for NSCC obligations under its rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That all customer brokers are direct members or that customer assets fund every obligation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Introducing and clearing brokers must be separated.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Requires T+1 standard settlement for most transactions
relationships.What evidence establishes: The U.S. standard settlement cycle moved to T+1 for most covered transactions on May 28, 2024.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Same-day settlement or elimination of all exceptions and fails.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Firm-commitment offerings and expressly agreed exceptions may have different treatment.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Collects funds or securities for settlement
relationships.What evidence establishes: Broker-dealers coordinate customer settlement under the shortened cycle.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: No prefunding, liquidity or recall risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Cross-border and securities-lending transactions can create timing frictions.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Maintains registered ownership records and corporate actions
relationships.Conversion output: Master securityholder file and processed distributions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Transfer agents maintain issuer securityholder records and process defined actions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial-owner records for all street-name positions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Bank and non-bank transfer agents can have different primary regulators.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.What evidence establishes: Computershare is a major provider of transfer and issuer services.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Service for every listed company or beneficial ownership of client shares.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Exact issuer appointments should be verified from filings and contracts.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Maintains downstream custody and account positions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Participant and intermediary records connect central-depository positions to beneficial investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That DTC itself maintains every ultimate owner record.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Multiple broker, bank and custodian layers may intervene.

relationships.Category: Equity clearing, settlement and registered ownership
relationships.Edge type: Processes dividends, splits, tenders and reorganisations
relationships.Conversion output: Cash, securities or election instruction through custody chain
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate actions are processed through issuer, agent and depository infrastructure.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every beneficial owner receives information simultaneously or makes a direct issuer election.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Voluntary and mandatory actions have different timelines and intermediaries.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.What evidence establishes: Short selling commonly depends on borrowing or a valid locate process.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every short position uses the same lender or violates delivery rules.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Derivatives and bona fide market-making positions require separate analysis.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.Edge type: Transfers securities against collateral and fee
relationships.Conversion output: Temporary possession and borrower's delivery capacity
relationships.What evidence establishes: Securities lending transfers securities under contractual terms against collateral or economics.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent beneficial ownership transfer or unrestricted voting by both parties simultaneously.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Recall, manufactured payments and voting arrangements vary by contract.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.What evidence establishes: Retail margin agreements create broker credit and liquidation rights.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Protection from market loss or guaranteed notice before every liquidation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: House requirements can exceed regulatory minimums.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.Edge type: Uses financing, custody, stock borrow and consolidated services
relationships.What evidence establishes: Prime-brokerage relationships combine financing and operational market access.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: The exact exposure of every named prime broker without filings or regulatory data.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Bank, broker-dealer and client legal entities must be separated.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.Edge type: Applies order marking and locate procedures
relationships.What evidence establishes: Broker-dealers have Regulation SHO-related short-sale compliance obligations.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.Edge type: Closes out defined fails or acquires securities
relationships.Conversion output: Purchased or borrowed securities and resolved fail
relationships.What evidence establishes: Clearing and broker processes address fails under settlement and short-sale rules.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.Edge type: Files Form SHO when thresholds apply

relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Compliance and public dissemination timing must be updated after extensions.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin

relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 10c-1a establishes a reporting architecture through a registered national securities association.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That final FINRA implementation or public data is already operational as of every earlier date.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The extended schedule and FINRA rulemaking must be verified.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SEC extended compliance timing for short-position and securities-lending transparency rules.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Rescission of the rules or permanent absence of reporting.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Further orders or litigation could change the schedule.

relationships.Category: Short selling, securities lending and margin

relationships.Conversion output: Trading volume, price signal and potential covering demand
relationships.What evidence establishes: Short selling can contribute to liquidity and price discovery as well as create risks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every price decline is caused by short sellers or that all short activity is beneficial.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Empirical effects vary by security, constraints and market conditions.

relationships.Category: Proxy voting, beneficial ownership and corporate control
relationships.What evidence establishes: Issuers use transfer agents to maintain registered ownership and process shareholder actions.

relationships.Conversion output: Vote totals and preliminary or final results
relationships.What evidence establishes: Tabulation infrastructure converts instructions into meeting results.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Proxy advisers provide research and voting recommendations to institutional clients.

relationships.Edge type: Approves or rejects proposals and directors

relationships.Conversion output: Claim that market maker can set any stock price at will

relationships.Conversion input: Critical routing, custody and voting infrastructure

relationships.What evidence does not establish: That one proposed design is legally or economically optimal.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Safeguards require testing against cost, resilience, competition and privacy.
