relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions

relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Limits and eligibility conditions apply.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Valid noncompetitive bids are awarded at the auction-determined terms.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury reports direct-bidder allotments as a distinct investor class.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury reports indirect-bidder awards as a separate auction class.

relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The category includes multiple customer types.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.Edge type: Operates direct securities access and records
relationships.What evidence establishes: TreasuryDirect enables eligible investors to buy and hold Treasury securities directly.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Secondary-market liquidity or insurance against market loss.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: TreasuryDirect holdings and broker-held marketable securities use different custody channels.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury formally seeks advice through TBAC and dealer consultations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Delegation of final issuance authority to the committee.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Advice is one input among official forecasts and policy decisions.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: TBAC provides reports, minutes and financing recommendations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic implementation or evidence that members control Treasury.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Treasury may accept, modify or reject advice.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury communicates financing policy and auction schedules through quarterly refunding.

relationships.Category: Sovereign debt issuance and Treasury auctions

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.Edge type: Expected to bid on a pro-rata basis
relationships.What evidence establishes: Primary dealers are expected to bid in all Treasury auctions at reasonably competitive prices.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed award or exclusive auction access.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Other direct and indirect bidders also participate.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Primary dealers are counterparties in Treasury operations conducted by the Desk.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That dealers determine FOMC policy or win every operation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Operations are directed by the FOMC and governed by eligibility and limits.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.Actor B: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
relationships.Edge type: Reports positions, transactions, financing and fails
relationships.What evidence establishes: Primary dealers submit FR 2004 data and aggregate series are published.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Public identification of each dealer's confidential positions or New York Fed audit of all data.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The New York Fed states it expects accuracy but does not audit the reports.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Desk lends Treasury and agency securities from SOMA to primary dealers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent transfer of ownership or rescue from every settlement fail.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Loans are temporary and priced under operation rules.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.Edge type: Quotes, buys and sells Treasury securities
relationships.What evidence establishes: Primary dealers maintain significant market-making and customer-trading roles.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Exclusive control of Treasury trading or uniform liquidity across conditions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Non-primary dealers and electronic platforms also intermediate activity.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.Conversion input: Expected auction supply and hedging demand
relationships.What evidence establishes: Primary dealers participate in the when-issued market around auctions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That when-issued trading fixes the auction result or constitutes collusion.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Order flow and risk management can move prices.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Interdealer markets are a major channel for Treasury price discovery and dealer risk transfer.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete visibility into dealer-to-customer trading or a single universal platform.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Venue-level data remain incomplete in public sources.

relationships.Category: Primary dealers, Treasury intermediation and monetary operations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Electronic platforms support dealer-to-customer fixed-income workflows.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That all Treasury customer trades occur electronically or use one protocol.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Voice, bilateral and portfolio trading remain relevant.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.Conversion output: Operational purchase, sale or reinvestment instructions
relationships.What evidence establishes: The FOMC directs the Desk's SOMA Treasury operations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct control by primary dealers or Treasury over FOMC decisions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Operational details are implemented by the New York Fed.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Desk executes Treasury purchases for SOMA.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That purchases are permanent or tied to one fiscal programme.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Purchases, sales, rollovers and inflation compensation all affect holdings.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: SOMA holdings are allocated among Federal Reserve Banks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Independent portfolio discretion by each Reserve Bank.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The New York Fed executes transactions for the common account.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Desk rolls over maturing SOMA Treasury holdings at auction under policy direction.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Competitive bidding like an ordinary investor or cancellation of Treasury debt.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Rollover mechanics are distinct from secondary-market purchases.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.Conversion output: Reduced bank reserve balances absent offset
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury receipts and debt settlement affect its cash account and system reserves.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A fixed reserve effect without considering Treasury spending and Federal Reserve operations.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Daily net flows determine the realised effect.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.Conversion output: Reserve and deposit creation for recipients
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury outlays move funds from the TGA into the banking system.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every payment creates net wealth or is unconnected to prior taxes and borrowing.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fiscal and monetary balance-sheet effects must be reconciled.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: SOMA securities lending supports smooth Treasury and agency clearing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of all fails or permanent transfer.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Borrowers remain subject to loan terms and return obligations.

relationships.Category: Federal Reserve portfolio and sovereign-debt transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Desk conducts published purchase operations to manage reserves and reinvestments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed monthly pace independent of market conditions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Operation amounts and composition can change.

relationships.Category: Treasury benchmarks, collateral and yield transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: Marketable Treasuries across maturities form core yield references.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A perfectly smooth, static or riskless curve.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Interpolation, liquidity and issue selection matter.

relationships.Category: Treasury benchmarks, collateral and yield transmission
relationships.Edge type: Serves as reference for corporate bond spreads
relationships.Conversion output: Coupon, reoffer yield and borrowing cost
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate bonds are commonly priced relative to benchmark yields and credit spreads.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: One-to-one pass-through or identical benchmark for every issue.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Swap curves and comparable bonds can also be used.

relationships.Category: Treasury benchmarks, collateral and yield transmission
relationships.What evidence establishes: Institutional investors compare bond yields with Treasury benchmarks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That Treasury-relative spread isolates only default risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Liquidity, optionality, tax and technical factors also enter.

relationships.Category: Treasury benchmarks, collateral and yield transmission
relationships.Actor B: Repo, reverse repo and secured wholesale funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury securities are central collateral in repo and official operations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: No haircut, duration risk or settlement dependency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Collateral treatment depends on counterparty, term and facility.

relationships.Category: Treasury benchmarks, collateral and yield transmission
relationships.Conversion input: Expected security value and order flow
relationships.What evidence establishes: When-issued prices and order flow are closely connected to auction dynamics.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Mechanical determination of the stop-out yield or proof of price manipulation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: News and balance-sheet conditions can move both markets.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.Conversion output: Proposed maturity, coupon, structure and execution plan
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate issuers engage investment-bank debt-capital-markets functions to structure offerings.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent bank control of the issuer or guaranteed execution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Mandates and underwriting form vary.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate bond offerings are distributed through underwriters and initial purchasers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform long-term holdings or identical incentives among syndicate members.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Bookrunner, co-manager and dealer roles must be separated.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Underwriters distribute registered corporate bonds to investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal allocation, permanent ownership or absence of stabilisation and hedging.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Allocation data are often not fully public.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.Conversion output: Issuer funding and investor creditor claim
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate bond buyers provide capital in exchange for contractual repayment claims.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Residual equity ownership or voting rights equivalent to stock.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Bondholder rights are defined by the security and indenture.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Corporate bonds create contractual payment obligations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed repayment or protection from issuer default.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Priority, security and guarantees differ by issue.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Rule 144A supports institutional resales to qualified institutional buyers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: SEC registration or unrestricted retail distribution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Other exemptions and Regulation S may operate alongside Rule 144A.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.Conversion output: Issuer funding and restricted security claim
relationships.What evidence establishes: Institutional investors fund exempt corporate debt offerings.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Public registration, retail suitability or absence of resale restrictions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Settlement may occur through initial purchasers and DTC.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Underwriters and DTC participants submit eligibility requests for new debt issues.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Credit approval or investment endorsement by DTC.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Documentation and operational conditions determine eligibility.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC eligibility permits electronic distribution and depository services.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Creditworthiness, profitability or public-registration status.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligible securities can include registered and exempt issues.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bond issues use identifiers to connect issuance and settlement systems.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership or economic-risk classification.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reopenings and multiple tranches require careful identifier mapping.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.Edge type: Places global bond in book-entry system
relationships.What evidence establishes: DTC holds eligible global securities and records participant positions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ultimate beneficial ownership by DTC or Cede.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Downstream intermediaries maintain investor records.

relationships.Category: Corporate bond issuance and institutional distribution
relationships.Edge type: Defines fixed-income index eligibility and weights
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bond indexes shape benchmark-relative allocation and performance measurement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Beneficial ownership or mandatory purchase by all investors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Tracking funds and active mandates respond differently.

relationships.Category: Credit ratings, methodologies and regulatory classification
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SEC's Office of Credit Ratings administers the NRSRO framework.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: SEC authorship or endorsement of individual ratings.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: NRSROs remain private rating organisations.

relationships.Category: Credit ratings, methodologies and regulatory classification
relationships.Edge type: Files Form NRSRO and regulatory disclosures

relationships.What evidence does not establish: Binding legal regulation or enforcement authority over every participant.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Local laws and regulators remain separate.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.What evidence establishes: Market participants can publicly state commitment to the Code.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Proof of complete compliance or legal immunity.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commitment scope and later conduct must be assessed separately.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.Edge type: Publishes spot and forward reference rates
relationships.What evidence establishes: WMR provides widely used FX benchmark rates under published methodology.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: The sole valid market rate or guaranteed execution at the fix.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Benchmark rates and dealer execution outcomes can differ.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.Edge type: Provides transaction and order data for EBS fixes
relationships.What evidence establishes: EBS benchmarks use specified transaction and order data windows.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Representation of all venues or every currency pair.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Venue concentration can affect benchmark representativeness.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.What evidence establishes: Institutional portfolios use fixing orders for valuation and rebalancing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That all fixing-window flows are manipulative or achieve exact benchmark execution.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Concentrated legitimate demand can move prices.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.Edge type: Creates offshore exposure to restricted currencies
relationships.What evidence establishes: NDF markets provide hedging and trading where physical delivery is restricted or impractical.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Removal of capital controls or deliverability of the underlying currency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Onshore and offshore rates can diverge.

relationships.Category: Foreign-exchange market structure and price formation
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cross-currency basis movements reflect global funding demand and intermediation constraints.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A single-cause measure or guaranteed arbitrage opportunity.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Credit, regulation, balance sheet and hedging demand interact.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Host dollar-denominated banking outside the United States
relationships.Amount / scale: $14.3 trillion dollar credit to non-U.S. borrowers at end-2025 across loans and debt securities
relationships.What evidence establishes: Banks outside the United States create and intermediate dollar-denominated credit and deposits.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Federal Reserve reserve balances or uniform U.S. legal protection.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: BIS global-liquidity measures include loans and debt securities, not only deposits.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Supplies dollar deposits, loans and securities funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: Global banks, funds and official institutions supply dollar funding outside the United States.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: One central issuer or a single pool of reusable dollars.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Gross interbank claims can multiply while net positions remain smaller.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Provides dollar loans and securities funding
relationships.Amount / scale: $14.3 trillion dollar credit outside the United States at end-2025
relationships.What evidence establishes: Non-U.S. borrowers obtain substantial dollar credit through banks and global bond markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: All dollar borrowing occurs through U.S.-chartered banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Borrower sectors and instruments differ.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.What evidence establishes: FX swaps are widely used to obtain foreign-currency funding.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unsecured credit or absence of rollover and basis risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The far-leg obligation remains.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Conversion input: Debt or asset cash flows in one currency
relationships.Conversion output: Principal and interest exposure in another currency
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cross-currency swaps transform longer-term funding and cash-flow exposures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Removal of counterparty or collateral risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Documentation and collateral terms influence economics.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.What evidence establishes: The dollar is widely used in global borrowing and finance.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct U.S. government control of each foreign borrowing decision.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Private contracts and market conventions transmit the currency hierarchy.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Conversion input: Dealer funding, hedging and client flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: Basis movements reflect the cost and capacity of currency intermediation.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A pure measure of bank credit risk or policy expectation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Collateral, regulation and demand also matter.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Measures foreign-currency credit outside currency areas
relationships.What evidence establishes: BIS indicators measure dollar, euro and yen credit to borrowers outside the respective currency areas.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete real-time mapping of every offshore deposit chain.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The methodology uses residence and statistical estimates.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Generates demand for official dollar liquidity
relationships.What evidence establishes: Swap lines are designed to address global dollar funding strains that can affect U.S. and foreign markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic access for every offshore bank or borrower.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access flows through selected foreign central banks.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Supplies liquid assets and payment infrastructure
relationships.Conversion input: Central-bank money, sovereign debt and banking networks
relationships.What evidence establishes: Reserve-currency systems provide deep assets and payment infrastructure used by global lenders.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed stable reserve share or equal access for all users.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Institutional quality and network depth can change.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Amount / scale: €4.9 trillion euro credit outside the euro area at end-2025
relationships.What evidence establishes: Euro-denominated credit outside the euro area is a major component of global liquidity.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Replacement of the dollar as universal funding currency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Currency use varies by region and sector.

relationships.Category: Offshore dollar funding and currency hierarchy
relationships.Edge type: Provides yen funding and hedging alternatives
relationships.What evidence establishes: The BIS tracks yen credit outside Japan alongside dollar and euro credit.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform scale, borrower profile or policy transmission across currencies.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Yen usage is smaller and structurally different.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cross-border payments begin with an originator's instruction to a financial institution.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Final settlement or beneficiary credit at the moment of message creation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Funding, screening and intermediary routing remain separate.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: SWIFT carries structured interbank payment messages.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Transfer of money on SWIFT's own balance sheet.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Settlement occurs through correspondent accounts and payment systems.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Beneficiary banks receive structured payment information through SWIFT.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic beneficiary credit regardless of funds, screening or errors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Funds and message may travel through different chains.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Correspondent banks provide payment and account services to respondent banks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ownership of the respondent bank or universal obligation to execute every payment.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access is conditioned by contract, compliance and liquidity.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: A nostro is a bank's account held with another bank, often in foreign currency.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct segregated ownership by the respondent's customers.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The account is an interbank asset-liability relationship.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: The correspondent records the same interbank balance as a vostro liability.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Separate economic funds beyond the corresponding nostro claim.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Nostro and vostro describe perspectives on one relationship.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Edge type: Uses separate customer and funding messages
relationships.Conversion input: Customer instruction and correspondent funding need
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cover payments separate customer information from the interbank funding transfer.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Removal of screening, reconciliation or delay.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Both chains must be linked accurately.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Intermediary banks may transmit the funding leg through correspondent accounts.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Knowledge of every customer relationship or automatic same-day completion.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Cut-offs and screening can delay settlement.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Serial payments move through one or more intermediary banks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A fixed route or absence of fees and delays.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Routing depends on accounts, currency and beneficiary-bank access.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Edge type: Channels dollar payments to direct participants
relationships.What evidence establishes: CHIPS participants provide broad correspondent reach for international dollar payments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct CHIPS access for every respondent bank.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Indirect banks depend on participant relationships.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Amount / scale: More than $2 trillion average daily value reported
relationships.What evidence establishes: CHIPS processes large domestic and international U.S.-dollar payments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Federal Reserve guarantee of each participant or gross prefunding of all payment value.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The system relies on participant funding and loss controls.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Conversion input: Queued payment instructions and participant funding
relationships.What evidence establishes: CHIPS uses a liquidity-saving algorithm and final settlement process.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of participant default or operational risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Liquidity efficiency depends on payment patterns and funding.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Amount / scale: About 95% of payments are a USD leg of transfers beginning or ending abroad according to TCH
relationships.Conversion output: Funds available through beneficiary bank chain
relationships.What evidence establishes: CHIPS is a core infrastructure for cross-border dollar payments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct retail account service or beneficiary identification by CHIPS.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Banks complete downstream account crediting.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.Edge type: Settles dollar funds through central-bank accounts
relationships.What evidence establishes: High-value dollar payments may settle through central-bank account infrastructure.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That SWIFT or CHIPS is used in every case.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fedwire and CHIPS are distinct settlement arrangements.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: ISO 20022 supports structured data across payment initiation, correspondent banking and settlement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed straight-through processing or removal of data-quality problems.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Legacy coexistence and local implementation differ.

relationships.Category: Correspondent banking and cross-border dollar payments
relationships.What evidence establishes: Nostro balances provide liquidity for cross-border payments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic customer credit, absence of intraday overdrafts or zero reconciliation risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Correspondent credit and cut-offs can supplement prefunding.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Conversion input: Risk of paying sold currency without receiving bought currency
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS was created to mitigate principal settlement risk in foreign exchange.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Removal of all market, liquidity, operational or counterparty risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Coverage depends on eligibility, currencies and participation.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: Settlement members submit eligible instructions directly to CLS Bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic settlement of unmatched, ineligible or unfunded trades.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Rules govern matching, rescission and funding.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Settles payment instructions in eligible currencies
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLSSettlement supports 18 actively traded currencies.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Coverage of all national currencies or every FX product.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Currency eligibility requires legal and operational integration.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS calculates member pay-in obligations by currency.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Zero liquidity requirement or guaranteed funding availability.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Members must meet time-critical pay-ins.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: Settlement members fund CLS through relevant currency payment systems.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: One global central-bank account or a single currency funding pool.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Each currency has its own central-bank and payment-system arrangements.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS provides PvP by conditioning settlement of each leg on the other.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Protection from changes in market value before settlement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Liquidity and operational obligations remain.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Accesses CLS through a settlement member
relationships.Amount / scale: Banks, funds, non-bank financials and corporations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Third parties use CLS through direct settlement members.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct membership, independent funding access or no member dependency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The member manages submission and service terms.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Provides settlement service and operational interface
relationships.What evidence establishes: Settlement members extend CLS services to indirect users.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: CLS guarantee of the member's broader service performance.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Commercial terms and credit support are bilateral.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Submits own or authorised official FX instructions
relationships.What evidence establishes: Eligible central banks can become settlement members for defined official transactions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Submission of commercial-bank client trades by a central bank member.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: CLS rules limit the scope of central-bank submissions.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Measures PvP and non-PvP settlement patterns
relationships.What evidence establishes: The BIS 2025 survey measures how FX trades are settled, including PvP coverage.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete transaction-level identification of every CLS trade.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Survey categories include bilateral and other settlement methods.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Routes eligible FX trades to CLS
relationships.What evidence establishes: Dealers use CLS directly or through service relationships for eligible settlement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: CLS coverage of every dealer trade.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Some trades settle bilaterally or through other PvP arrangements.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Amount / scale: More than $8 trillion of payments settled daily reported by CLS
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS materially reduces principal settlement risk for eligible instructions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of the full value and replacement-cost risks of FX trading.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Risk remains for uncovered trades and operational failures.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Compresses gross funding into net pay-ins
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS uses multilateral netting to reduce settlement liquidity needs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: No intraday funding pressure or zero liquidity concentration.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Timing and currency-specific shortages still matter.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.What evidence establishes: CLS settlement depends on linked currency payment systems and legal finality.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: One uniform legal regime across currencies.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Operating hours and finality rules differ.

relationships.Category: CLS payment-versus-payment and FX settlement risk
relationships.Edge type: Reduces principal exposure through member access
relationships.What evidence establishes: Third-party access extends PvP risk reduction beyond direct members.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Protection if the member fails to submit, fund or operate correctly.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Third-party dependence creates additional service-provider risk.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Amount / scale: $13.10 trillion total official FX reserves in 2026Q1
relationships.What evidence establishes: Monetary authorities hold and manage large official foreign-exchange reserve portfolios.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A single global portfolio or uniform investment policy.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: COFER aggregates do not identify every country's allocation.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: Participating economies report reserve composition to the IMF for aggregate publication.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Public country-by-country currency allocations for confidential reporters.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reporting participation and coverage can change.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: The IMF publishes global reserve-currency aggregates.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Identification of individual secret portfolios or causal interpretation of every share change.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Exchange-rate valuation affects reported shares.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: The dollar remained the largest reported reserve currency in 2026Q1.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent dominance, active purchases equal to the share change or U.S. control of reserve managers.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Valuation and reporting effects matter.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: The euro was the second-largest reported reserve currency in 2026Q1.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A unified euro-area fiscal asset or identical reserve use by every country.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reserve instruments include multiple issuers and maturities.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: The renminbi is separately identified in COFER and held as an official reserve currency.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Full capital-account convertibility or replacement of dollar and euro systems.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access, liquidity and policy constraints remain relevant.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: The yen is a separately identified reserve currency in COFER.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform allocation or stable share across time.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Valuation and policy decisions affect holdings.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: Sterling remains a separately identified official reserve currency.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Absence of exchange-rate or sovereign-asset risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reserve use depends on market depth and policy objectives.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Edge type: Holds monetary gold alongside currency reserves
relationships.What evidence establishes: Official reserve portfolios can include monetary gold in addition to foreign exchange.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: COFER currency shares including gold or a transaction whenever gold's valuation rises.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: COFER reports foreign exchange reserves separately from gold.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Edge type: Supplies liquid reserve assets and settlement access
relationships.Conversion input: Sovereign debt, central-bank money and financial markets
relationships.What evidence establishes: Deep markets and payment networks support reserve-currency use.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed reserve demand or permanent geopolitical alignment.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Safety, return, liquidity and policy considerations interact.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Conversion input: Existing reserve positions and exchange-rate moves
relationships.What evidence establishes: Exchange-rate valuation can change measured reserve shares without transactions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every share change is passive or every valuation effect is fully observable.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Asset-price and reporting changes can also matter.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: Central banks can conduct FX intervention through market counterparties.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed exchange-rate target or public disclosure of every operation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Intervention can be announced, secret, coordinated or rules-based.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Conversion input: Domestic liquidity created or withdrawn by intervention
relationships.What evidence establishes: Central banks may sterilise domestic monetary effects of FX intervention.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Perfect or costless neutralisation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Sterilisation instruments and effectiveness vary.

relationships.Category: Reserve currencies, official reserve management and intervention
relationships.Edge type: Taxes, limits or conditions capital flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: Governments can regulate cross-border capital transactions and currency conversion.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete prevention of flows or absence of economic side effects.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Controls can change incentives and create parallel channels.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Maintains reciprocal dollar liquidity swap line
relationships.Conversion input: Reciprocal currency claims and policy agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve maintains a standing dollar swap arrangement with the Bank of Canada.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent drawing, grant funding or Federal Reserve lending directly to that country's commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Drawings occur under announced terms and central-bank decisions.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Maintains reciprocal dollar liquidity swap line
relationships.Conversion input: Reciprocal currency claims and policy agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve maintains a standing dollar swap arrangement with the Bank of England.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent drawing, grant funding or Federal Reserve lending directly to that country's commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Drawings occur under announced terms and central-bank decisions.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Maintains reciprocal dollar liquidity swap line
relationships.Conversion input: Reciprocal currency claims and policy agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve maintains a standing dollar swap arrangement with the Bank of Japan.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent drawing, grant funding or Federal Reserve lending directly to that country's commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Drawings occur under announced terms and central-bank decisions.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Maintains reciprocal dollar liquidity swap line
relationships.Conversion input: Reciprocal currency claims and policy agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve maintains a standing dollar swap arrangement with the European Central Bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent drawing, grant funding or Federal Reserve lending directly to that country's commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Drawings occur under announced terms and central-bank decisions.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Maintains reciprocal dollar liquidity swap line
relationships.Conversion input: Reciprocal currency claims and policy agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve maintains a standing dollar swap arrangement with the Swiss National Bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent drawing, grant funding or Federal Reserve lending directly to that country's commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Drawings occur under announced terms and central-bank decisions.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.What evidence establishes: The standing network includes the Bank of Canada, Bank of England, Bank of Japan, ECB and Swiss National Bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Universal access for all central banks or guaranteed use in every crisis.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Temporary swap lines can also be created separately.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.What evidence establishes: A swap drawing exchanges dollars for the foreign central bank's currency under a repurchase obligation.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unsecured permanent transfer or assumption of local commercial-bank credit risk by the Federal Reserve.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The foreign central bank is the Federal Reserve's counterparty.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Conversion input: Swap-line dollar proceeds and domestic collateral
relationships.What evidence establishes: Foreign central banks distribute swap-line dollars to institutions in their jurisdictions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct Federal Reserve loan to the domestic bank.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Local central banks determine eligible counterparties and collateral.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Pledges local collateral and repays dollars
relationships.Conversion input: Eligible local collateral and repayment promise
relationships.What evidence establishes: The foreign central bank bears direct credit exposure to local recipients under its facility terms.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Federal Reserve review or acceptance of each local bank's collateral.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Local operation designs differ.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Returns dollars and receives its currency
relationships.What evidence establishes: Swap drawings are reversed at maturity with interest under the agreement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A fiscal grant or permanent reserve allocation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The Federal Reserve does not take exchange-rate risk on the foreign-currency leg under the standard structure.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Actor B: Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility
relationships.Conversion input: Treasury securities held in New York Fed custody
relationships.What evidence establishes: Approved foreign official institutions can use FIMA repo against Treasury collateral.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unsecured financing, automatic eligibility or permanent sale of Treasuries.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Terms, limits and operation tenors apply.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Actor A: Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility
relationships.What evidence establishes: The standing facility converts approved official Treasury holdings into temporary dollar funding.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Debt cancellation, currency grant or unconditional access.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The counterparty must repurchase the collateral.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.What evidence establishes: FIMA repo uses Treasury securities held in custody at the New York Fed.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Forced liquidation or loss of beneficial ownership absent default.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligible security and custody requirements apply.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Edge type: Backstops dollar funding through foreign central banks
relationships.What evidence establishes: Swap lines are designed to limit global dollar stress and spillbacks to U.S. markets.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of every offshore dollar liability.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Use depends on central-bank access and local distribution.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Actor A: Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility
relationships.Edge type: Provides alternative to Treasury asset sales
relationships.What evidence establishes: FIMA repo can reduce incentives for disorderly Treasury sales during dollar stress.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Prevention of all reserve sales or support for non-Treasury assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reserve managers choose among multiple liquidity responses.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Amount / scale: $14.3 trillion dollar credit outside the United States at end-2025
relationships.Conversion input: Cross-border loans, securities and FX data
relationships.What evidence establishes: BIS data quantify global dollar credit and FX activity relevant to backstop design.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A complete map of institution-level emergency liquidity exposure.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Aggregate statistics conceal distribution.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Actor A: Foreign commercial banks receiving swap dollars
relationships.Edge type: Maintains dollar credit and payment capacity
relationships.Conversion input: Central-bank-provided dollars and bank balance sheet
relationships.What evidence establishes: Swap-line distribution can support banks serving dollar borrowers and payments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Mandatory pass-through, unchanged lending or protection from borrower losses.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Banks can retain liquidity or tighten credit.

relationships.Category: Central-bank swap lines and official dollar backstops
relationships.Actor B: Foreign commercial banks receiving swap dollars
relationships.Edge type: Does not lend directly through the swap agreement
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Federal Reserve's swap counterparty is the foreign central bank.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A direct Federal Reserve loan or collateral relationship with each foreign commercial bank.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Other Federal Reserve facilities may have different counterparties.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF members provide quota subscriptions that form the institution's primary resources.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal contribution or equal voting power across members.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Quotas broadly reflect relative positions in the world economy.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Quota shares are a central determinant of IMF voting power.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Pure one-country-one-vote governance or automatic Board support.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Basic votes and constituency arrangements also matter.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.Edge type: Appoints governors and exercises reserved powers
relationships.What evidence establishes: Each member appoints a governor to the IMF Board of Governors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal voting weight or direct management of daily operations.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Most powers are delegated to the Executive Board.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.Conversion input: Collective assessment of long-term global reserve need
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Board of Governors retains authority to allocate or cancel SDRs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic annual issuance or ordinary national-currency spending.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: General allocations require broad member support.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.Conversion output: Allocated SDR holdings and matching allocation liability
relationships.What evidence establishes: General SDR allocations are distributed in proportion to quotas.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Need-based distribution or equal per-country allocation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Quota structure shapes the distribution.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: The IMF administers SDR allocations, holdings and transactions through the SDR system.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Commercial-bank deposit taking or retail payment accounts.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: SDR participation is limited to members and prescribed holders.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.Conversion input: Fixed currency amounts and market exchange rates
relationships.What evidence establishes: The SDR value is based on the U.S. dollar, euro, renminbi, yen and pound sterling.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A separate circulating currency or fixed value against one currency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Basket weights fluctuate with exchange rates.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: SDRs are international reserve assets that can supplement official reserves.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: General public currency, commercial-bank deposit or fiscal grant.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Use requires exchange or domestic institutional conversion.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.Edge type: Exchanges SDRs for freely usable currency
relationships.What evidence establishes: Members can voluntarily exchange SDRs for currency through arrangements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed exchange at any time without counterparties or interest effects.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The IMF can designate participants if needed under its Articles.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Part of a member's quota contribution forms a reserve tranche position.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: An IMF loan to the member or an instrument identical to SDR holdings.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The position changes with IMF use of the member's currency.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Quota resources are the primary funding source for GRA lending.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unlimited lending capacity or direct bilateral loans from each member to each borrower.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Resources are pooled through the IMF.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: NAB participants provide supplementary resources when activated.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent activation or direct programme control by individual creditors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Activation requires specified voting support.

relationships.Category: IMF quotas, reserve assets and governance
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bilateral borrowing agreements have served as a third line of IMF resources.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent or currently unchanged capacity beyond agreement terms.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Availability depends on effective agreements and activation conditions.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Members request IMF financing to address actual or prospective balance-of-payments needs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic approval or absence of domestic policy choices.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Programme design is negotiated and Board-approved.

relationships.Conversion input: Country data, financing gap and policy preferences
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF programmes are developed through discussions between staff and national authorities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal bargaining power or unilateral authorship by either side.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Financing urgency and alternatives shape negotiations.

relationships.Edge type: Submits Letter of Intent and programme documents
relationships.What evidence establishes: Programme authorities formally state commitments in programme documents.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every measure originated outside domestic institutions.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Documents often describe nationally adopted plans within an IMF-supported framework.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Staff reports are presented to the Executive Board for discussion and decisions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Final Board approval at staff level or identical views among directors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Board decisions can modify or reject recommendations.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Article IV consultations cover exchange-rate, monetary, fiscal and financial policies.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Binding financing conditionality for countries without programmes.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Advice can influence markets and other institutions without legal compulsion.

relationships.Edge type: Provides policy advice and Board views
relationships.What evidence establishes: The IMF provides surveillance assessments and policy recommendations to members.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct power to enact national laws.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Publication depends on member consent under IMF transparency policy.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Prior actions are measures completed before programme approval or review.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed Board approval or proof of programme success.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The Board retains decision authority.

relationships.Conversion input: Measured fiscal, monetary or reserve outcome
relationships.Conversion output: Pass, waiver request or failed test
relationships.What evidence establishes: Quantitative performance criteria are formal review conditions in many arrangements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Mechanical programme cancellation after every miss.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Waivers and corrective actions may be considered.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Structural benchmarks track reforms important to programme goals.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every benchmark is a formal performance criterion or directly triggers disbursement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Legal status differs across conditionality instruments.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Programme reviews are completed by the Executive Board before later purchases or disbursements.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic release after staff-level agreement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Board waivers and modifications can affect the decision.

relationships.What evidence establishes: The Board can approve Stand-By Arrangements for members with balance-of-payments needs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Unconditional grant or permanent financing.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Repayment, charges and reviews apply.

relationships.Conversion input: Protracted balance-of-payments problem and structural programme
relationships.What evidence establishes: EFF arrangements support members with medium-term structural balance-of-payments problems.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Debt relief or non-repayable financing.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Longer repayment and programme horizons apply.

relationships.Conversion input: Strong policy framework and potential financing need
relationships.What evidence establishes: FCL access is available to qualifying countries with strong policy frameworks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A programme with ex post structural conditionality identical to an SBA.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Qualification is a stringent ex ante assessment.

relationships.What evidence establishes: The RFI provides prompt financing when a full programme may be unnecessary or infeasible.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: No policy assessment or unlimited emergency access.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access is lower and repeated use is constrained.

relationships.What evidence establishes: The ECF provides concessional programme support to eligible low-income countries.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ordinary GRA lending terms or debt cancellation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligibility, reviews and conditions apply.

relationships.What evidence establishes: The RCF provides rapid concessional assistance to eligible low-income members.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Full programme review structure in every case or non-repayable grant.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Access and safeguards remain defined.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Board completion of a review enables scheduled financing access.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic release after numerical compliance or absence of judgement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Waivers, rephasing and financing assurances may matter.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.Conversion input: Debt data, macro assumptions and shock scenarios
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF staff conduct debt sustainability analysis for relevant countries and programmes.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Deterministic forecast or court finding of insolvency.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Judgement and scenario assumptions influence results.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF and World Bank staff jointly apply the LIC debt-sustainability framework.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Identical institutional mandates or automatic agreement on every policy.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The framework supports lending and debt-limit design.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.What evidence establishes: DSAs help determine IMF financing access and programme debt limits.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Legally binding ceiling outside the programme or guaranteed debt outcome.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Framework thresholds and judgement vary by country type.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.Conversion output: Potential financing assurances and coordinated support
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF programmes can catalyse or condition support from other official creditors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed additional financing or formal subordination of every creditor.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Creditors retain their own decision processes.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF decisions can influence private creditor expectations and market access.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guarantee of bond repayment or creditor agreement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Market response may be positive or negative.

relationships.Category: IMF debt sustainability and catalytic effects
relationships.Conversion output: Need for reserves, adjustment or external financing
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF financing is designed around balance-of-payments needs.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every programme country is insolvent or lacks policy alternatives.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Needs can be temporary, precautionary or structural.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: External financing need and sovereign promise
relationships.What evidence establishes: Sovereigns issue bonds under domestic or foreign law to external investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Creditor ownership of the state or guaranteed repayment.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Currency, governing law and payment structure determine risk.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Official bilateral creditors hold external claims on sovereign borrowers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A single uniform contract or creditor bloc.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Paris Club and non-Paris Club claims differ.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion output: Scheduled preferred or senior external claims
relationships.What evidence establishes: Multilateral creditors are major components of many countries' external debt.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Identical legal priority across institutions or routine participation in debt reduction.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Creditor policies and preferred-creditor treatment differ.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: External sovereign bonds create contractual claims held by private investors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ability of bondholders to tax residents or directly administer government.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Enforcement is limited by contract, immunity and available assets.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Measures external debt stocks and flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: IDS provides country-level external debt data for reporting economies.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete beneficial ownership, current market value or every unreported claim.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Coverage depends on debtor reporting and methodology.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: Official bilateral claims and common principles
relationships.What evidence establishes: Paris Club creditor governments coordinate treatments through an informal forum.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Legal personality equivalent to a multilateral bank or automatic authority over non-members.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Treatments require bilateral implementation.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Debtor countries approach the Paris Club for coordinated official treatment.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic eligibility or immediate debt cancellation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: An IMF-supported programme and financing need commonly frame negotiations.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Agreed Minutes set common terms for bilateral implementation.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct amendment of every underlying loan without bilateral agreements.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Each creditor implements the treatment legally.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: Official creditor claims and DSA envelope
relationships.What evidence establishes: Official creditor committees coordinate Paris Club and non-Paris Club creditors in Common Framework cases.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic agreement, equal legal instruments or immediate implementation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Committee formation and memorandum timelines vary.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Common Framework brings Paris Club and other G20 official creditors into case-specific committees.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A supranational bankruptcy court or binding control of private creditors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Implementation depends on creditor and debtor agreements.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: Debt-sustainability analysis and programme financing gap
relationships.What evidence establishes: IMF analysis and financing assurances are central inputs in many official debt treatments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Power to compel every creditor to accept a specified haircut.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Creditors negotiate the legal treatment.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Requires pursuit of comparable treatment from other creditors
relationships.What evidence establishes: Paris Club treatments include a comparability-of-treatment undertaking.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Mechanically identical haircuts across unlike instruments.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Assessment considers economic and legal differences.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Debtors often seek private-creditor treatment after or alongside official restructuring.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A fixed legal formula binding private holders.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Market conditions and bond clauses shape the offer.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Modern sovereign bonds commonly include contractual collective action clauses.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform wording across all issues or guaranteed restructuring success.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Older bonds and jurisdictions may differ.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion output: Amended payment or other reserved terms
relationships.What evidence establishes: CACs allow specified majorities to amend terms binding all holders in a series.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of litigation, holdouts or procedural challenge.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Thresholds and disenfranchisement rules matter.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Enhanced CACs support aggregation across multiple bond series.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A single vote regardless of thresholds or protection for every minority position.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Contract language determines aggregation mechanics.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private creditors often coordinate through committees during restructurings.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Representation of all holders or identical economic interests.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Committee membership and holdings can change.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: Member bond claims and adviser analysis
relationships.What evidence establishes: Creditor committees provide a structured counterparty for debtor engagement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Binding authority over non-members or automatic agreement.
