relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Final treatment requires contractual voting and implementation.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Sovereigns restructure external bonds through exchange offers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Universal participation or identical value across creditor groups.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Terms can change maturity, coupon, principal and security.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Tenders old bonds or votes under CACs
relationships.Conversion output: Accepted new bonds or dissenting position
relationships.What evidence establishes: Bondholders participate through tenders and contractual votes.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal recovery or voluntary consent from every holder.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: CAC activation can bind dissenters after thresholds.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Holdout creditors may seek payment through litigation or asset enforcement.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed recovery or ability to seize sovereign assets generally.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Immunity, governing law and attachable assets constrain remedies.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Can be bound if contractual thresholds are met
relationships.Conversion output: Binding amended terms or retained holdout claim
relationships.What evidence establishes: CACs reduce holdout capacity for covered bonds when thresholds are satisfied.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Elimination of holdouts across non-CAC debt or every legal strategy.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Instrument coverage is decisive.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Conversion input: Debt inventory, reserves and policy objectives
relationships.What evidence establishes: Sovereigns retain advisers to structure and negotiate debt treatments.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Adviser authority to bind the sovereign or creditors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Mandates and conflicts require transaction-level evidence.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: Private creditor committees commonly use shared advisers.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Representation of non-members or absence of conflicts among series.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Adviser fees can be paid by the debtor under engagement arrangements.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.What evidence establishes: DSA results inform official creditor treatment parameters.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A legally binding haircut formula or certainty about future debt paths.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Negotiation and judgement remain.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Provides debt-service relief or financing assurances
relationships.Conversion output: Rescheduled, reduced or deferred debt service
relationships.What evidence establishes: Official creditors can provide treatments that support programme financing.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform debt cancellation or automatic new financing.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Bilateral legal implementation follows.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Changes fiscal, monetary or structural policy
relationships.Conversion input: Debt service, reserve shortage and programme conditions
relationships.What evidence establishes: External financing constraints can materially influence domestic policy choices.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every reform is externally imposed or lacks domestic political support.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Crisis necessity, ideology and domestic institutions also matter.

relationships.Category: Sovereign external debt and creditor coordination
relationships.Edge type: Receives payments or bears restructuring loss
relationships.What evidence establishes: External debt service and restructuring distribute costs between public budgets and creditors.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A simple one-to-one incidence on all residents or universal creditor gains.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Taxes, spending, inflation and recovery allocations determine incidence.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Files cross-border banking and securities reports
relationships.What evidence establishes: U.S. institutions report defined cross-border positions and transactions under TIC.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete ultimate-beneficial-owner identification or global coverage.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Residence and intermediary reporting conventions apply.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Produces official capital-flow and holdings data
relationships.What evidence establishes: Treasury publishes TIC data on cross-border flows and positions.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Perfect real-time balance of payments or nationality-based ownership.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Revisions and custodial bias affect interpretation.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.What evidence establishes: TIC is a principal official source on foreign holdings of U.S. securities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ultimate ownership when securities are held through third-country custodians.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Residence-based reporting can differ from nationality.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Publishes international banking and global-liquidity measures
relationships.Conversion input: Bank claims and international debt securities
relationships.What evidence establishes: BIS data reveal cross-border and foreign-currency credit structures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Every bilateral exposure or all non-bank private claims.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Consolidated and locational statistics answer different questions.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Reports creditor-category debt stocks and flows
relationships.What evidence establishes: IDS reports official, multilateral and private external-debt categories.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete contractual terms or real-time creditor identity.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Coverage and classification depend on reporting.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.What evidence establishes: COFER combines confidential reports into global aggregates.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Public disclosure of each reporting economy's portfolio.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: The IMF protects reporter confidentiality.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Observes messages carried on its network
relationships.What evidence establishes: SWIFT can analyse message traffic across its own network.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Complete global payment settlement value or ownership of funds.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Off-network and domestic systems are outside the message dataset.

relationships.Category: Cross-border financial statistics and ownership legibility
relationships.Edge type: Informs surveillance, reserve and stability analysis
relationships.Conversion input: TIC, BIS, COFER, IDS and payment data
relationships.What evidence establishes: Official datasets make parts of the international monetary system measurable.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A complete unified real-time graph or proof of causality from one dataset.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Different residence, currency and sector definitions must be reconciled.

relationships.Edge type: Claim that SWIFT directly stores and settles all global money
relationships.What evidence establishes: SWIFT is a major secure financial-messaging network.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Ownership of all funds or direct final settlement of every message.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Correspondent accounts and payment systems perform settlement.

relationships.Edge type: Claim that SDR is already a circulating world currency
relationships.What evidence establishes: SDRs are IMF reserve assets and a unit of account.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: General legal tender, retail circulation or direct public bank deposits.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Members must exchange or domestically convert them for spending.

relationships.Actor B: Foreign commercial banks receiving swap dollars
relationships.Edge type: Claim that swap lines are permanent free money paid directly to foreign banks
relationships.What evidence establishes: Swap lines provide temporary dollars to foreign central banks with repayment and interest.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct permanent grants to commercial banks.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Local central banks intermediate domestic lending and collateral.

relationships.Edge type: Claim of permanent irreversible dollar dominance
relationships.What evidence establishes: The dollar is currently dominant across FX, reserves and international finance.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Permanent monopoly or inability of alternatives to gain share.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Network structures can change gradually or under crisis.

relationships.Edge type: Auditable cross-border monetary access and appeal framework
relationships.Conversion input: Currency, messaging, settlement, reserve and programme gates
relationships.Conversion output: Transparent authority, data minimisation and review rights
relationships.What evidence establishes: Cross-border finance contains concentrated access, information and conditionality interfaces.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That one proposed governance design is optimal or costless.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reforms must balance stability, sovereignty, privacy, liquidity and moral hazard.

relationships.Actor B: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
relationships.Edge type: Subscribe capital and exercise governance rights
relationships.What evidence establishes: IBRD is governed and capitalised by member countries and finances development operations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Equal voting power or direct member control of individual projects.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Governance and project approval are institutionally separated.

relationships.What evidence establishes: IDA provides concessional financing to eligible countries from replenished resources.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: A commercial bank deposit or equal contribution by all members.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Terms depend on eligibility and policy.

relationships.Actor A: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
relationships.Conversion input: Sovereign borrowing capacity and project design
relationships.What evidence establishes: IBRD uses IPF to finance defined projects, goods, works, services and institutional activities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: General budget support or proof of completed outputs at approval.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Disbursement and implementation depend on project documents.

relationships.Edge type: Provides concessional IPF credit or grant
relationships.What evidence establishes: IDA can provide credits or grants for investment projects.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Uniform grant treatment or absence of repayment obligations.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Terms vary by country eligibility and operation.

relationships.Conversion input: Legal financing agreement and public administration
relationships.What evidence establishes: Borrowers implement projects through designated public entities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: World Bank direct operation of the project or ownership of procured assets.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Implementation responsibility remains with the borrower.

relationships.Conversion input: Approved procurement plan and project requirements
relationships.What evidence establishes: World Bank-financed projects use borrower procurement under the applicable framework.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic selection of the lowest nominal bid or World Bank beneficial ownership of contractors.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Methods and review thresholds vary.

relationships.What evidence establishes: Procurement documents define eligibility, evaluation and award procedures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Absence of discretion, influence or later contract modification.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Complaint and review mechanisms can apply.

relationships.Actor A: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
relationships.Conversion input: Programme of policy and institutional actions
relationships.What evidence establishes: DPF supports policy and institutional actions through rapidly disbursing finance.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Funding tied to one physical project or proof that prior actions caused all outcomes.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Funds are generally non-earmarked after agreed conditions.

relationships.Edge type: Implements prior policy and institutional actions
relationships.Conversion input: National reform programme and financing need
relationships.What evidence establishes: Borrowers undertake policy and institutional actions supporting DPF objectives.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every action originated externally or lacks domestic political ownership.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Reforms can reflect domestic priorities and financing incentives.

relationships.Actor A: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
relationships.What evidence establishes: World Bank guarantees can support commercial financing under defined project or policy structures.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Cash grant equal to the guarantee face amount or coverage of every project risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Coverage and counter-guarantee terms are transaction-specific.

relationships.Actor B: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
relationships.What evidence establishes: World Bank guarantee structures can create sovereign reimbursement obligations.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Immediate funded public expenditure before a guarantee claim.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Fiscal exposure depends on covered events and claim occurrence.

relationships.What evidence establishes: PforR links disbursement to defined and verified programme results.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Project-expenditure reimbursement or automatic proof of long-run impact.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Disbursement-linked indicators are specific to each operation.

relationships.What evidence establishes: PforR disbursements are linked to verified results.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That the indicator captures all programme quality or causally measures welfare.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Verification method and scalability matter.

relationships.Edge type: Commits to environmental and social actions
relationships.What evidence establishes: World Bank borrowers prepare environmental and social commitments under applicable projects.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Absence of harm or guaranteed full implementation.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Monitoring and remedy remain necessary.

relationships.Conversion input: Alleged harm from IBRD or IDA project
relationships.What evidence establishes: The Inspection Panel provides an independent complaint route for eligible IBRD and IDA project concerns.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Automatic compensation or binding court judgement.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Eligibility and Board processes govern outcomes.

relationships.Conversion output: Bankable project documents and market engagement
relationships.What evidence establishes: Multilateral preparation platforms support governments in structuring infrastructure projects.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Guaranteed private finance or project approval.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Preparation support is distinct from financing commitment.

relationships.Edge type: Supports PPP policy and institutional capacity
relationships.Conversion output: PPP frameworks and project preparation capacity
relationships.What evidence establishes: PPIAF-type support helps governments improve infrastructure and PPP frameworks.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Award of a project or endorsement of a specific private sponsor.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Technical assistance and transaction finance are separate.

relationships.Edge type: Monitors project guarantees and long-term obligations
relationships.What evidence establishes: Governments need systems to track guarantees, availability payments and termination liabilities.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: That every country records or provisions all exposures accurately.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Off-budget and subnational obligations can remain hidden.

relationships.What evidence establishes: IFC is a multilateral institution owned by member countries and finances private-sector development.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Direct government management of individual investee companies.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Board and management processes govern transactions.

relationships.What evidence establishes: IFC lends directly to eligible private companies and projects.
relationships.What evidence does not establish: Sovereign guarantee, project success or absence of commercial risk.
relationships.Competing explanation / caveat: Loan terms and security are transaction-specific.

mechanisms.Input: Domestic currency issuance and central-bank network
mechanisms.Statement: Issuer plus selected swap partners can stabilise funding markets and reinforce currency centrality.
mechanisms.Limitation: Selective access and collateral; not a universal guarantee.

mechanisms.Output: Claims on future taxes, exports and policy room
mechanisms.Statement: Currency, maturity and refinancing conditions transmit financial claims into future national surplus.
mechanisms.Limitation: Productive use and domestic choices can alter outcomes.

mechanisms.Statement: Past ownership becomes present financing advantage and future ownership concentration.
mechanisms.Limitation: Collateral also genuinely reduces lender risk.

mechanisms.Statement: Pooled funds separate beneficial ownership from practical voting authority.
mechanisms.Limitation: Fiduciary law and voting choice constrain managers.

mechanisms.Statement: A platform can shape institutional cognition by defining objects, scenarios and workflows.
mechanisms.Limitation: Users remain responsible and can supplement models.

mechanisms.Statement: Sovereign funds convert resource rents into diversified productive capacity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Financial return and diversification explain many investments.

mechanisms.Input: Control of scarce route or processing step
mechanisms.Output: Higher exit cost and bargaining leverage
mechanisms.Statement: A scarce conversion step can matter more than abundant upstream ownership.
mechanisms.Limitation: Substitution and new investment can erode leverage.

mechanisms.Statement: Data-integration platforms create decision-ready representations.
mechanisms.Limitation: Representations can be wrong; authority remains distributed.

mechanisms.Statement: Brokers gain power by connecting institutions that cannot easily verify one another.
mechanisms.Limitation: Contact does not imply coordination, motive or crime.

mechanisms.Statement: Complementary assets create reinforcing contracts and institutions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Mutual dependence is not total corporate or state control.

mechanisms.Statement: Subjects become machine-readable faster than governing networks become transparent.
mechanisms.Limitation: Courts, audits and journalism provide partial counter-legibility.

mechanisms.Statement: Institutions measure response and retain interventions that better achieve objectives.
mechanisms.Limitation: Gaming, errors and goal conflict create brittleness.

mechanisms.Statement: The power to choose what AI-enabled institutions optimise is a core form of sovereignty.
mechanisms.Limitation: Institutions pursue multiple conflicting objectives.

mechanisms.Statement: Cybernetic systems may prevent dispersed pressure becoming coordinated force.
mechanisms.Limitation: Prediction is imperfect and organisation can migrate offline.

mechanisms.Statement: Separation, purpose limits, appeal, expiry and exit preserve capacity while limiting domination.
mechanisms.Limitation: Safeguards require independent enforcement.

mechanisms.Input: Dependence, conversion control, information, brokerage, enforcement and feedback
mechanisms.Statement: Power lies in controlling enough interfaces to observe, intervene and learn without owning every asset.
mechanisms.Limitation: No actor controls all terms; coalitions fragment and fail.

mechanisms.Output: Private asset value, fundraising and market demand
mechanisms.Statement: A public officeholder's brand and regulatory authority can raise the value and network reach of family-linked financial instruments without a formally proven quid pro quo.
mechanisms.Limitation: Market demand may reflect ideology, speculation or genuine product utility; transaction-specific proof is required for corruption claims.

mechanisms.Output: Ownership or large transactions with politically connected private firms
mechanisms.Statement: Capital can purchase economic rights and durable access near public authority even where no explicit policy bargain is documented.
mechanisms.Limitation: Investment is not proof of influence purchase; governance rights, timing and communications matter.

mechanisms.Statement: Donations and proposed donor networks can rehabilitate or amplify an elite broker by embedding them in respected institutions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Recipients may seek legitimate funding and may lack knowledge of concealed wrongdoing.

mechanisms.Output: Continued access to banking, philanthropy or academia
mechanisms.Statement: Organisations can preserve a risky relationship when incentives and information are distributed across departments.
mechanisms.Limitation: Failure does not require a central conspiracy and responsibility differs across employees.

mechanisms.Input: A name, photo, email, calendar entry or guest list
mechanisms.Statement: Weak documentary adjacency is often inflated into motive, knowledge or criminal participation.
mechanisms.Limitation: Some appearances do lead to stronger evidence, but only through independent corroboration.

mechanisms.Statement: Analysts create false coordination by placing historical and current edges on one undated graph.
mechanisms.Limitation: Temporal graphs and start/end dates reduce but do not eliminate ambiguity.

mechanisms.Input: Model-lab demand, chip/cloud supply and strategic investment
mechanisms.Output: Mutual financing, purchase commitments and infrastructure lock-in
mechanisms.Statement: Suppliers invest in model labs that commit to buying their chips or cloud, converting anticipated demand into financeable infrastructure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Such arrangements may accelerate useful investment but can create concentration, valuation reflexivity and counterparty risk.

mechanisms.Output: Privileged access to public policy formation
mechanisms.Statement: Presidential councils convert elite technical reputation into formal advisory proximity to executive power.
mechanisms.Limitation: Advisory access is not legal command and members may disagree.

mechanisms.Input: Nonprofit foundation or purpose trust plus private capital
mechanisms.Output: Plural control over a frontier AI company
mechanisms.Statement: OpenAI and Anthropic use legal structures intended to preserve mission authority while raising enormous private capital.
mechanisms.Limitation: Formal rights may not predict practical power under financing, talent and compute constraints.

mechanisms.Output: Leverage over politically active technology executives
mechanisms.Statement: The state can pressure private infrastructure providers through contracts even when those firms have major political influence.
mechanisms.Limitation: Procurement law, courts and operational dependence constrain arbitrary action.

mechanisms.Output: Legally final central-bank or private-system settlement
mechanisms.Statement: Fedwire, CHIPS and CLS turn messages and liquidity into final obligations, making payment infrastructure a constitutional layer of markets.
mechanisms.Limitation: Finality of the payment leg does not validate the underlying commercial or political transaction.

mechanisms.Statement: Netting algorithms allow a small amount of liquidity to support a much larger volume of settled claims, concentrating operational importance in the clearing system.
mechanisms.Limitation: Efficiency creates dependence and systemic concentration; failures or exclusions can propagate widely.

mechanisms.Input: Legal ownership plus assets held through a foreign custodian
mechanisms.Output: Practical access, immobilisation or redirected income
mechanisms.Statement: The jurisdiction and intermediary holding an asset can matter more in crisis than the nominal owner legal title.
mechanisms.Limitation: Freeze, income use and confiscation of principal remain legally distinct.

mechanisms.Statement: Stablecoin issuers extend dollar use beyond banking hours and borders while retaining reserve, redemption and administrative-control chokepoints.
mechanisms.Limitation: Private tokens lack central-bank finality and may carry issuer, bank, market and software risk.

mechanisms.Statement: Sanctions authority reaches public blockchains when a centralised issuer can administratively immobilise tokens.
mechanisms.Limitation: Timing, chain ordering and non-custodial assets can limit enforcement.

mechanisms.Output: Present acquisition of GPUs and data-centre assets
mechanisms.Statement: Special-purpose vehicles and private credit move compute assets off model-lab balance sheets and make future demand financeable.
mechanisms.Limitation: Credit wrapping transfers risk; it does not remove obsolescence, tenant or power risk.

mechanisms.Statement: Infrastructure investors increasingly combine compute ownership with generation to bypass congested public-grid queues.
mechanisms.Limitation: Dedicated power can create emissions, fuel and local-resource externalities.

mechanisms.Statement: AI compute depends on memory supply, packaging and networking as well as GPU design, distributing chokepoint power across suppliers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Technology cycles and capacity investment can change the bottleneck.

mechanisms.Input: Commercial AI software plus incumbent military systems
mechanisms.Statement: Startups increasingly partner with or become enterprise suppliers alongside traditional defence primes rather than simply displacing them.
mechanisms.Limitation: Government command, doctrine and procurement law remain separate from supplier influence.

mechanisms.Input: Trading balance sheet, storage, shipping and information
mechanisms.Output: Ability to reroute physical supply across buyers and sanctions regimes
mechanisms.Statement: Commodity traders gain power from optionality across geography, time, quality, finance and logistics rather than from owning all production.
mechanisms.Limitation: Producer states, refiners and regulators can reduce trader rents through direct contracts.

mechanisms.Output: Practical ability and price to move through a dangerous corridor
mechanisms.Statement: Marine insurance converts geopolitical risk into a tradable premium and can determine whether commerce remains financeable.
mechanisms.Limitation: Self-insurance, public backstops and uninsured shipping can bypass some constraints.

mechanisms.Output: Portable score used in mandates, collateral and pricing
mechanisms.Statement: Ratings coordinate dispersed investors and can become a gateway to market access without legally commanding them.
mechanisms.Limitation: Ratings are opinions, can lag markets and do not mechanically determine borrowing costs.

mechanisms.Statement: Audit networks create a credibility layer that allows distant investors and regulators to rely on company accounts.
mechanisms.Limitation: Audit is not a guarantee and concentrated markets create independence and capacity risks.

mechanisms.Statement: Private data intermediaries make people and organisations legible across institutional boundaries.
mechanisms.Limitation: False matches, stale data and weak appeal rights can convert error into exclusion.

mechanisms.Statement: Platforms govern both the political information environment and the evidence available to outsiders studying it.
mechanisms.Limitation: Control of access is not proof of manipulation; independent measurement is still required.

mechanisms.Input: Legal jurisdiction over a strategic supplier or route
mechanisms.Output: Permission, denial or conditions on a transaction
mechanisms.Statement: States can exercise control without ownership by licensing exports, cable landings, spectrum, grid access or platform conduct.
mechanisms.Limitation: Licences can be evaded, challenged, reversed or offset through alternative suppliers and jurisdictions.

mechanisms.Input: EDA software, IP libraries and simulation workflows
mechanisms.Statement: Control of design software can constrain semiconductor capability upstream of fabrication.
mechanisms.Limitation: Open-source and domestic alternatives exist but advanced workflow substitution can be costly and slow.

mechanisms.Input: Foreign foundry using controlled technology and serving global customers
mechanisms.Output: Compliance with another state's end-use and customer rules
mechanisms.Statement: Export controls can extend extraterritorially through technology origin, equipment dependencies and market access.
mechanisms.Limitation: Overreach can accelerate substitution and create allied-policy conflict.

mechanisms.Output: Owned or prioritised international fibre capacity
mechanisms.Statement: Hyperscalers increasingly own the cables carrying their traffic, reducing dependence on telecom intermediaries while increasing infrastructure concentration.
mechanisms.Limitation: Landing licences, repair fleets, shared fibres and terrestrial networks prevent complete unilateral control.

mechanisms.Input: Commercial hyperscale platform plus security accreditation
mechanisms.Statement: Governments gain rapid scalable computing but can become dependent on proprietary APIs, personnel and release cycles.
mechanisms.Limitation: Multi-cloud procurement and air-gapped deployment can reduce but not eliminate lock-in.

mechanisms.Output: Approval, ranking, billing and removal of third-party software
mechanisms.Statement: App stores convert control of device ecosystems into quasi-regulatory authority over developers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Security review has legitimate benefits and alternative channels vary by jurisdiction.

mechanisms.Statement: Index providers do not manage most linked assets, but their constituent and classification decisions coordinate portfolios at scale.
mechanisms.Limitation: Price effects differ by liquidity, anticipation and active-manager response.

mechanisms.Output: Contract settlement, valuation and risk transfer
mechanisms.Statement: A benchmark's power comes from reuse across many contracts rather than ownership of the underlying commodity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Methodology, liquidity and manipulation risk require governance and surveillance.

mechanisms.Output: Separation of title, control, benefit and public visibility
mechanisms.Statement: Corporate and trust law can make practical control harder to observe than registered legal ownership.
mechanisms.Limitation: Layering is not inherently illicit and financial institutions may possess non-public information.

mechanisms.Output: Different disclosure duties for economically similar entities
mechanisms.Statement: Legal definitions can create unequal visibility between domestic and foreign companies.
mechanisms.Limitation: Other tax, banking and law-enforcement tools partly offset registry gaps.

mechanisms.Output: Additional local insurance underwriting and catastrophe capacity
mechanisms.Statement: Reinsurers convert geographically diversified capital into claims-paying capacity for primary insurers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Exclusions, repricing and correlated catastrophes can reduce availability when most needed.

mechanisms.Output: Timing and cost of electricity access
mechanisms.Statement: For AI infrastructure, a grid connection can be as decisive as chips or capital.
mechanisms.Limitation: Self-generation, storage and alternative sites can reduce dependence but create new externalities.

mechanisms.Statement: Internet naming requires a trusted coordination layer even though content and routing remain decentralised.
mechanisms.Limitation: Root governance cannot ordinarily control individual pages and is constrained by distributed technical actors.

mechanisms.Output: Broad access disruption from configuration error or policy action
mechanisms.Statement: A widely used resolver can become an invisible dependency despite users retaining theoretical alternatives.
mechanisms.Limitation: Resolver competition and local caching limit total control.

mechanisms.Input: Privately owned satellite and launch stack
mechanisms.Statement: States increasingly rent strategic space infrastructure from vertically integrated private suppliers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Contractual dependence does not transfer sovereign command, and alternative constellations may emerge.

mechanisms.Statement: Patent systems exchange public disclosure for time-limited legal rights, turning knowledge into an enforceable asset.
mechanisms.Limitation: Patent quality, claim breadth, litigation capacity and jurisdiction determine practical power.

mechanisms.Statement: Firms can preserve advantages through secrecy, access controls and employment agreements rather than patents.
mechanisms.Limitation: Independent discovery and lawful reverse engineering can limit protection.

mechanisms.Input: Widely adopted instruction-set and software ecosystem
mechanisms.Output: Recurring licence and per-unit royalty income
mechanisms.Statement: Processor-IP firms can capture value from global hardware production without owning fabs or end products.
mechanisms.Limitation: Open standards, alternative architectures and customer bargaining constrain rents.

mechanisms.Output: Multiple implementers and lower architecture exit cost
mechanisms.Statement: Open standards reduce dependence on a single licensor while leaving implementation, verification and software bottlenecks intact.
mechanisms.Limitation: Openness at one layer does not make the full stack open or inexpensive.

mechanisms.Statement: A voluntary standard becomes coercive in practice when buyers, insurers or regulators require conformity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Adoption can improve safety but may entrench incumbents able to afford compliance.

mechanisms.Statement: Certification converts complex technical and governance claims into a simplified signal used by purchasers and regulators.
mechanisms.Limitation: Scope, assessor incentives and renewal determine reliability.

mechanisms.Output: Compatible technology investment before products exist
mechanisms.Statement: Standards bodies coordinate suppliers and operators around shared interfaces, reducing uncertainty while allocating agenda power.
mechanisms.Limitation: Consensus can be slow and dominant firms may contribute more resources.

mechanisms.Output: Research access to scarce models, data and compute
mechanisms.Statement: Public allocation institutions can broaden who crosses the frontier-compute barrier.
mechanisms.Limitation: Scarcity, selection criteria and dependence on donated resources remain.

mechanisms.Statement: Government agencies translate national-security objectives into scientific funding priorities and evaluation criteria.
mechanisms.Limitation: Research outcomes remain uncertain and academic autonomy can be strained.

mechanisms.Statement: Immigration pathways convert organisational sponsorship into partial control over worker mobility and bargaining power.
mechanisms.Limitation: Transfer, self-petition and alternative statuses can reduce but not eliminate dependence.

mechanisms.Input: Publications, awards, investment and professional recognition
mechanisms.Statement: Immigration systems turn professional reputation and capital signals into legal access to national innovation systems.
mechanisms.Limitation: Adjudication is discretionary and can reproduce unequal access to recognised credentials.

mechanisms.Output: Professional access, messaging and legislative advocacy
mechanisms.Statement: Lobbying firms convert money and specialised relationships into repeated access to public decision processes.
mechanisms.Limitation: A disclosed lobbying relationship does not establish corruption or policy causation.

mechanisms.Statement: Former officials can monetise knowledge of procedures, relationships and institutional language after leaving office.
mechanisms.Limitation: Prior service does not imply continuing authority or improper conduct.

mechanisms.Statement: Disclosure systems reveal formal advocacy channels but do not measure informal influence or causal impact.
mechanisms.Limitation: Amounts are estimates and reporting definitions exclude some activities.

mechanisms.Output: State-recognised entity governed by selected law
mechanisms.Statement: Businesses can choose a legal home whose statutes, courts and filing systems shape governance and dispute resolution.
mechanisms.Limitation: Choice of incorporation does not eliminate federal law, operational jurisdictions or contractual variation.

mechanisms.Output: Concentrated managerial authority in an elected board
mechanisms.Statement: Corporate law separates economic ownership from day-to-day control to reduce collective-action costs.
mechanisms.Limitation: Delegation creates agency risk and may be altered by dual-class structures or controlling shareholders.

mechanisms.Output: Standardised recommendation and operational vote workflow
mechanisms.Statement: Proxy advisers lower research costs for institutional investors while becoming influential informational intermediaries.
mechanisms.Limitation: Clients retain legal responsibility and may use custom policies or independent analysis.

mechanisms.Statement: Book-entry settlement scales markets by separating registered ownership from beneficial ownership.
mechanisms.Limitation: Layering complicates voting, reconciliation and ultimate-owner transparency.

mechanisms.Input: Private security agreement plus public perfection
mechanisms.Statement: Secured-transactions law converts credit into a property-like interest enforceable against competing claimants.
mechanisms.Limitation: Priority does not guarantee full recovery and can be avoided or subordinated in defined circumstances.

mechanisms.Output: Court-supervised estate governance focused on creditors and reorganisation
mechanisms.Statement: Financial distress changes the relevant control coalition from shareholders and boards toward courts, lenders and creditor committees.
mechanisms.Limitation: Existing management may remain in possession and shareholders may retain value in some cases.

mechanisms.Output: Priority liens, budgets and restructuring deadlines
mechanisms.Statement: Rescue lenders can shape the timing and feasible outcomes of reorganisation through financing conditions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Court approval and creditor objections constrain lender terms.

mechanisms.Statement: Netting reduces counterparty exposure and liquidity shock by replacing many obligations with one claim.
mechanisms.Limitation: It can also move derivatives outside ordinary collective insolvency processes.

mechanisms.Statement: Parties and states pre-select adjudicative forums whose authority activates when a dispute arises.
mechanisms.Limitation: National courts remain essential for enforcement, annulment and public-law limits.

mechanisms.Output: Constituted tribunal, procedure and scrutinised award
mechanisms.Statement: Arbitral institutions provide procedural infrastructure without necessarily deciding the merits.
mechanisms.Limitation: Institutional quality does not guarantee correct or consistent awards.

mechanisms.Statement: CACs lower the unanimity barrier that otherwise gives small creditors blocking power.
mechanisms.Limitation: Different series, thresholds and non-bonded debt remain coordination problems.

mechanisms.Output: Pressure for private and other creditor burden-sharing
mechanisms.Statement: Comparability principles seek to stop one creditor class from free-riding on another's relief.
mechanisms.Limitation: Measurement is contested and not equivalent to a global bankruptcy priority rule.

mechanisms.Output: Present non-recourse capital and contingent ownership-like return
mechanisms.Statement: Litigation finance converts legal claims into investable cash-flow exposures.
mechanisms.Limitation: Funding may improve access while introducing conflicts, selection effects and opacity.

mechanisms.Input: Choice of incorporation, bankruptcy venue, arbitration seat or governing law
mechanisms.Output: Different procedural rights and expected outcomes
mechanisms.Statement: Sophisticated actors structure transactions around jurisdictions and forums with preferred rules and expertise.
mechanisms.Limitation: Courts can challenge abusive venue or contractual choices, and outcomes remain uncertain.

mechanisms.Output: Creditor and court influence after default
mechanisms.Statement: Control follows the scarce resource needed to preserve value: votes in solvency, liquidity and priority in distress.
mechanisms.Limitation: The transition is gradual and varies with capital structure and enterprise value.

mechanisms.Input: Low effective tax rate in one jurisdiction
mechanisms.Output: Additional tax under domestic implementing rules
mechanisms.Statement: Pillar Two reduces the value of booking in-scope income below a coordinated minimum rate.
mechanisms.Limitation: Implementation, safe harbours and credits vary and may create new planning margins.

mechanisms.Statement: CbC reporting makes profit, tax and substance patterns visible to multiple tax administrations.
mechanisms.Limitation: Aggregated data does not prove mispricing and is generally not public at company level.

mechanisms.Limitation: Margin calls can amplify stress and fire sales.

mechanisms.Statement: Variation margin prevents current exposure accumulation by transferring cash quickly.
mechanisms.Limitation: It can create acute liquidity shocks.

mechanisms.Statement: Eligibility and haircuts turn asset quality into usable risk resources.
mechanisms.Limitation: Market stress can reduce collateral value and liquidity.

mechanisms.Statement: Waterfalls allocate the failed participant's resources before mutualised layers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Extreme losses can exceed defaulter resources.

mechanisms.Statement: Central clearing distributes extreme tail losses across surviving members under rules.
mechanisms.Limitation: Mutualisation can transmit stress among major institutions.

mechanisms.Statement: CCPs mobilise member expertise to restore a balanced book after failure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Auction incentives and concentration risk require governance.

mechanisms.Statement: Resolution authorities preserve critical clearing functions or wind them down.
mechanisms.Limitation: Resolution can still impose losses and market disruption.

mechanisms.Statement: Legally enforceable netting reduces replacement-cost exposure across contracts.
mechanisms.Limitation: Notional remains large and netting can fail legally or operationally.

mechanisms.Output: Actual market, credit and liquidity exposure
mechanisms.Statement: Notional measures scale, not the amount economically at risk.
mechanisms.Limitation: Notional can still signal interconnectedness and operational burden.

mechanisms.Statement: Bank balance-sheet expansion creates money-like claims while also creating credit or market exposure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Capital, liquidity, credit demand and settlement outflows constrain expansion.

mechanisms.Output: Payment at face value in cash or settlement money
mechanisms.Statement: Deposit insurance, central-bank liquidity and supervision support the expectation that bank deposits trade at par.
mechanisms.Limitation: Uninsured claims can lose value after failure.

mechanisms.Statement: Payments can move deposits away from the originating bank and create refinancing needs.
mechanisms.Limitation: Banks can offset flows through markets and central-bank facilities.

mechanisms.Statement: Banks earn spreads by funding less-liquid assets with runnable or repricing liabilities.
mechanisms.Limitation: Runs and rate changes can reverse the spread.

mechanisms.Statement: Regulation converts stressed cash-flow assumptions into liquid-asset requirements.
mechanisms.Limitation: HQLA may lose value or operational accessibility under extreme stress.

mechanisms.Statement: The NSFR discourages financing long-duration assets with unstable short-term liabilities.
mechanisms.Limitation: It does not eliminate all funding runs.

mechanisms.Statement: Deposit insurance preserves the money value of eligible deposit claims after failure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Coverage is capped and category-specific.

mechanisms.Statement: The industry collectively prepays part of the cost of insured-bank failure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Large systemic losses can exceed accumulated fund resources.

mechanisms.Statement: The FDIC compares estimated costs to the insurance fund before selecting a resolution method.
mechanisms.Limitation: The least-cost option for the DIF need not maximise every creditor's recovery.

mechanisms.Statement: A bridge bank preserves payments and franchise value while ownership is reallocated.
mechanisms.Limitation: It is temporary and can still generate losses.

mechanisms.Statement: Statutory priority converts asset recoveries into unequal creditor outcomes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Final recovery depends on asset realisation.

mechanisms.Statement: Resolution authorities can recapitalise a failing systemic bank by writing down or converting eligible liabilities.
mechanisms.Limitation: Execution across borders remains operationally difficult.

mechanisms.Statement: The discount window turns illiquid bank assets into temporary settlement cash at a haircut.
mechanisms.Limitation: It addresses liquidity, not necessarily solvency.

mechanisms.Output: Overnight reserves at a standing rate
mechanisms.Statement: A standing secured facility can cap extreme repo rates if eligible firms use it.
mechanisms.Limitation: Stigma and balance-sheet costs can limit uptake.

mechanisms.Statement: FHLBank funding converts collateral into liquidity while increasing asset encumbrance.
mechanisms.Limitation: Secured priority can shift losses to unsecured creditors.

mechanisms.Statement: Repo finances securities through a sale-and-repurchase legal structure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Maturity rollover and haircut risk remain.

mechanisms.Statement: A haircut protects the lender against price and liquidation risk.
mechanisms.Limitation: Haircuts can rise procyclically during stress.

mechanisms.Statement: A clearing bank reduces operational burden while becoming critical infrastructure.
mechanisms.Limitation: The agent does not guarantee the principal counterparties.

mechanisms.Statement: Money funds offer cash-like investment claims backed by market portfolios.
mechanisms.Limitation: Shares are not insured deposits.

mechanisms.Output: Asset sale, maturing cash or liquidity fee
mechanisms.Statement: Money funds transform investor withdrawals into portfolio liquidity demands.
mechanisms.Limitation: Large simultaneous redemptions can pressure markets.

mechanisms.Output: Overnight claim on the Federal Reserve
mechanisms.Statement: Eligible funds can replace private repo exposure with a public overnight counterparty.
mechanisms.Limitation: Facility access is limited and policy-driven.

mechanisms.Statement: Sponsorship expands CCP access to nonbanks without granting direct membership.
mechanisms.Limitation: Sponsor credit, margin and operational obligations remain.

mechanisms.Statement: FICC netting reduces settlement volumes and bilateral exposures.
mechanisms.Limitation: It concentrates default and liquidity risk at the CCP.

mechanisms.Statement: Securities lending enables market use without permanent disposal of the investment exposure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Legal title, voting and manufactured payments vary.

mechanisms.Statement: Recall rights let asset owners recover securities for voting, sale or settlement.
mechanisms.Limitation: Recall can create sourcing pressure and settlement risk.

mechanisms.Output: Potential realised loss during forced sale
mechanisms.Statement: Stable funding can defer loss realisation, while runs can force assets into the market.
mechanisms.Limitation: Economic value and accounting classification remain distinct.

mechanisms.Statement: Tax and plan rules convert current income into institutionally managed future consumption.
mechanisms.Limitation: Participation, vesting, fees and withdrawal rules vary.

mechanisms.Statement: The plan sponsor and pension vehicle retain investment, longevity and funding risk behind a promised benefit.
mechanisms.Limitation: PBGC protection is limited and does not erase sponsor obligations.

mechanisms.Statement: An account structure transfers much investment and retirement-income uncertainty from sponsor to participant.
mechanisms.Limitation: Default design, advice and annuity options can partly reshape the risk.

mechanisms.Statement: A QDIA turns non-decision into a consequential investment allocation.
mechanisms.Limitation: Participants retain opt-out rights and fiduciaries retain selection duties.

mechanisms.Statement: A target-date design automates rebalancing and de-risking across decades.
mechanisms.Limitation: The target date does not guarantee principal or sufficient retirement income.

mechanisms.Statement: Sponsors, committees, trustees and advisers divide control while retaining distinct duties.
mechanisms.Limitation: Delegation does not necessarily eliminate the delegating fiduciary’s oversight obligations.

mechanisms.Statement: PBGC premiums and legal authority convert a failed sponsor promise into a limited public-corporation payment claim.
mechanisms.Limitation: Not every plan or benefit is fully covered.

mechanisms.Output: Portfolio demand for duration, growth and illiquidity premia
mechanisms.Statement: Retirement obligations shape demand for bonds, equities, private markets and hedging instruments.
mechanisms.Limitation: Asset allocation differs across funding status, law and governance.

mechanisms.Statement: Registered funds aggregate savings into scalable market ownership.
mechanisms.Limitation: Shareholders own fund interests rather than specific portfolio assets.

mechanisms.Statement: An advisory contract converts beneficial capital into professional trading and stewardship authority.
mechanisms.Limitation: The adviser does not ordinarily become beneficial owner of client assets.

mechanisms.Statement: Redeemability converts a portfolio claim into a daily liquidity promise.
mechanisms.Limitation: Underlying assets may be less liquid than the redemption term.

mechanisms.Statement: Authorised participants connect the fund’s portfolio to exchange trading through creation and redemption.
mechanisms.Limitation: APs are not unconditional liquidity guarantors.

mechanisms.Statement: Price discrepancies can motivate APs and market makers to trade baskets and shares toward alignment.
mechanisms.Limitation: Stress, costs or market closure can weaken the mechanism.

mechanisms.Input: ETF portfolio and tax or liquidity needs
mechanisms.Statement: Written basket policies permit controlled deviations from pro-rata portfolio delivery.
mechanisms.Limitation: Discretion creates conflicts and requires governance.

mechanisms.Statement: Securities can be registered to a nominee while economic rights are recorded through participant and customer ledgers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Record title, possession, voting and economic exposure must be traced separately.

mechanisms.Statement: DTC centralises registered holdings and enables electronic transfer at scale.
mechanisms.Limitation: DTC does not maintain ultimate beneficial-owner records.

mechanisms.Statement: Notices, votes and payments move through depository, participant, custodian and owner layers.
mechanisms.Limitation: Delay and reconciliation risk remain.

mechanisms.Statement: Benchmark rules translate issuer characteristics into eligibility for tracked portfolios.
mechanisms.Limitation: Inclusion is not an endorsement or permanent status.

mechanisms.Statement: Index-tracking funds convert methodology changes into repeatable trades.
mechanisms.Limitation: Actual flows depend on assets tracking the index and implementation choices.

mechanisms.Statement: Consultations provide a formal channel from users to index governance.
mechanisms.Limitation: Consultation does not give any respondent final authority.

mechanisms.Statement: A limited partnership agreement lets the manager draw investor capital over time.
mechanisms.Limitation: Commitment is not immediate cash and is generally illiquid.

mechanisms.Statement: Private-fund agreements concentrate operating control in the general partner.
mechanisms.Limitation: LP consent rights and fiduciary or contractual limits vary.

mechanisms.Statement: Management fees and carried interest convert asset scale and realised gains into manager revenue.
mechanisms.Limitation: Headline performance does not equal LP net return.

mechanisms.Statement: A facility bridges capital calls and can alter reported timing and return metrics.
mechanisms.Limitation: It adds leverage and lender dependence without creating underlying investment value.

mechanisms.Statement: Later-stage fund assets become collateral for liquidity or distributions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Valuation uncertainty and structural priority can shift risk among stakeholders.

mechanisms.Statement: A non-bank fund converts long-duration investor capital into business credit.
mechanisms.Limitation: Illiquidity does not remove default or valuation risk.

mechanisms.Statement: Payment-in-kind terms preserve near-term borrower cash by capitalising interest.
mechanisms.Limitation: They can mask or postpone credit deterioration.

mechanisms.Statement: Banks fund funds, BDCs, warehouses and SPVs even when final credit is labelled non-bank.
mechanisms.Limitation: Commitment size is not identical to drawn exposure or loss.

mechanisms.Statement: A CLO aggregates corporate loans into a bankruptcy-remote vehicle.
mechanisms.Limitation: The vehicle remains exposed to borrower defaults and manager performance.

mechanisms.Statement: Payment priority redistributes expected loss and return across senior notes, mezzanine notes and equity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Tranching reallocates rather than eliminates credit loss.

mechanisms.Statement: Coverage tests redirect cash from junior to senior claims when protection erodes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Test compliance does not guarantee full repayment.

mechanisms.Statement: The manager can reshape portfolio risk within indenture constraints.
mechanisms.Limitation: Manager discretion is bounded and may conflict with different tranche interests.

mechanisms.Statement: The trustee and indenture operationalise priority across fees, debt and residual equity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Operational compliance does not eliminate valuation disputes.

mechanisms.Output: Private equity or private credit exposure
mechanisms.Statement: Alternative-asset sleeves can transmit private-market fees, valuation and liquidity characteristics into defined-contribution savings.
mechanisms.Limitation: The 2026 U.S. rule is proposed, not final, and product adoption is not guaranteed.

mechanisms.Statement: Registration and prospectus convert a private financing need into an offer to public investors.
mechanisms.Limitation: Registration enables lawful distribution but does not guarantee investor demand or capital raised.

mechanisms.Statement: Underwriters bridge issuer financing and investor demand while assuming contract-specific distribution and market risk.
mechanisms.Limitation: Firm commitment, best efforts and other structures must be distinguished.

mechanisms.Statement: Lead bookrunners aggregate demand signals and allocate scarce offering inventory.
mechanisms.Limitation: Indications may change and allocation need not be pro rata or neutral.

mechanisms.Statement: An exchange converts compliance with listing standards into admission to its market.
mechanisms.Limitation: Listing does not certify investment quality or prevent later delisting.

mechanisms.Statement: An opening auction compresses overnight information and order imbalance into a first transaction price.
mechanisms.Limitation: Auction design and participant mix influence but do not predetermine value.

mechanisms.Statement: The closing auction converts concentrated orders into a reference price used by indexes, funds and derivatives.
mechanisms.Limitation: A closing print can be sensitive to rebalancing flows and is not a complete measure of fundamental value.

mechanisms.Statement: A broker converts customer instructions into venue choice under best-execution and disclosure duties.
mechanisms.Limitation: The broker may use algorithms, affiliates or clearing arrangements; routing is not customer control of the venue.

mechanisms.Statement: Order-routing compensation can alter broker economics and create a conflict that must be managed under best-execution duties.
mechanisms.Limitation: Payment alone does not prove inferior execution or a rule violation.

mechanisms.Statement: A wholesaler executes against customer flow and may provide price improvement relative to displayed quotations.
mechanisms.Limitation: Internalisation can reduce displayed interaction and must be assessed with execution-quality data.

mechanisms.Input: Venue quality, price and routing economics
mechanisms.Statement: A broker's supervisory process compares reasonably available markets and customer outcomes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Best execution is facts-and-circumstances based and does not promise the single best imaginable fill.

mechanisms.Input: Minimum increment and venue fee schedule
mechanisms.Statement: Pricing increments and fee caps shape queue competition, rebates and order-placement economics.
mechanisms.Limitation: Observed spreads reflect many variables beyond rule design.

mechanisms.Statement: An ATS can connect selected counterparties without displaying all interest to the public market.
mechanisms.Limitation: ATSs are regulated broker-dealer systems, not unregulated private exchanges.

mechanisms.Statement: A market maker uses capital and inventory to absorb order imbalances and quote two-sided markets.
mechanisms.Limitation: Market making creates exposure and does not grant unilateral control of the security's price.

mechanisms.Output: Facilitated open, close and volatility event
mechanisms.Statement: A DMM combines defined obligations, capital and auction participation at a primary listing venue.
mechanisms.Limitation: The DMM operates under exchange rules and competes with other liquidity sources.

mechanisms.Statement: SIPs aggregate exchange and FINRA reports into system-wide quotation and transaction feeds.
mechanisms.Limitation: Consolidation does not make the feed identical to every proprietary depth product.

mechanisms.Statement: Commercial feeds can provide depth and latency characteristics beyond consolidated core data.
mechanisms.Limitation: A data advantage does not establish misuse, guaranteed profit or knowledge of hidden orders.

mechanisms.Statement: Trading venues convert compulsory market interaction into sellable data products and connectivity services.
mechanisms.Limitation: Commercial value does not prove monopoly pricing without cost and substitution analysis.

mechanisms.Statement: CAT converts fragmented broker and venue records into a regulator-accessible order lifecycle.
mechanisms.Limitation: Regulatory visibility must be balanced against cybersecurity, privacy and data-minimisation concerns.

mechanisms.Output: Additional price discovery and thinner liquidity periods
mechanisms.Statement: Near-continuous trading expands access while shifting liquidity, staffing, data and corporate-action dependencies across time zones.
mechanisms.Limitation: Approval of an exchange does not establish universal 23/5 liquidity or final approval of every extended-hours phase.

mechanisms.Statement: NSCC becomes central counterparty and compresses many trades into net positions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Netting reduces movements but concentrates member, liquidity and operational risk.

mechanisms.Statement: DTC reduces physical movement by maintaining central custody and changing participant records electronically.
mechanisms.Limitation: DTC or Cede record status does not make them the ultimate economic owner.

mechanisms.Statement: T+1 reduces the time available for adverse price moves or counterparty failure before standard settlement.
mechanisms.Limitation: A shorter cycle does not eliminate fails, funding pressure or operational error.

mechanisms.Statement: Transfer agents maintain the issuer-facing record of ownership and process corporate actions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Registered-holder data do not necessarily identify every beneficial owner in street name.

mechanisms.Statement: A margin agreement converts portfolio collateral into purchasing or short-selling capacity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Leverage amplifies gains and losses and permits contractual liquidation.

mechanisms.Statement: Locate rules connect proposed short sales to securities-borrow availability.
mechanisms.Limitation: A locate does not guarantee delivery or prevent later borrow recall.

mechanisms.Statement: Close-out rules force defined unresolved fails toward settlement.
mechanisms.Limitation: A fail can arise from operational or market causes and is not itself proof of naked short manipulation.

mechanisms.Output: Regulatory and later public loan data
mechanisms.Statement: Rule 10c-1a is designed to make terms and activity in securities lending more legible.
mechanisms.Limitation: Compliance dates were extended and reported data will not reveal every beneficial-owner motive.

mechanisms.Statement: Form SHO converts threshold-level manager reports into market transparency.
mechanisms.Limitation: Aggregated reporting does not identify every strategy or prove manipulation.

mechanisms.Output: Broker, DTC participant and registered-holder chain
mechanisms.Statement: Intermediated holding separates economic ownership, record title, custody and communication rights.
mechanisms.Limitation: The chain can create opacity without erasing the investor's economic entitlement.

mechanisms.Output: Issuer visibility or anonymity within the proxy system
mechanisms.Statement: The OBO/NOBO distinction determines whether issuer communications can identify a street-name owner directly.
mechanisms.Limitation: OBO status is not anonymity from brokers, regulators or legal process.

mechanisms.Input: Issuer meeting materials and intermediary positions
mechanisms.Statement: Proxy processors convert record-holder positions into distributed voting materials and returned instructions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Operational processing does not determine how the investor votes.

mechanisms.Statement: Tabulators translate dispersed instructions into proposal and director-election outcomes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Certified totals may still be subject to legal challenge or reconciliation issues.

mechanisms.Statement: Proxy advisers convert complex meeting materials into policy-based recommendations for clients.
mechanisms.Limitation: A recommendation is not a vote and clients may apply custom policies.

mechanisms.Statement: Universal proxy lets shareholders voting remotely select among duly nominated candidates across slates.
mechanisms.Limitation: Access to a common card does not equal campaign success or board control.

mechanisms.Statement: Rule 14a-8 can convert a qualifying shareholder request into a company-wide vote.
mechanisms.Limitation: Ballot inclusion does not make a proposal binding or adopted.

mechanisms.Statement: Large-position reporting makes ownership concentration and possible control intent visible to the market.
mechanisms.Limitation: Crossing a threshold does not itself establish control, coordination or wrongdoing.

mechanisms.Statement: An activist can convert a minority stake, public argument and proxy solicitation into governance leverage.
mechanisms.Limitation: Influence depends on other shareholders, law, board response and campaign credibility.

mechanisms.Output: Voting right at meeting despite later trading
mechanisms.Statement: Corporate record dates can separate current economic exposure from the right to instruct a vote.
mechanisms.Limitation: The effect depends on jurisdiction, settlement and securities-lending arrangements.

mechanisms.Statement: Voting infrastructure converts dispersed ownership claims into board composition and advisory or binding outcomes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Many resolutions are advisory and boards retain legally defined discretion.

mechanisms.Statement: Large order-flow share is sometimes misread as authority to set any public stock price at will.
mechanisms.Limitation: Prices emerge across competing venues, investors, arbitrage, rules and capital constraints.

mechanisms.Output: Claim that Cede economically owns all deposited companies
mechanisms.Statement: Record ownership is sometimes collapsed into beneficial ownership and control.
mechanisms.Limitation: Cede is nominee record holder for deposited securities; participant and beneficial-owner claims remain distinct.

mechanisms.Output: Auditable duties, data minimisation and appeal rights
mechanisms.Statement: A resilient design would expose routing, ownership and voting conversions to independent audit while limiting unnecessary personal-data collection.
mechanisms.Limitation: Normative proposal requiring legal, technical and cost evaluation.

mechanisms.Input: Government cash shortfall and refinancing need
mechanisms.Statement: Treasury issuance converts current fiscal financing needs into tradable claims on future public revenues.
mechanisms.Limitation: Issuance volume is jointly determined by deficits, redemptions, cash policy and debt-management choices.

mechanisms.Statement: Treasury auctions aggregate bids and award successful bidders at the highest accepted yield, rate or margin.
mechanisms.Limitation: Auction results can be influenced by market conditions without implying manipulation.

mechanisms.Statement: Competitive bidders reveal willingness to fund Treasury at specified terms.
mechanisms.Limitation: Bids may reflect hedges, customer demand, balance-sheet constraints or trading strategies.

mechanisms.Output: Guaranteed award at auction-determined terms within limits
mechanisms.Statement: Noncompetitive bidding permits access without forecasting the clearing yield.
mechanisms.Limitation: The bidder accepts price uncertainty and remains subject to eligibility and limits.

mechanisms.Statement: The primary-dealer system connects monetary-policy counterparties to sovereign issuance coverage.
mechanisms.Limitation: Primary dealers do not purchase every Treasury security and their relationship is not regulatory endorsement.

mechanisms.Statement: When-issued trading produces a market reference for auction bidding and hedging.
mechanisms.Limitation: The when-issued price is not the auction result and can move materially.

mechanisms.Statement: Treasury combines official forecasts, dealer views and TBAC recommendations before announcing financing policy.
mechanisms.Limitation: Private advice is not final governmental authority.

mechanisms.Statement: An advisory committee converts private market knowledge into debt-management advice.
mechanisms.Limitation: Membership does not confer statutory decision power or prove capture.

mechanisms.Statement: Liquid sovereign yields become benchmarks for discounting and pricing other obligations.
mechanisms.Limitation: Benchmark use does not make every Treasury maturity equally liquid or free of market risk.

mechanisms.Statement: Treasury securities can be converted into repo funding, margin resources and regulatory liquidity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Collateral value remains sensitive to duration, haircut, settlement and market stress.

mechanisms.Output: Lower yield or tighter spread relative to less liquid securities
mechanisms.Statement: Trading concentration can create a liquidity value separate from credit risk.
mechanisms.Limitation: Observed differences also reflect maturity, supply, taxes and hedging demand.

mechanisms.Statement: Dealers use capital and repo funding to absorb imbalances across auctions and secondary markets.
mechanisms.Limitation: Dealer capacity is finite and can deteriorate in stress.

mechanisms.Output: Reserve balances and SOMA security holdings
mechanisms.Statement: The Trading Desk exchanges reserves for Treasury securities under FOMC direction.
mechanisms.Limitation: A purchase does not directly finance a specific fiscal expenditure or guarantee asset-price outcomes.

mechanisms.Statement: Rollovers maintain portfolio exposure without an ordinary competitive bid.
mechanisms.Limitation: Rollover policy can change and does not remove Treasury refinancing needs.

mechanisms.Statement: Federal Reserve lending can reduce settlement pressure in particular Treasury issues.
mechanisms.Limitation: Lending is temporary and does not eliminate shorts, fails or scarcity.

mechanisms.Statement: Movements into and out of the TGA alter reserve balances unless offset by Federal Reserve operations.
mechanisms.Limitation: The direction and magnitude depend on contemporaneous flows and policy operations.

mechanisms.Statement: A bond offering converts future payment promises into current financing.
mechanisms.Limitation: The transaction creates leverage and does not ensure productive use of proceeds.

mechanisms.Output: Tradable institutional security among eligible buyers
mechanisms.Statement: Rule 144A supports institutional resale without a registered public offering.
mechanisms.Limitation: The exemption does not eliminate disclosure, antifraud or investor-credit risk.

mechanisms.Statement: A rating agency converts information and methodology into a standardised credit opinion.
mechanisms.Limitation: A rating is an opinion, not a guarantee or substitute for investor analysis.

mechanisms.Statement: Contracts and mandates can translate a rating change into forced action or higher financing costs.
mechanisms.Limitation: Not every mandate uses the same thresholds and causality can run from fundamentals to rating.

mechanisms.Output: Restricted issuer action or creditor remedy
mechanisms.Statement: Bond covenants constrain defined actions and allocate control in adverse states.
mechanisms.Limitation: Many investment-grade bonds have limited covenants and enforcement depends on exact drafting.

mechanisms.Statement: A negative pledge can protect unsecured bondholders from later collateral subordination.
mechanisms.Limitation: Exceptions and permitted liens can materially weaken protection.

mechanisms.Output: Higher creditor priority over specified assets
mechanisms.Statement: Security interests convert general repayment claims into asset-backed enforcement rights.
mechanisms.Limitation: Priority depends on perfection, competing claims, valuation and insolvency law.

mechanisms.Output: Central contract administration and enforcement channel
mechanisms.Statement: The trustee administers the indenture and may act for holders after specified defaults.
mechanisms.Limitation: Trustee duties before default can be limited and the trustee is not an investment manager.

mechanisms.Statement: Indentures aggregate dispersed holders through voting thresholds.
mechanisms.Limitation: Thresholds and reserved matters vary, and minority holders may retain individual rights.

mechanisms.Statement: Acceleration transforms future scheduled payments into a current enforcement claim.
mechanisms.Limitation: Acceleration may be rescinded, stayed or limited by bankruptcy and contract.

mechanisms.Output: DTC book-entry distribution and settlement access
mechanisms.Statement: DTC eligibility makes a debt security operable within central depository infrastructure.
mechanisms.Limitation: Eligibility is not a credit assessment or investment endorsement.

mechanisms.Output: Linked issuance, trading, reporting and settlement records
mechanisms.Statement: A common identifier permits institutional systems to refer to the same bond.
mechanisms.Limitation: Identifier accuracy does not resolve beneficial ownership or economic exposure.

mechanisms.Statement: TRACE converts opaque over-the-counter trades into time, price, yield and volume records.
mechanisms.Limitation: Dissemination caps, delays and reporting corrections affect the public view.

mechanisms.Input: Dealer principal trade and customer execution
mechanisms.Statement: A dealer embeds compensation in the bond price subject to fair-pricing and disclosure rules.
mechanisms.Limitation: A spread is not automatically excessive and prevailing market price can be difficult to establish.

mechanisms.Statement: Electronic RFQ protocols expose an order to competing dealer quotes.
mechanisms.Limitation: Dealer selection, information leakage and response quality remain important.

mechanisms.Statement: All-to-all protocols can allow asset managers and other participants to supply liquidity.
mechanisms.Limitation: Participation does not eliminate dealer intermediation or guarantee execution.

mechanisms.Statement: Sparse transactions cause valuations to depend on estimates and comparable securities.
mechanisms.Limitation: Illiquidity differs across issues, sectors, sizes and market conditions.

mechanisms.Statement: A pooled vehicle can offer investors easier exit than direct sale of every underlying bond.
mechanisms.Limitation: Redemption liquidity can create sales, dilution or pricing stress in adverse markets.

mechanisms.Statement: Fixed-income benchmarks translate methodology into portfolio holdings and trading flows.
mechanisms.Limitation: Index inclusion is not endorsement and active managers can deviate.

mechanisms.Statement: A tender offer converts current cash into reduced future debt obligations.
mechanisms.Limitation: Participation is voluntary unless separate contractual rights apply.

mechanisms.Output: New bond with altered maturity, coupon or priority
mechanisms.Statement: Exchange offers restructure liabilities without a conventional cash repayment.
mechanisms.Limitation: The exchange can transfer value among issuer and holder groups.

mechanisms.Statement: A consent solicitation converts voting thresholds into changed creditor protection.
mechanisms.Limitation: Consent does not establish unanimous holder support and may be linked to a tender.

mechanisms.Statement: Distressed investors can convert debt priority and blocking positions into restructuring influence.
mechanisms.Limitation: Influence depends on capital structure, thresholds, law and coalition formation.

mechanisms.Statement: Committees reduce coordination costs in defaults and restructurings.
mechanisms.Limitation: Committee membership does not bind all holders or eliminate conflicts among tranches.

mechanisms.Output: Market-implied compensation for credit and liquidity risk
mechanisms.Statement: The spread over a Treasury or swap benchmark converts multiple risks into a quoted premium.
mechanisms.Limitation: Spread changes do not identify a single cause or default probability.

mechanisms.Statement: Corporate debt pricing commonly references sovereign or swap benchmarks plus a spread.
mechanisms.Limitation: Issuer-specific credit, liquidity and optionality can dominate benchmark movements.

mechanisms.Output: Claim of guaranteed repayment or objective truth
mechanisms.Statement: Ratings are sometimes treated as deterministic guarantees rather than opinions.
mechanisms.Limitation: Ratings can change, disagree and fail to predict realised losses.

mechanisms.Output: Claim of zero risk in every dimension
mechanisms.Statement: Treasuries are sometimes described as literally riskless without specifying credit, market, inflation, liquidity or custody risk.
mechanisms.Limitation: They are commonly treated as default-risk benchmarks in U.S. dollars but remain exposed to other risks.

mechanisms.Output: Transparent authority, audit and creditor protections
mechanisms.Statement: A robust design would expose auction, rating, covenant, dealer and restructuring interfaces to auditable rules and appeal.
mechanisms.Limitation: The optimal balance among liquidity, privacy, cost and constraint requires empirical testing.

mechanisms.Input: Buy and sell interest across a currency pair
mechanisms.Statement: Dealer quotes, electronic orders and risk transfer convert relative currency demand into a tradable price.
mechanisms.Limitation: The observed rate depends on venue, size, timing, credit and settlement terms.

mechanisms.Statement: Dealers use balance sheet, credit and hedging capacity to absorb currency imbalances.
mechanisms.Limitation: Dealer capacity is finite and does not grant unilateral control of a currency.
