claims.Claim: Large AI infrastructure is increasingly financed through circular supplier–customer–investor relationships joining model labs, clouds, chip firms and sovereign capital.
claims.Review rule: Track conditional tranches, purchase obligations, credit guarantees and ultimate risk holders.

claims.Claim: The dollar system power depends on clearing, settlement, custody and sanctions institutions—not only currency denomination or Treasury reserves.
claims.Review rule: Map participant access, legal jurisdiction and failure modes for each rail.

claims.Claim: Stablecoins extend the dollar while creating new private chokepoints at reserve managers, issuers, custodians and administrative freeze keys.
claims.Review rule: Track reserve custodians, redemption banks, blacklist governance and bankruptcy rights.

claims.Claim: AI infrastructure is increasingly financed as a coupled system of private credit, supplier guarantees, dedicated power and special-purpose asset ownership.
claims.Review rule: Obtain project-level loan documents, guarantees, PPAs, leases and beneficial ownership.

claims.Claim: New defence-tech firms are converging with incumbent primes and enterprise procurement rather than simply replacing the traditional defence industry.
claims.Review rule: Add task orders, data rights, weapons-authorisation layers and programme outcomes.

claims.Claim: Commodity traders, shipping networks and marine insurers are conversion institutions linking finance to physical resource delivery.
claims.Review rule: Add facility banks, cargo ownership, charter parties, insurance exclusions and sanctions licences.

claims.Claim: Credit ratings, audit opinions and data-broker scores are private classifications that become powerful when institutional mandates attach consequences to them.
claims.Review rule: Map issuer-payment models, client mandates, appeal rights, error rates and regulatory dependencies.

claims.Claim: Political-platform power includes control over paid reach, policy eligibility and the data interfaces through which outsiders can audit the platform.
claims.Review rule: Separate paid advertising, organic ranking, enforcement and research-data access.

claims.Claim: Strategic control increasingly operates through licences and permissions rather than direct ownership.
claims.Related IDs: CTL, DIG, CLD, APPSTORE and GRID relationships
claims.Review rule: Record the issuing authority, legal basis, object controlled, duration and appeal route for every permission edge.

claims.Claim: The advanced-semiconductor stack is a sequence of interdependent chokepoints: EDA, equipment, foundry capacity, memory, packaging and export licences.
claims.Related IDs: CTL-001–CTL-013; prior MAT and INF rows
claims.Review rule: Add KLA, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, packaging and HBM contracts in the next pass.

claims.Claim: Hyperscalers are vertically integrating cables and classified cloud, making communications infrastructure part of platform power.
claims.Review rule: Obtain cable ownership shares, landing licences, capacity allocations and JWCC task orders.

claims.Claim: App stores function as private regulatory systems whose permissioning power is now constrained by public gatekeeper law.
claims.Review rule: Measure approval, removal, appeal, fees and alternative-distribution usage by jurisdiction.

claims.Claim: Index and benchmark providers influence capital and contract terms through methodology reuse, not through beneficial ownership of linked assets.
claims.Review rule: Test event-study effects of inclusions, exclusions, country reclassifications and benchmark revisions.

claims.Claim: Current US beneficial-ownership rules create an explicit transparency asymmetry between domestic and defined foreign entities.
claims.Review rule: Track final rule changes, state registries, bank CDD and law-enforcement access.

claims.Claim: Reinsurance and grid access are hidden capacity constraints: they determine whether physical assets can be insured and AI loads can be energised.
claims.Review rule: Add treaty terms, exclusions, regional capacity auctions and cost-allocation outcomes.

claims.Claim: The internet remains decentralised in operation but depends on concentrated coordination layers including root-zone management, major resolvers, cables and commercial satellite systems.
claims.Review rule: Map root-server operators, major resolvers, cable ownership and government satellite task orders.

claims.Claim: Knowledge power is distributed across patents, trade secrets, architecture licences and open standards rather than patents alone.
claims.Review rule: Add direct patent-family and licence-contract review before making company-specific exclusion claims.

claims.Claim: Arm and RISC-V represent contrasting architecture-governance models: proprietary licensing and royalties versus an open standard with commercial implementations.
claims.Review rule: Compare total switching costs, software ecosystems, verification and national-security dependencies.

claims.Claim: AI standards become power when procurement, certification, insurance or regulation attaches consequences to conformity.
claims.Review rule: Map which contracts and laws incorporate each standard by reference.

claims.Claim: Public AI research infrastructure can counter compute concentration but remains dependent on allocation rules and private contributions.
claims.Review rule: Add partner-level resources, award recipients, utilisation and conflict-of-interest rules.

claims.Claim: Immigration systems are part of the innovation stack because visas and work authorisation determine which firms and universities can access global talent.
claims.Review rule: Add employer-level sponsorship, wage, nationality, transfer and retention data.

claims.Claim: Technology lobbying is a documented policy-conversion channel, but disclosure establishes advocacy rather than bribery or policy causation.
claims.Review rule: Link filings to meeting logs, draft text, rule changes and counter-lobbying before making causal claims.

claims.Claim: Professional intermediaries—including standards bodies, certifiers, research allocators, immigration authorities and lobbyists—shape access without owning the underlying technology.
claims.Related IDs: STD, RES, TAL and LOB layers
claims.Review rule: Treat each intermediary's formal authority and appeal structure separately.

claims.Claim: Corporate governance power is split among legal jurisdiction, boards, shareholders, advisers, custodians and courts rather than residing in shareholders alone.
claims.Review rule: Map company-specific charters, share classes, delegated votes and litigation outcomes.

claims.Claim: Intermediated securities markets separate record title, beneficial ownership, voting instructions and economic exposure.
claims.Review rule: Add stock-lending, omnibus-account and reconciliation data before attributing final voting control.

claims.Claim: Secured-credit law determines loss allocation before bankruptcy by assigning collateral priority, while Chapter 11 reallocates control during distress.
claims.Review rule: Collect loan agreements, financing statements, DIP orders and confirmed plans for empirical testing.

claims.Claim: Close-out netting reduces gross derivatives exposure but creates a legally privileged failure-resolution path outside ordinary claim-by-claim insolvency.
claims.Review rule: Compare netting jurisdictions, safe harbours and actual default outcomes.

claims.Claim: Arbitration converts prior consent into private or international adjudicative authority, but national courts remain necessary for enforcement and public-law boundaries.
claims.Review rule: Map seats, governing laws, enforcement actions, arbitrator appointments and funders.

claims.Claim: Sovereign debt restructuring is a coordination system without a single bankruptcy court, relying on IMF analysis, creditor groups, CACs and comparability principles.
claims.Review rule: Build case-level timelines for official, bonded, bank and domestic debt treatments.

claims.Claim: Litigation finance can broaden access to enforcement while converting legal claims into private financial assets with disclosure and conflict questions.
claims.Review rule: Collect funding agreements, return waterfalls, control rights, disclosures and case outcomes.

claims.Claim: The spring-loaded door is legally implemented through priority and forum rules: the actor controlling liquidity, collateral or adjudication can capture value after failure.
claims.Related IDs: COLL, BK, DNET, ARB, SOV and LIT layers
claims.Review rule: Test crisis transactions using court dockets, bond exchanges and recovery waterfalls.

claims.Claim: Tax sovereignty is increasingly coordinated through minimum-tax, transfer-pricing and country-reporting systems, but tax collection remains nationally administered.
claims.Review rule: Distinguish model rules, domestic implementation, information exchange and final assessment.

claims.Claim: Federal procurement power is exercised through contract type, supplier eligibility, ordering authority, data rights and the difference between ceilings and actual obligations.
claims.Review rule: Never treat IDIQ or OTA ceilings as realised expenditure without order-level data.

claims.Claim: Industrial policy combines negotiated grants, public R&D and formula-based tax credits, each with different selection, accountability and risk-sharing mechanisms.
claims.Review rule: Measure disbursement, private co-investment, additionality, output and spillovers separately.

claims.Claim: Federal credit programmes can support projects with modest recorded subsidy costs relative to face exposure because the budget records expected net present-value cost rather than maximum liability.
claims.Review rule: Retain face exposure, subsidy estimate, re-estimate and realised cash loss as separate fields.

claims.Claim: Deposit insurance is principally industry funded, but its confidence and resolution function makes it part of the public financial safety net.
claims.Review rule: Do not infer current taxpayer loss from the existence of a public backstop.

claims.Claim: Central-bank collateral rules determine which private assets can be converted into public money during stress and at what haircut.
claims.Review rule: Map facility eligibility, collateral class, haircut, maturity, rate and recourse.

claims.Claim: Development and export guarantees mobilise private capital by reallocating selected risks, but authorised exposure is not equivalent to expected public cost.
claims.Review rule: Separate authorisation, commitment, disbursement, exposure, subsidy cost, claim and recovery.

claims.Claim: Public risk transfer is the fiscal mirror of private collateral priority: the state can lower private financing cost by absorbing risks that are remote, political or difficult to diversify.
claims.Related IDs: SUB, FCR, DEP, LIQ and GUA layers
claims.Review rule: Test whether support creates additional capacity or merely transfers rents and tail losses.

claims.Claim: Land ownership is a regulated bundle whose economic value depends on zoning, permits, development rights, taxation and infrastructure access.
claims.Review rule: Map parcel-level zoning, permits, assessments and infrastructure before attributing value to title alone.

claims.Claim: US housing transactions depend on layered public and private registries: county records establish public notice while MERS tracks member-reported servicing and beneficial interests.
claims.Review rule: Separate deed title, mortgagee of record, note ownership, servicing rights and eNote control.

claims.Claim: Mortgage securitization separates household occupancy, property title, loan ownership, servicing, guaranty and investor cash-flow rights.
claims.Review rule: Never use 'the bank owns the house' without identifying default status and the exact legal claim.

claims.Claim: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae, FHA and the FHLBanks perform different public-risk and liquidity functions and must not be collapsed into one housing guarantee.
claims.Review rule: Preserve explicit sovereign guarantee, Enterprise corporate guarantee, insurance and collateralised advance as separate instruments.

claims.Claim: Institutional single-family rental ownership is economically significant in selected markets, but portfolio counts alone do not prove national market dominance or abusive conduct.
claims.Review rule: Test local acquisition share, rent, eviction, maintenance and tenant outcomes against matched landlords.

claims.Claim: Property tax and municipal debt connect land values and user charges to local fiscal capacity, infrastructure and intergenerational obligations.
claims.Review rule: Separate general-obligation, revenue-bond, tax increment and conduit structures.

claims.Claim: Zoning and mortgage standards jointly determine access: one governs physical supply while the other governs which households and loans can receive scalable finance.
claims.Review rule: Test interactions between permitting, conforming limits, insurance and local prices.

claims.Claim: Housing is simultaneously shelter, collateral, tax base, securitized cash flow and institutional portfolio asset; each role creates a different claim on the same physical property.
claims.Review rule: Maintain separate legal objects and do not infer unified control from overlap.

claims.Claim: Oil production coordination is a recurring sovereign bargaining system, not proof that OPEC or one state controls the entire world oil price.
claims.Review rule: Compare coalition output, spare capacity, inventories, demand and non-member supply before attributing price changes.

claims.Claim: Commodity benchmarks are privately or exchange-administered constitutions that convert selected physical evidence into prices used across contracts and derivatives.
claims.Review rule: Audit methodology, eligible grades, timing, participants and conflict controls before alleging manipulation.

claims.Claim: Commodity merchants exercise power through liquidity, information, logistics and optionality rather than necessarily owning the underlying reserves or final industrial assets.
claims.Review rule: Measure counterparty concentration, storage, credit facilities, offtake and benchmark participation by commodity.

claims.Claim: LNG power depends on the integrated stack of upstream gas, liquefaction, long-term offtake, specialised vessels, destination access and benchmark pricing.
claims.Review rule: Separate nameplate capacity, operational output, contracted volume, cargo liftings and destination.

claims.Claim: Ship ownership, flag, registered owner, commercial charterer, operator, insurer and cargo owner are different legal and economic roles.
claims.Review rule: Use IMO identifiers and voyage-specific records before attributing control or liability.

claims.Claim: Marine insurance and sanctions policy turn private service networks into geopolitical enforcement channels, but they do not physically stop every targeted cargo.
claims.Review rule: Track insurer, flag, bank, service jurisdiction, attestation and alternative providers by voyage.

claims.Claim: Letters of credit finance documents rather than goods: payment assurance arises from bank undertakings conditioned on documentary compliance.
claims.Review rule: Separate commercial performance, documentary compliance, fraud, sanctions and final cargo delivery.

claims.Claim: A commodity cargo is simultaneously physical material, benchmark exposure, warehouse or bill-of-lading title, financed collateral, insured risk and sanctions-screened trade.
claims.Review rule: Maintain separate identities for cargo, contract, vessel, benchmark, bank obligation and insurance policy.

claims.Claim: AI compute power is a stack, not a single-company asset: EDA, lithography, foundry, packaging, memory, networking, cloud, power and model demand are separate conversion points.
claims.Review rule: Identify the exact layer before attributing control or dependency.

claims.Claim: NVIDIA's commercial dominance does not mean it owns TSMC, ASML, cloud customers or the electricity infrastructure supporting its accelerators.
claims.Review rule: Separate supplier dependence, bargaining power, ownership and technical standards.

claims.Claim: OpenAI's infrastructure strategy is multi-provider: Microsoft remains the primary cloud partner while Stargate, Oracle, SoftBank and custom silicon expand alternative capacity.
claims.Review rule: Preserve cloud priority, purchase commitment, equity investment and project ownership as different relationships.

claims.Claim: Anthropic's Amazon and Google agreements demonstrate multi-cloud bargaining rather than ownership by either provider.
claims.Review rule: Track investment, primary-cloud status, accelerator type, contracted GW and model availability separately.

claims.Claim: AI infrastructure can be financed as long-duration infrastructure when GPUs, powered facilities and customer contracts are bundled, but technological obsolescence creates unusual collateral risk.
claims.Review rule: Record debt maturity, collateral, customer concentration, hardware generation and residual value.

claims.Claim: Electricity and interconnection are now binding AI inputs; compute capacity should be measured in energised, operational megawatts rather than announced dollars or planned gigawatts alone.
claims.Review rule: Separate announced, contracted, interconnected, energised and utilised capacity.

claims.Claim: Export controls convert chip performance, ultimate-parent identity and destination into legal access to AI capability.
claims.Review rule: Track item classification, destination, customer, licence status, conditions and end use.

claims.Claim: AI CEOs are high-leverage authorised brokers inside corporate systems, but public prominence is not evidence that they personally own partner companies or secretly coordinate the whole stack.
claims.Review rule: Use formal office, board rights, share ownership, signed contracts and disclosed investments—not fame or social proximity.

claims.Claim: Bill Gates is historically central to Microsoft but is not the current executive controlling Microsoft's Azure and OpenAI infrastructure decisions.
claims.Review rule: Preserve historical influence while assigning current executive authority to current officeholders.

claims.Claim: The Internet is a federation of independently owned networks joined through standards, routing, peering and identifier systems; no single company owns it.
claims.Review rule: Identify the exact physical, routing, naming or platform layer before attributing control.

claims.Claim: Private platform companies increasingly own submarine-cable capacity, but cable ownership is not equivalent to ownership of landing stations, national backhaul or all traffic on the route.
claims.Review rule: Record fiber-pair ownership, landing entities, capacity rights and terrestrial interconnection separately.

claims.Claim: ICANN and IANA coordinate identifiers and the DNS root; they do not control Internet content, access networks or the routing decisions of autonomous systems.
claims.Review rule: Preserve policy, root-zone operations, registry, registrar, resolver and hosting as distinct roles.

claims.Claim: Internet exchanges and CDNs reduce latency and transit dependence while creating new concentration and correlated-failure risks.
claims.Review rule: Measure connected networks, traffic, facility dependence, control-plane design and failover.

claims.Claim: Satellite broadband is an integrated stack of spectrum, launch, satellites, gateways, terminals and terrestrial interconnection; constellation size alone does not equal usable national service.
claims.Review rule: Separate launched, operational, licensed, covered and subscribed capacity.

claims.Claim: App stores govern distribution, review and discovery on their platforms, but ecosystem billings are not identical to platform commission revenue.
claims.Review rule: Separate developer sales, physical-goods commerce, digital payments and platform fees.

claims.Claim: Executive authority must be date-specific: Tim Cook is Apple CEO on July 27, 2026, while John Ternus is designated to assume the role on September 1, 2026.
claims.Review rule: Assign authority using the effective date rather than announcement date.

claims.Claim: Elon Musk has unusually concentrated formal voting and executive control at SpaceX, but that does not create legal authority over spectrum regulators, foreign markets or independent ground infrastructure.
claims.Review rule: Separate corporate voting control from sovereign licensing and third-party assets.

claims.Claim: Digital distribution power exists at several layers—cable route, landing station, routing exchange, DNS, CDN, satellite gateway and app store—and can migrate when redundancy is added.
claims.Review rule: Map substitution and failover before claiming a permanent chokepoint.

claims.Claim: Digital identity is not a single database: issuer, wallet, authentication service, credential holder and relying party are separate roles.
claims.Review rule: Record the exact credential, issuer, presentation, verifier and downstream decision.

claims.Claim: A successful identity authentication establishes that supplied factors matched the system's record; it does not by itself establish eligibility, consent, truthfulness or legal guilt.
claims.Review rule: Separate identity match from the service or enforcement decision.

claims.Claim: Visa and Mastercard are high-scale payment networks, but they usually do not hold the customer's bank deposit, extend every credit line or own the merchant sale.
claims.Review rule: Preserve issuer, network, acquirer, merchant and customer roles.

claims.Claim: Instant-payment rails settle between institutions; retail customers generally access them through banks or payment service providers that retain identity, fraud and compliance controls.
claims.Review rule: Separate wholesale rail participation from retail product availability.

claims.Claim: Advertising power combines auction rules, predicted user response, inventory access and consent architecture; it is not reducible to the highest monetary bid.
claims.Review rule: Record bid, quality, prediction, inventory, identifier and platform-policy layers.

claims.Claim: LiveRamp identity resolution is commercial interoperability infrastructure, not a state-issued identity or an infallible representation of a person.
claims.Review rule: Distinguish legal identity, directly identifiable information, pseudonymous identifiers and modelled matches.

claims.Claim: Risk, fraud and operational analytics become consequential when embedded in institutional decision rules; vendors provide inputs while customers retain formal authority.
claims.Review rule: Document who sets thresholds, who can override and who issues the final decision.

claims.Claim: Public-safety platforms can connect sensors and evidence across agencies, but platform reach does not establish lawful use, accuracy or federal access in every deployment.
claims.Review rule: Record local ownership, retention, sharing settings, audit logs and legal authority.

claims.Claim: The adaptive surveillance risk arises from feedback among identity, payment, advertising, risk and sensor systems; evidence of one connection is not evidence of a unified command system.
claims.Review rule: Require a documented contract, data flow or governance right for every cross-system edge.

claims.Claim: FATF Recommendations are international standards, not self-executing domestic law; coercive effect comes from national implementation and private responses.
claims.Review rule: Record the implementing statute, regulation, supervisor and effective date.

claims.Claim: FATF increased monitoring is not a FATF economic-sanctions regime, although institutions may impose higher due diligence or de-risking in response.
claims.Review rule: Separate formal FATF status from bank, investor and government reactions.

claims.Claim: Beneficial ownership identifies ultimate natural-person ownership or control; it does not by itself establish criminality, operational control or legal title to every asset.
claims.Review rule: Record ownership percentage, control right, registry source and verification status.

claims.Claim: A Suspicious Activity Report is a confidential financial-intelligence lead, not proof that the reported person committed a crime.
claims.Review rule: Separate report, analysis, investigation, charge and conviction.

claims.Claim: OFAC blocking immobilises property; it is not the same as confiscation, forfeiture or transfer of title to the U.S. government.
claims.Review rule: Use distinct fields for blocked, seized, forfeited, returned and distributed assets.

claims.Claim: SWIFT transmits financial messages and does not generally hold customer funds or manage customer accounts; message exclusion can impede payments without itself seizing money.
claims.Review rule: Separate messaging access, correspondent account, liquidity and settlement.

claims.Claim: CRS, CARF and FATCA create defined reporting and exchange duties, not a universal public or real-time database of every person's financial activity.
claims.Review rule: Record reportable account, taxpayer nexus, exchange agreement, period and recipient authority.

claims.Claim: World Bank debarment is an administrative procurement sanction and may propagate through cross-debarment; it is not necessarily a criminal conviction or universal business ban.
claims.Review rule: Record decision tier, sanction period, release conditions and participating institutions.

claims.Claim: Seizure, blocking and forfeiture are different legal states; final forfeiture requires a separate legal process and may generate victim or third-party claims.
claims.Review rule: Track custody, title, court order, claim status and distribution separately.

claims.Claim: Appointment to an advisory council establishes formal access and a consultative role; it does not establish binding authority, policy adoption or control of government.
claims.Review rule: Record appointment, term, ethics status, advice produced and actual policy adoption separately.

claims.Claim: Lobbying expenditure establishes paid advocacy on disclosed issues, not successful persuasion, corruption or control of an official.
claims.Review rule: Link lobbying to outcomes only through meetings, drafts, timing, correspondence and decision evidence.

claims.Claim: Super PAC contributions and independent expenditures establish political-finance relationships, but do not by themselves establish candidate coordination, quid pro quo or electoral causation.
claims.Review rule: Preserve donor, committee, vendor, communication, beneficiary and coordination evidence separately.

claims.Claim: Philanthropic grants allocate resources and agenda capacity; they do not automatically purchase research conclusions or transfer public authority to the donor.
claims.Review rule: Record grant restrictions, governance rights, outputs, recipient independence and renewal dependence.

claims.Claim: Think-tank funding can shape institutional capacity and policy supply, but donor support is not proof that a donor authored or controlled a specific conclusion.
claims.Review rule: Trace project funding, author independence, citations, appointments and policy uptake.

claims.Claim: Media ownership and voting control create governance power, but do not establish owner direction of every article, broadcast or journalistic conclusion.
claims.Review rule: Separate voting rights, executive authority, budget, editorial constitution and item-level intervention.

claims.Claim: Bill Gates and Foundation personnel had repeated documented meetings with Epstein, and the Foundation review found vetting failures; the review found no Foundation payment to Epstein or evidence of participation in or knowledge of his crimes.
claims.Review rule: State both the documented relationship and the review's evidentiary limits.

claims.Claim: Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein were documented social acquaintances; describing Epstein as Trump's proven 'best friend' or inferring participation in Epstein's crimes exceeds the available evidence.
claims.Review rule: Use dated events, travel and direct quotations; quarantine superlative relationship claims and guilt by association.

claims.Claim: A person's name, planned meeting or reference in the DOJ Epstein Library is not evidence of wrongdoing or proof that a meeting occurred.
claims.Review rule: Classify each record by source, role, occurrence, corroboration and alleged conduct.

claims.Claim: Elite networks are real channels of access, but network density does not prove a unified command structure; authority must be traced through offices, votes, contracts, money, appointments and decisions.
claims.Review rule: Require a documented conversion mechanism for each claimed exercise of power.

claims.Claim: The strongest political-power map separates capital, access, expertise, narrative reach and legal authority rather than treating prominence as one undifferentiated form of control.
claims.Review rule: Score each edge by the exact power dimension and the institution capable of acting.

claims.Claim: A complaint, defence or arbitration request begins a legal process; it does not establish the truth of allegations, liability or entitlement to a remedy.
claims.Review rule: Track filing, jurisdiction, interim orders, merits findings and final judgment separately.

claims.Claim: A judicial or arbitral interim order is not the same as a final judgment or award, and a final award is not the same as successful collection.
claims.Review rule: Record procedural state, appeal or annulment status, enforcement forum and asset recovery.

claims.Claim: Arbitration institutions administer disputes and appointments; the case-specific tribunal ordinarily decides the merits.
claims.Review rule: Separate registry, institutional court, tribunal, national court and enforcement actor.

claims.Claim: Third-party litigation funding provides nonrecourse capital and a contingent return; it does not automatically transfer claim ownership or litigation control.
claims.Review rule: Review each funding contract for economics, control rights, privilege and disclosure.

claims.Claim: A bankruptcy petition creates a collective legal process; it does not predetermine liquidation, creditor recovery, plan confirmation or equity cancellation.
claims.Review rule: Track filing, stay, financing, sale, plan, conversion, dismissal and distribution as separate states.

claims.Claim: DIP financing and secured-creditor collateral rights create priority and bargaining leverage, but do not automatically confer ownership of the debtor.
claims.Review rule: Record liens, covenants, milestones, adequate protection, remedies and court orders.

claims.Claim: A patent grant is a territorial right to exclude, not proof of commercial value, freedom to operate, infringement or immunity from later invalidation.
claims.Review rule: Separate application, grant, ownership, licence, challenge, infringement and remedy.

claims.Claim: A PCT application preserves international filing options but does not create a unitary worldwide patent.
claims.Review rule: Record national-phase entry and each office's decision separately.

claims.Claim: A USITC exclusion order can block covered imports at the U.S. border; it is not a damages judgment, patent transfer or worldwide market prohibition.
claims.Review rule: Track investigation, violation finding, order scope, presidential review and CBP enforcement.

claims.Claim: Legal power is best represented as a sequence of claim, jurisdiction, interim control, final decision, review and enforcement—not as a binary label that a party 'won.'
claims.Review rule: Require exact procedural state and enforcing institution for every legal-power claim.

claims.Claim: Insurance transfers only contractually defined losses; a premium does not buy protection against every possible loss or guarantee immediate full payment.
claims.Review rule: Record insured peril, exclusions, deductible, limit, claims state and payment separately.

claims.Claim: Reinsurance and retrocession move defined underwriting risk among insurers; they do not eliminate aggregate catastrophe risk or reinsurer credit risk.
claims.Review rule: Trace treaty layer, attachment, limit, collateral, ultimate risk bearer and collectability.

claims.Claim: Lloyd's is a marketplace with syndicates, member capital and central resources—not one ordinary insurance company or an unlimited guarantee fund.
claims.Review rule: Separate Corporation, Council, managing agent, syndicate, member and Central Fund.

claims.Claim: Catastrophe bonds transfer specified insurance risk to investors whose principal can be reduced after a contractual trigger; they are not ordinary risk-free bonds.
claims.Review rule: Record sponsor, vehicle, trigger, attachment, exhaustion, collateral and principal outcome.

claims.Claim: The catastrophe protection gap is the difference between economic loss and insured recovery; it is not borne by one actor and may be redistributed through savings, credit and public aid.
claims.Review rule: Track household, corporate, insurer, lender and government loss incidence.

claims.Claim: Derivative notional is a reference amount, not the value at risk or the loss if counterparties fail; exposure depends on market value, netting, collateral and liquidity.
claims.Review rule: Report gross notional, gross market value, net exposure and collateral separately.

claims.Claim: A derivative may be used for hedging, market making, arbitrage or speculation; the instrument label alone does not reveal the user's economic purpose.
claims.Review rule: Link position to the underlying exposure, hedge ratio, accounting and portfolio context.

claims.Claim: Central clearing reduces and standardises bilateral counterparty risk but concentrates operational, liquidity and default risk in the CCP.
claims.Review rule: Measure concentration, margin, member resources, recovery and resolution plans.

claims.Claim: Initial margin is collateral for potential future exposure, not a premium or final loss payment; variation margin settles current exposure and can generate acute liquidity demand.
claims.Review rule: Separate ownership, custody, reuse, haircut, call timing and return of collateral.

claims.Claim: A CCP default waterfall applies resources in a defined sequence; mutualised funds and assessments are contingent tail-loss mechanisms, not ordinary operating capital or government guarantees.
claims.Review rule: Record product silo, defaulter resources, CCP skin, fund, assessments and resolution.

claims.Claim: CCP resolution planning does not promise lossless continuity or a taxpayer bailout; it establishes powers and resources for an orderly response after private recovery is inadequate.
claims.Review rule: Track national implementation, funding source, creditor hierarchy and continuity outcome.

claims.Claim: A bank deposit is a liability of the bank and a claim of the depositor; it is not a segregated ownership interest in specific cash, reserves or loans.
claims.Review rule: Record issuing bank, ownership category, insurance status, maturity and settlement route.

claims.Claim: Bank lending can create deposits, but banks are constrained by capital, liquidity, credit risk, profitability, regulation and the need to settle deposit outflows.
claims.Review rule: Do not replace balance-sheet constraints with a fixed reserve-multiplier story or an unlimited-money claim.

claims.Claim: FDIC insurance protects eligible depositors up to statutory limits; it does not protect shareholders, mutual funds, securities, crypto assets or every uninsured deposit.
claims.Review rule: Classify account ownership category and insured versus uninsured balance.

claims.Claim: The Deposit Insurance Fund is an industry-funded collective reserve backed by the U.S. government; its reserve ratio is not cash equal to all insured or total deposits.
claims.Review rule: Report fund balance, insured deposits, reserve ratio, borrowing capacity and projected losses separately.

claims.Claim: Central-bank lending and FHLBank advances provide collateralised liquidity; they do not erase credit losses, restore insolvent equity or transfer asset ownership without enforcement.
claims.Review rule: Separate borrower eligibility, collateral value, haircut, maturity, priority and repayment.

claims.Claim: Repo is economically collateralised borrowing even when documented as a sale and repurchase; collateral transfer does not by itself mean the lender owns the borrower's economic position permanently.
claims.Review rule: Record legal title, beneficial exposure, haircut, margin, maturity and default rights.

claims.Claim: Money market fund shares are investment-company securities, not FDIC-insured deposits; stable NAV conventions and sponsor reputation do not create a public guarantee.
claims.Review rule: Record fund type, NAV, liquidity assets, fee framework, sponsor support and portfolio exposure.

claims.Claim: FICC central clearing reduces bilateral gross exposures and settlement obligations but concentrates margin, operational and default risk in a private regulated CCP.
claims.Review rule: Measure gross and net positions, margin, membership, default resources and access model.

claims.Claim: A sponsored repo participant is not a direct FICC member; the sponsoring member remains a separate credit, operational and legal intermediary.
claims.Review rule: Record sponsor, sponsored entity, margin responsibility and default obligations.

claims.Claim: Securities lending transfers temporary possession and may transfer legal title under contract, but it does not necessarily transfer the lender's long-term economic exposure or all governance rights.
claims.Review rule: Record collateral, manufactured payments, voting, recall, term and default rights.

claims.Claim: TLAC and bail-in are designed to impose systemic-bank losses on eligible private creditors and create recapitalisation capacity; insured deposits are not ordinary TLAC instruments.
claims.Review rule: Record resolution entity, eligible liability, creditor location, conversion mechanism and public liquidity support.

claims.Claim: Liquidity and solvency are different: a bank can possess valuable long-term assets yet lack immediate cash, or obtain central-bank liquidity while still having insufficient economic capital.
claims.Review rule: Track market value, cash-flow timing, collateral lending value, capital and loss recognition separately.

claims.Claim: A defined-benefit pension promise and a defined-contribution account are different claims: the first is formula-based and sponsor-funded, while the second is an account whose value depends on contributions, fees and investment returns.
claims.Review rule: Record plan type, sponsor obligation, vesting, account balance and investment-risk bearer separately.

claims.Claim: PBGC insurance protects qualifying private-sector defined-benefit claims up to legal limits; it does not guarantee every retirement plan, every benefit or the sponsoring employer.
claims.Review rule: Record programme, plan coverage, benefit limit, termination date and recovery source.

claims.Claim: ERISA fiduciary status creates duties of loyalty, prudence, diversification and reasonable expense; it does not guarantee positive returns.
claims.Review rule: Separate decision process and duty from ex-post investment outcome.

claims.Claim: A target-date fund’s target year describes an asset-allocation design, not a guarantee of principal, income adequacy or retirement readiness.
claims.Review rule: Record glide path, underlying holdings, fees, assumptions and participant circumstances.

claims.Claim: A mutual-fund or ETF shareholder owns a fund interest, not direct title to each security in the portfolio.
claims.Review rule: Separate fund legal ownership, shareholder beneficial claim and adviser authority.

claims.Claim: An investment adviser manages assets under mandate but does not ordinarily become the beneficial owner of those assets.
claims.Review rule: Record client, fund, custodian, adviser and voting authority separately.

claims.Claim: ETF authorised participants connect primary and secondary markets through creation and redemption, but they are not unconditional guarantors that market price will equal NAV in every condition.
claims.Review rule: Track AP agreements, baskets, spreads, underlying-market status and creation-redemption activity.

claims.Claim: Cede & Co. record ownership, DTC participant positions and ultimate beneficial ownership are distinct layers in the securities-holding chain.
claims.Review rule: Trace issuer register, DTC account, intermediary books and end-investor rights separately.

claims.Claim: Index inclusion or exclusion follows a methodology and governance process; it is not a permanent status, credit opinion or universal endorsement of the constituent.
claims.Review rule: Record methodology, committee discretion, consultation, effective date and tracked assets.

claims.Claim: Delegated proxy voting creates recurring governance influence but does not transfer beneficial ownership or guarantee control of a corporate vote.
claims.Review rule: Record voting authority, policy, vote, securities-lending status and client mandate.

claims.Claim: A private-fund capital commitment is a contingent obligation, not immediate invested cash, a liquid security or a guaranteed return.
claims.Review rule: Separate commitment, called capital, NAV, distributions and unfunded amount.

claims.Claim: Subscription and NAV facilities can improve timing flexibility but add leverage, collateral priority and valuation dependence at the fund level.
claims.Review rule: Record borrower, collateral base, covenants, draw, maturity and repayment source.

claims.Claim: Private credit is non-bank lending, but banks can remain connected through subscription lines, NAV loans, warehouse facilities and commitments to funds and BDCs.
claims.Review rule: Map both final corporate loan and upstream fund financing.

claims.Claim: A CLO is a tranched securitisation of a loan portfolio; its senior rating, overcollateralisation tests and waterfall redistribute risk but do not eliminate borrower credit losses.
claims.Review rule: Record collateral, tranche, rating, test, manager, trustee and final loss allocation.

claims.Claim: The 2026 Department of Labor alternative-asset proposal is a proposed fiduciary safe-harbour framework, not a final mandate requiring 401(k) plans to add private assets.
claims.Review rule: Maintain proposal status, final-rule outcome, litigation and actual plan adoption separately.

claims.Claim: A registered offering authorises public distribution subject to disclosure and liability rules; it does not guarantee that the issuer raises the maximum amount or that the security performs well.
claims.Review rule: Separate registration, pricing, allocation, proceeds and secondary-market performance.

claims.Claim: An underwriting syndicate can assume contractual distribution risk and allocate securities, but participation does not establish permanent ownership or control of the issuer.
claims.Review rule: Record underwriting form, syndicate role, allocation, stabilization and post-offering holdings separately.

claims.Claim: Exchange listing is permission to trade under exchange standards, not an endorsement of investment quality or a guarantee against delisting.
claims.Review rule: Keep eligibility, continued listing, trading and issuer value distinct.

claims.Claim: Payment for order flow is a documented routing-compensation arrangement and a potential conflict; its existence alone does not prove inferior execution or a best-execution violation.
claims.Review rule: Compare execution outcomes, routing alternatives, disclosures and supervision before inferring harm.

claims.Claim: A large market maker may internalise substantial order flow and provide liquidity, but scale does not grant unilateral authority to determine a security's market price.
claims.Review rule: Measure venue share, inventory, spreads, capital, competition and arbitrage constraints.

claims.Claim: An ATS is a regulated broker-dealer trading system operating under Regulation ATS; 'dark pool' does not mean unregulated or invisible to regulators.
claims.Review rule: Distinguish pre-trade display, regulatory reporting, subscriber disclosure and public transparency.

claims.Claim: The SIP consolidated feed and exchange proprietary feeds are distinct products with different depth and latency; neither should be treated as the complete market by itself.
claims.Review rule: Map exact content, timestamps, access cost and user population.

claims.Claim: CAT creates regulatory order-lifecycle visibility but is not a public database of named investors, and current privacy and governance questions remain under active review.
claims.Review rule: Track data fields, regulator access, retention, security, governance and exemptions.

claims.Claim: NSCC netting and DTC book-entry settlement reduce movements and counterparty complexity; they do not eliminate member default, liquidity or operational risk.
claims.Review rule: Record novation, net positions, margin, settlement bank and loss-allocation layers.

claims.Claim: T+1 shortens the standard settlement interval but does not eliminate failed trades, funding needs, securities borrowing or corporate-action processing risk.
claims.Review rule: Measure fails, affirmation timing, liquidity demand and operational exceptions.

claims.Claim: Cede & Co. and DTC participant positions represent record and intermediary ownership states; they do not establish that Cede or DTC is the ultimate beneficial owner of deposited securities.
claims.Review rule: Maintain issuer register, DTC participant, broker, custodian and beneficial-owner layers separately.

claims.Claim: A fail to deliver or reported short position does not by itself prove illegal naked short selling or manipulation.
claims.Review rule: Require transaction, locate, borrow, close-out, intent and enforcement evidence.

claims.Claim: Rule 10c-1a and Form SHO transparency regimes have extended compliance schedules; final operational data availability must not be backdated or assumed.
claims.Review rule: Track effective date, exemption period, first reporting date and public dissemination separately.

claims.Claim: A proxy adviser supplies research and recommendations; the adviser does not cast the client's vote unless separately authorised through a voting service or client policy.
claims.Review rule: Separate research, custom policy, automated execution, override and final vote.

claims.Claim: A beneficial owner in street name is not ordinarily the registered shareholder on the issuer ledger and may need a voting-instruction form or legal proxy to act directly at a meeting.
claims.Review rule: Record record holder, intermediary, beneficial owner, OBO/NOBO status and voting authority.

claims.Claim: Universal proxy cards expand candidate choice in contested elections; they do not guarantee election of dissident nominees or transfer board authority before the vote.
claims.Review rule: Separate nomination, solicitation, card format, vote count and legal seating.

claims.Claim: Schedule 13D or 13G reports a threshold ownership state under defined rules; filing does not itself prove control, collusion, activism or illegality.
claims.Review rule: Review filer category, voting and investment power, derivatives, group evidence and stated purpose.

claims.Claim: A Rule 14a-8 shareholder proposal can obtain agenda access but may be non-binding, excluded under applicable rules or rejected by shareholders.
claims.Review rule: Track eligibility, exclusion basis, ballot status, vote and board implementation.

claims.Claim: 24X exchange approval and operation must be separated from approval and implementation of every future overnight-trading phase, SIP change or clearing extension.
claims.Review rule: Maintain exchange registration, operating session, exemptive relief and infrastructure readiness as separate states.

claims.Claim: Treasury auctions use a single-price allocation process; a primary dealer's bid contributes to price discovery but does not unilaterally set the auction yield.
claims.Review rule: Record announcement, bid type, bidder class, stop-out result and award separately.

claims.Claim: Primary-dealer status is a New York Fed business counterparty relationship with operational expectations, not regulatory approval or endorsement of the firm's other activities.
claims.Review rule: Keep counterparty, supervision, capital, auction and client roles separate.

claims.Claim: TBAC provides private-sector advice to Treasury; its recommendations do not constitute final sovereign debt-management authority or prove private capture.
claims.Review rule: Track questions, recommendation, Treasury decision and implementation independently.

claims.Claim: The Treasury yield curve is a benchmark term structure, not proof that Treasury securities are free of duration, inflation, liquidity, custody or political risk.
claims.Review rule: Specify the risk dimension whenever using the term risk-free.

claims.Claim: SOMA Treasury purchases and rollovers implement monetary policy and portfolio management; they do not directly identify which fiscal expenditure was financed.
claims.Review rule: Separate primary issuance, secondary purchase, rollover and reserve effects.

claims.Claim: A corporate bond is a creditor claim governed by contract; it does not ordinarily confer residual ownership or general voting rights equivalent to common equity.
claims.Review rule: Record principal, coupon, maturity, priority, security, guarantee and voting rights.

claims.Claim: An NRSRO registration establishes regulatory status, not SEC endorsement of a rating, guaranteed repayment or permanent accuracy.
claims.Review rule: Preserve rating agency, methodology, committee, surveillance and realised outcome separately.

claims.Claim: A credit rating is an opinion about creditworthiness under a methodology; it is not a deterministic default probability or substitute for investor analysis.
claims.Review rule: Record rating date, instrument, outlook, methodology, paid status and later transition.

claims.Claim: An indenture trustee represents bondholders under the contract but may have limited pre-default duties and does not manage the investment portfolio for holders.
claims.Review rule: Map pre-default, post-default, direction, indemnity and conflict provisions.

claims.Claim: The existence of covenants does not establish strong creditor protection; covenant scope, exceptions, thresholds and enforcement rights must be read from the exact indenture.
claims.Review rule: Do not grade covenant quality from the instrument label alone.

claims.Claim: DTC eligibility and a CUSIP make a bond operationally identifiable and settleable; they do not establish credit quality, investor suitability or beneficial ownership.
claims.Review rule: Separate eligibility, global-note custody, participant position and ultimate holder.

claims.Claim: TRACE reporting creates transaction transparency but does not prove that a customer received best execution or that every bond has a continuously observable market price.
claims.Review rule: Combine TRACE with dealer capacity, size, timing, inventory and customer context.

claims.Claim: The current general TRACE reporting outer limit remains 15 minutes for corporate bonds; the previously approved shorter framework has no effective date in its existing form.
claims.Review rule: Track new FINRA filings and SEC approval before changing the effective rule state.

claims.Claim: Retail bond mark-up disclosure applies under defined same-day principal-trade conditions and does not disclose every element of dealer economics on every bond transaction.
claims.Review rule: Record customer type, capacity, offsetting trade, prevailing market price and disclosure trigger.

claims.Claim: Corporate bonds trade predominantly over the counter, so two customers can receive different executable prices without that difference alone proving misconduct.
claims.Review rule: Test fair pricing against size, time, liquidity, dealer capacity and market evidence.

claims.Claim: A Rule 144A bond is an exempt institutional security and should not be represented as an SEC-registered public bond merely because TRACE later reports secondary trades.
claims.Review rule: Maintain issuance exemption, purchaser status, resale and public reporting separately.

claims.Claim: A bond fund or ETF offers a redeemable or tradable fund claim, not guaranteed immediate sale of every underlying corporate bond at carrying value.
claims.Review rule: Measure cash, dealer bids, swing pricing, ETF baskets and redemption tools.

claims.Claim: A consent solicitation can amend or remove bondholder protections when the contractual voting threshold is met; it does not establish unanimous holder agreement.
claims.Review rule: Record eligible principal, votes, consent fee, threshold and non-consenting treatment.

claims.Claim: A distressed creditor can acquire restructuring leverage through priority and blocking positions, but debt ownership does not automatically equal board control or ownership of the company.
claims.Review rule: Trace default, threshold, bankruptcy class, plan treatment and resulting ownership separately.

claims.Claim: A tender or exchange offer can be proactive liability management rather than evidence that the issuer has defaulted or is insolvent.
claims.Review rule: Record stated purpose, funding source, participation, accounting effect and later credit outcome.

claims.Claim: The BIS 2025 survey measures average daily OTC FX turnover of $9.6 trillion in April 2025; turnover is gross market activity, not net cross-border capital transfer or global income.
claims.Review rule: Keep turnover, notional exposure, settlement value and net funding separate.

claims.Claim: The U.S. dollar appeared on one side of 89 percent of FX trades in the 2025 BIS survey; this establishes market centrality, not permanent dominance or U.S. control of every offshore dollar liability.
claims.Review rule: Distinguish currency use, issuer authority, bank liability creation and settlement access.

claims.Claim: The FX Global Code is a voluntary global good-practice code and Statement of Commitment mechanism; it does not replace law or prove full compliance by a signatory.
claims.Review rule: Record signatory, date, business scope, governance and later conduct separately.

claims.Claim: An FX benchmark fixing is a methodology-based reference rate, not the only market price or guaranteed best execution for every fixing order.
claims.Review rule: Record window, inputs, order type, execution method and tracking error.

claims.Claim: A prime broker supplies credit intermediation and settlement support; it does not automatically choose the client's executing dealer or control the market price.
claims.Review rule: Separate client instruction, executing dealer, prime broker, give-up and final settlement.

claims.Claim: SWIFT provides secure financial messaging and standards; a SWIFT message is not itself the transfer or final settlement of central-bank or commercial-bank money.
claims.Review rule: Trace the message, correspondent account debit, payment system and beneficiary credit independently.

claims.Claim: A nostro account is the respondent bank's asset and the correspondent bank's liability; it is not automatically a segregated account owned directly by the respondent's customers.
claims.Review rule: Map legal account holder, customer entitlement, currency, jurisdiction and insolvency treatment.

claims.Claim: CHIPS clears and settles high-value U.S.-dollar payments with liquidity-saving mechanisms; it is not a federal guarantee of every participant obligation.
claims.Review rule: Record participant funding, finality, loss allocation and settlement-bank layers.

claims.Claim: CLS payment-versus-payment settlement eliminates principal settlement risk for eligible matched instructions that settle, but it does not remove market, replacement-cost, liquidity, operational or counterparty risk outside the settlement process.
claims.Review rule: Record eligibility, currency, member, funding, match, rescission and final settlement.

claims.Claim: CLS settles 18 eligible currencies and provides third-party access through settlement members; this does not establish PvP coverage of all currencies, counterparties or global FX turnover.
claims.Review rule: Measure uncovered currencies, products and bilateral settlement methods.

claims.Claim: COFER reports aggregate official reserve composition and does not publish country-by-country currency allocations for confidential reporters.
claims.Review rule: Do not infer an individual country's portfolio from global aggregates.

claims.Claim: Changes in reported reserve-currency shares can reflect exchange-rate valuation effects as well as purchases and sales.
claims.Review rule: Decompose valuation, transaction and reporting changes before inferring policy.

claims.Claim: Offshore dollar deposits are commercial-bank liabilities created outside the United States; they are not Federal Reserve reserve balances and are not automatically protected by the U.S. government.
claims.Review rule: Separate currency denomination, booking location, issuer and backstop access.

claims.Claim: Federal Reserve swap-line drawings create a claim on a foreign central bank; foreign commercial banks receive dollars from their home central bank rather than borrowing directly from the Federal Reserve.
claims.Review rule: Map Federal Reserve counterparty, local auction, collateral and domestic credit risk.

claims.Claim: The FIMA repo facility provides approved foreign official institutions with temporary dollars against Treasury collateral; it is not an unsecured grant or permanent monetisation of foreign losses.
claims.Review rule: Record counterparty approval, collateral, term, rate, limit and repayment.

claims.Claim: The SDR is an international reserve asset and IMF unit of account based on a five-currency basket; it is not a circulating world currency or an ordinary fiscal grant.
claims.Review rule: Separate allocation, holdings, interest, exchange and domestic budget use.

claims.Claim: IMF quotas influence voting power, financing contributions, normal access references and general SDR allocation shares; they do not give equal votes to all member states.
claims.Review rule: Record quota, basic votes, constituency, Board vote and access decision.

claims.Claim: IMF conditionality is linked to programme objectives and safeguarding resources; describing it as purely unilateral coercion or purely voluntary equal bargaining both omit the negotiated but asymmetric institutional setting.
claims.Review rule: Record financing need, alternatives, domestic authorship, negotiations, Board approval and implementation.

claims.Claim: An IMF staff-level agreement or completed mission is not the same as Executive Board approval or release of a financing tranche.
claims.Review rule: Maintain mission, staff agreement, Board paper, Board decision and disbursement as separate states.

claims.Claim: A debt sustainability analysis is a scenario-based official assessment used in financing and debt-limit design; it is not a deterministic forecast or legal finding that debt will or will not be repaid.
claims.Review rule: Preserve assumptions, shocks, thresholds, judgement and later forecast error.

claims.Claim: Paris Club treatments can reschedule or reduce official bilateral debt service, but the Paris Club does not automatically bind non-member official creditors or private bondholders.
claims.Review rule: Record creditor perimeter, cut-off date, eligible claims and implementation agreements.

claims.Claim: Comparable treatment seeks burden sharing across creditor groups; it does not require mechanically identical net-present-value treatment for instruments with different legal and economic characteristics.
claims.Review rule: Document methodology, creditor class, timing and enforcement.

claims.Claim: Collective action clauses permit specified majorities to amend sovereign bond terms, but they do not guarantee rapid, litigation-free or comprehensive restructuring across every debt instrument.
claims.Review rule: Track series coverage, aggregation, thresholds, disenfranchisement and governing law.

claims.Claim: TIC data provide official cross-border positions and flows for the United States but do not fully identify ultimate beneficial ownership or every offshore chain.
claims.Review rule: Preserve residence, nationality, custodian, issuer and beneficial-owner distinctions.

claims.Claim: World Bank IPF, DPF and PforR are distinct financing instruments: project expenditures, policy and institutional actions, and verified programme results must not be collapsed into one generic loan category.
claims.Review rule: Preserve financing instrument, disbursement basis, borrower and project or programme object.

claims.Claim: A World Bank or MDB guarantee is a contingent risk-transfer instrument, not automatically a cash grant or funded reserve equal to its face amount.
claims.Review rule: Record covered event, beneficiary, sovereign counter-guarantee, maximum exposure, claim and recovery separately.

claims.Claim: IFC B-loan and similar A/B structures allow private lenders to participate while the MDB remains lender of record; participants still bear the underlying credit risk and are not simply guaranteed by IFC.
claims.Review rule: Separate lender of record, participant funding, direct claim, preferred treatment and guarantee coverage.

claims.Claim: Reported private-capital mobilisation is a methodology-defined associated financing amount, not proof that every dollar would have been absent without MDB or DFI participation.
claims.Review rule: Maintain direct mobilisation, indirect mobilisation, cofinancing and causal additionality as separate fields.

claims.Claim: Blended finance can alter rank, price, tenor, security or loss absorption; it is not costless capital and may create subsidy, competition and selection concerns.
claims.Review rule: Record concessional provider, instrument, subsidy, first-loss position, beneficiaries and counterfactual.

claims.Claim: MIGA political-risk insurance covers defined non-commercial risks under a guarantee contract; it does not insure ordinary commercial underperformance or every government-related event.
claims.Review rule: Map peril, waiting period, exclusions, compensation, subrogation and recovery.

claims.Claim: Non-honoring coverage and breach-of-contract coverage are different legal pathways: one centres on specified payment failure and the other can require a dispute and unhonoured award under product terms.
claims.Review rule: Do not collapse government nonpayment, contractual breach, arbitration and claim payment.

claims.Claim: EXIM and other ECAs support exports through direct loans, guarantees, insurance and working-capital products; official support can advance national trade and strategic objectives rather than representing neutral private-market allocation.
claims.Review rule: Record exporter eligibility, domestic content, foreign buyer, lender, support type and public risk.

claims.Claim: The January 2026 OECD Arrangement disciplines financing terms among participating official export-credit providers; it does not bind all countries or private finance.
claims.Review rule: Record participant status, sector understanding, repayment term, premium and tied-aid rules.

claims.Claim: A project SPV ring-fences contracts and cash flows but does not make the project economically independent of sponsors, government, contractors, offtakers or public infrastructure.
claims.Review rule: Map guarantees, shared services, sponsor support, public obligations and insolvency links.

claims.Claim: Limited-recourse project finance is not zero recourse: sponsors, contractors, offtakers, governments and insurers can retain substantial contractual exposure.
claims.Review rule: Record each support contract and the conditions under which recourse becomes available.

claims.Claim: An offtake or take-or-pay contract improves revenue predictability but does not eliminate buyer credit risk, force majeure, termination, curtailment or political intervention.
claims.Review rule: Record buyer, volume, price, indexation, security, exceptions and termination rights.

claims.Claim: Availability-payment PPPs transfer less demand risk to the private party than user-fee concessions and create long-term public payment obligations linked to performance.
claims.Review rule: Separate demand risk, performance deductions, appropriation, inflation indexation and termination exposure.

claims.Claim: A PPP or concession is not equivalent to permanent privatisation: ownership, control, revenue rights and handback obligations depend on the contract and law.
claims.Review rule: Record asset title, concession term, operating rights, tariff authority and handback.

claims.Claim: Lender step-in rights can convert creditor exposure into temporary operational influence after default; they do not grant ordinary day-to-day ownership or unrestricted permanent control.
claims.Review rule: Record trigger, notice, cure, substitution, approval, duration and exit.

claims.Claim: PPP termination payments can protect senior debt and project value while creating substantial contingent public liabilities; the payment formula must be separated by termination cause.
claims.Review rule: Record authority default, company default, force majeure, public-interest termination and debt/equity treatment.

claims.Claim: Viability-gap funding can reduce tariffs or financing needs, but a subsidy does not by itself establish value for money, additionality or equitable benefit distribution.
claims.Review rule: Compare public-sector comparator, affordability, competition, subsidy incidence and outcomes.

claims.Claim: Equator Principles and MDB environmental-social standards create financing conditions and monitoring requirements; they are not government regulation and do not prove absence of harm.
claims.Review rule: Record applicable standard, categorisation, action plan, consultation, monitoring, grievance and remedy.

claims.Claim: Affected communities can use project grievance and MDB accountability mechanisms, but access, independence, remedy and implementation authority differ across mechanisms.
claims.Review rule: Preserve project grievance, ombudsman, compliance review, judicial and political channels separately.

claims.Claim: MDB procurement approval or no-objection is not proof that a contractor is the beneficial owner, cheapest lifecycle provider or politically independent.
claims.Review rule: Record bidding consortium, subcontractors, beneficial owners, evaluation, complaint and contract modification.

claims.Claim: Sovereign guarantees, availability payments and termination clauses can move project risk onto public balance sheets even when initial borrowing is legally located in a private SPV.
claims.Review rule: Build a fiscal-risk ledger rather than relying on headline public-debt accounting.

claims.Claim: MDB participation may improve standards, tenor, confidence and creditor coordination, but it does not guarantee project success, repayment or beneficial social outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Measure realised cost, service, repayment, additionality, distribution and safeguards.

claims.Claim: Preferred-creditor treatment is an institutional practice and expectation rather than a single universal statutory priority applicable identically to all MDB claims.
claims.Review rule: Record institution, borrower, instrument, restructuring episode and actual payment treatment.

claims.Claim: Development finance can serve development and strategic state interests simultaneously; strategic alignment is not by itself proof of corruption, command or absence of public benefit.
claims.Review rule: Separate mandate, eligibility, geopolitical objective, procurement, development result and distribution.

claims.Claim: Private-fund assets under management, committed capital, invested capital, net asset value and sponsor ownership are distinct measures and legal objects.
claims.Review rule: Never equate AUM with assets beneficially owned by the adviser.

claims.Claim: A limited partner commitment is an unfunded contractual obligation until called and contributed; it is not cash already held by the fund.
claims.Review rule: Track commitment, called capital, funded capital and remaining commitment separately.

claims.Claim: The general partner can exercise broad contractual management authority without beneficially owning the limited partners' contributed capital.
claims.Review rule: Separate legal control, economic interest, fiduciary duty and custody.

claims.Claim: Management fees are contractual compensation and expenses; they are not investment returns earned for limited partners.
claims.Review rule: Separate gross portfolio performance, fund expenses, fees and net return.

claims.Claim: Carried interest is a contingent partnership profit allocation and may be subject to hurdles, vesting, tax rules and clawback; it is not guaranteed annual compensation.
claims.Review rule: Track allocation, distribution, unrealised carry and final clawback separately.

claims.Claim: Subscription credit facilities can alter reported IRR through cash-flow timing without changing total asset proceeds or MOIC.
claims.Review rule: Recalculate unlevered and facility-adjusted investor cash flows.

claims.Claim: A private-fund NAV mark is a valuation estimate, not a realised transaction price or distributable cash amount.
claims.Review rule: Preserve valuation date, methodology, governance, later sale and cash distribution.

claims.Claim: A continuation-fund transaction is an affiliated transfer that can provide liquidity and extend ownership; it is not automatically equivalent to an arm's-length third-party sale.
claims.Review rule: Record process, adviser, valuation, LPAC consent, buyer competition and roll/sell elections.

claims.Claim: Leveraged-buyout debt is an obligation of the acquisition or portfolio-company structure and is distinct from sponsor equity and limited guarantees.
claims.Review rule: Map borrower, guarantor, collateral, sponsor commitment and recourse separately.

claims.Claim: Limited recourse does not mean zero sponsor risk: sponsor equity, capped guarantees, reputation and future fundraising may remain exposed.
claims.Review rule: Identify each recourse channel and its cap.

claims.Claim: A portfolio-company board seat creates governance power but not a licence for a sponsor director to ignore duties owed under applicable corporate law.
claims.Review rule: Separate nomination rights, board vote, fiduciary duties and sponsor instructions.

claims.Claim: A dividend recapitalisation produces owner liquidity by increasing company debt; it is not itself evidence of operating improvement or realised final fund success.
claims.Review rule: Track debt increase, distribution, credit metrics and later company outcome.

claims.Claim: A signed or announced merger is not a completed acquisition; financing, shareholder, antitrust, foreign-investment and other closing conditions remain.
claims.Review rule: Maintain announcement, signing, approval, clearance, funding and closing states.

claims.Claim: A fairness opinion addresses a defined financial question and does not prove that a deal is legally fair, conflict-free or the highest attainable price.
claims.Review rule: Record scope, assumptions, compensation, committee process and alternative bids.

claims.Claim: Tendering shares is a holder election within an offer; it does not complete a back-end merger until statutory and contractual conditions are satisfied.
claims.Review rule: Separate tender, acceptance, payment, minimum condition and merger.

claims.Claim: A Delaware appraisal claim is a judicial fair-value process and does not guarantee a premium above the merger price.
claims.Review rule: Record standing, procedural compliance, valuation evidence and judgment.

claims.Claim: A de-SPAC transaction is a public-listing pathway with sponsor compensation, redemptions and financing effects; it is not identical to a traditional IPO.
claims.Review rule: Separate trust cash, redemptions, PIPEs, dilution, target disclosure and closing.

claims.Claim: A SAFE is a contractual future-equity instrument and does not ordinarily confer current common-stock voting rights before conversion.
claims.Review rule: Record conversion trigger, cap, discount, liquidation treatment and issued shares.

claims.Claim: Preferred stock is equity with contractual preferences; a liquidation preference is not a guaranteed creditor recovery when company value is insufficient.
claims.Review rule: Separate equity priority, debt status, participation and enterprise value.

claims.Claim: Protective provisions and board designation rights can create minority investor influence without ordinary day-to-day operational control.
claims.Review rule: Identify the exact veto list, vote threshold and board composition.

claims.Claim: The 2026 HSR size-of-transaction threshold is $133.9 million, but reportability depends on transaction structure, exemptions and other tests.
claims.Review rule: Use the thresholds effective at closing and analyse exemptions separately.

claims.Claim: Expiration or termination of an HSR waiting period does not provide permanent substantive immunity from antitrust challenge.
claims.Review rule: Separate premerger procedure, agency decision, court review and later conduct.

claims.Claim: The 2023 Merger Guidelines are non-binding agency guidance and do not replace statutes, judicial precedent or transaction-specific evidence.
claims.Review rule: Record the legal theory, evidence and forum for each enforcement action.

claims.Claim: CFIUS clearance or mitigation addresses covered national-security concerns and does not constitute general antitrust, securities or sectoral regulatory approval.
claims.Review rule: Maintain each sovereign approval gate separately.

claims.Claim: A multinational enterprise group can operate as one coordinated economic system while its subsidiaries remain separate legal persons with distinct assets, liabilities and tax residences.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal entity, branch, PE, parent and consolidated group separately.

claims.Claim: Legal ownership of an intangible does not by itself establish entitlement to all associated returns; actual DEMPE functions, funding and risk control must be analysed.
claims.Review rule: Record legal title, functions, risks, funding and contractual rights separately.

claims.Claim: An intercompany loan is both a financing claim and a controlled tax transaction; its legal principal, pricing, deductibility and economic debt capacity are separate questions.
claims.Review rule: Identify borrower, lender, currency, maturity, security, rate and interest-limitation treatment.

claims.Claim: A cash-pool balance is not automatically an equity contribution, bank deposit owned by the pool leader or risk-free treasury claim.
claims.Review rule: Track legal account ownership, sweep mechanics, guarantees and participant credit exposure.

claims.Claim: An intercompany guarantee may create a compensable benefit, but group membership and implicit support can already affect creditworthiness.
claims.Review rule: Separate explicit guarantee, implicit support and borrower standalone rating.

claims.Claim: A contract assigning risk to one affiliate does not establish that affiliate controls the risk or deserves the residual return if actual decision-making occurs elsewhere.
claims.Review rule: Compare written contract with conduct, people functions and financial capacity.

claims.Claim: Country-by-country reporting is designed for high-level risk assessment and does not mechanically determine arm's-length prices or prove tax avoidance.
claims.Review rule: Keep CbCR aggregates separate from transaction-level evidence.

claims.Claim: Public country-by-country reporting increases visibility but can aggregate jurisdictions and omit the transaction detail required for causal conclusions.
claims.Review rule: Record reporting scope, aggregation, currency and reconciliation limits.

claims.Claim: A tax treaty reduces or reallocates taxation only when residence, beneficial ownership, nexus and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
claims.Review rule: Do not infer treaty entitlement from incorporation or payment routing alone.

claims.Claim: A permanent establishment is a taxable nexus, not necessarily a separate legal entity, bank account or subsidiary.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal entity, branch operations and attributed tax profit separately.

claims.Claim: A principal purpose test can deny a treaty benefit but does not establish that every tax-motivated arrangement is unlawful or abusive.
claims.Review rule: Identify the benefit, purposes, object and purpose of treaty provisions.

claims.Claim: An advance pricing agreement provides prospective certainty for covered facts and methods; it is not immunity from audit of other transactions or changed facts.
claims.Review rule: Track scope, term, critical assumptions and rollback separately.

claims.Claim: Mutual agreement procedure is government-to-government treaty dispute resolution and does not guarantee that competent authorities will reach agreement.
claims.Review rule: Preserve request, admission, negotiation, agreement and implementation states.

claims.Claim: A DAC6 or other mandatory-disclosure filing is a risk signal, not a legal determination that the arrangement is abusive.
claims.Review rule: Separate hallmark-triggered disclosure from audit outcome.

claims.Claim: Hybrid mismatch, CFC and interest-limitation rules are distinct anti-BEPS mechanisms and should not be collapsed into one general anti-avoidance edge.
claims.Review rule: Record legal trigger and tax consequence for each rule separately.

claims.Claim: Economic-substance requirements can condition access to preferential treatment, but headcount or local expenditure alone does not establish where all value was created.
claims.Review rule: Track core functions, decision rights, employees, expenditure and assets.

claims.Claim: Transfer-pricing income-tax value and customs value are governed by related but non-identical legal frameworks and can create opposite revenue incentives.
claims.Review rule: Preserve tax adjustment, customs entry and post-import price adjustment separately.

claims.Claim: A deferred tax asset or liability is an accounting estimate of future tax consequences and is not current tax cash paid or refunded.
claims.Review rule: Separate current tax, deferred tax, uncertain positions and cash payments.

claims.Claim: Pillar Two computes jurisdictional effective tax rates under GloBE rules; it is not a universal entity-by-entity flat tax of exactly 15 percent.
claims.Review rule: Track scope, exclusions, QDMTT, IIR, UTPR, safe harbours and credits.

claims.Claim: A qualified domestic minimum top-up tax, income inclusion rule and undertaxed profits rule are ordered but legally separate top-up-tax mechanisms.
claims.Review rule: Identify collecting jurisdiction and legal basis for each amount.
