claims.Claim: The Subject to Tax Rule is a treaty-based source rule for specified intragroup payments and is distinct from the GloBE jurisdictional minimum-tax calculation.
claims.Review rule: Preserve payment-level source tax and group-level top-up tax separately.

claims.Claim: A tax incentive can still influence investment even when Pillar Two reduces its effective-rate benefit, because refundable credits, cash grants, substance and non-tax factors differ.
claims.Review rule: Model incentive legal form and GloBE treatment instead of assuming full neutralisation.

claims.Claim: A low-tax, holding or shell entity may be legally valid and own assets even when tax authorities challenge treaty entitlement, substance or transfer pricing.
claims.Review rule: Do not convert low substance into unsupported claims of legal nonexistence.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of multinational profit allocation combines legal ownership, contracts, people functions, financial accounts, tax filings, payment records and authority decisions.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation before asserting control or artificial profit shifting.

claims.Claim: Employment status depends on applicable law and facts; contract labels alone do not determine whether a worker is an employee or independent contractor.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A corporate group, staffing arrangement, franchise or subcontracting chain can divide formal employment from operational control without eliminating all shared responsibility.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Gross wages, base salary, overtime, tips, benefits, equity and net pay are distinct compensation objects.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A payroll record is evidence of reported hours and pay but does not by itself prove that all work time was captured or all deductions were lawful.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A pay gap is a risk and enforcement signal, not by itself proof of unlawful discrimination or equal-value comparability.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A collective bargaining agreement regulates employment conditions but does not make the union an owner of the enterprise or individual workers.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Union certification establishes representation for a bargaining unit; it does not establish unanimous worker support or permanent representation.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Exclusive representation creates a duty of fair representation but does not guarantee that every grievance will be pursued or succeed.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Works council information and consultation rights can delay, inform or reshape corporate decisions but are not automatically a veto.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Temporary agency and host employers can share safety and employment responsibilities; the agency payroll role does not erase host control.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Employer-sponsored immigration status can create material bargaining dependence but does not make the employer the owner of the migrant worker.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Worker-paid recruitment fees can create debt and coercive dependence even when migration and employment documents are formally valid.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Employment-eligibility verification establishes a compliance process, not permanent immigration status or worker suitability.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Occupational safety compliance, an audit or an inspection does not guarantee that a workplace is free from hazards.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A workers compensation or unemployment insurance claim is a benefit-eligibility process, not proof of employer fault or permanent income replacement.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: An employee benefit plan is legally and financially distinct from the employer operating assets, and plan fiduciary authority is not corporate ownership.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A retirement account balance or equity award is not the same as cash compensation received; vesting, market value, taxes and distribution conditions matter.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A non-compete or confidentiality covenant is not automatically enforceable and cannot be assumed to extinguish protected whistleblowing, organising or statutory rights.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: A strike or lockout is a collective economic-pressure mechanism, not proof that either party is legally or morally correct.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: An automated employment score or recommendation is not inherently neutral, valid or independently authoritative merely because a vendor produced it.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: The EU Platform Work Directive requires national transposition by 2 December 2026; employment-AI obligations must be dated because high-risk employment rules apply from 2 December 2027 under the current framework.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Platform account access can function as access to income but is not identical to employee status, ownership of the platform or guaranteed future work.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Human review of an automated employment decision is meaningful only when the reviewer has information, authority and time to change the outcome.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Lead-firm purchasing and delivery requirements can influence supplier labour conditions without making the lead firm the direct employer of every supplier worker.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: The strongest labour-power evidence combines employer identity, actual supervision, pay and time records, worker testimony, collective rights, safety data, algorithmic systems and remedy outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Preserve legal state, actual conduct, chronology, decision authority and final remedy separately.

claims.Claim: Health insurance coverage creates a contractual or statutory payment claim, not a guarantee that a provider is available, a service is authorised or the patient owes nothing.
claims.Review rule: Separate eligibility, benefit coverage, provider access, prior authorization and cost sharing.

claims.Claim: A provider directory entry does not prove current appointment availability, accurate network status or willingness to accept a specific patient.
claims.Review rule: Verify contract, directory date, scheduling and actual access.

claims.Claim: Prior authorization approval is not a clinical recommendation, guarantee of payment or finding that all claim conditions are satisfied.
claims.Review rule: Preserve clinical order, authorization, service delivery and claim adjudication separately.

claims.Claim: A paid healthcare claim proves an adjudicated payment state, not medical necessity, quality or correct coding.
claims.Review rule: Link claim, documentation, coding, coverage criteria and outcome.

claims.Claim: Hospital gross charge, negotiated rate, allowed amount, patient cost sharing and provider cost are separate financial objects.
claims.Review rule: Preserve every price and payment state separately.

claims.Claim: Hospital price-transparency publication increases legibility but does not by itself reveal the final patient bill or total episode cost.
claims.Review rule: Include insurance status, coding, ancillary services and adjudication.

claims.Claim: The No Surprises Act protects patients in defined encounters while leaving a separate provider-plan payment dispute.
claims.Review rule: Separate patient cost-sharing protection from provider reimbursement.

claims.Claim: An IDR determination selects a payment amount for a qualifying dispute; it does not establish clinical quality, network adequacy or the economic cost of care.
claims.Review rule: Record dispute eligibility, submissions, determination and payment.

claims.Claim: Medical debt can result from coverage gaps, cost sharing, billing error or denied assistance; the face amount does not establish final lawful liability.
claims.Review rule: Track claim, EOB, assistance, appeal, collection and settlement.

claims.Claim: Capitation and value-based payment transfer financial risk but do not transfer ownership of patients or eliminate professional duties.
claims.Review rule: Separate payment risk, clinical authority and patient rights.

claims.Claim: A drug formulary converts coverage policy into practical access, but preferred status is not proof that a product is clinically superior for every patient.
claims.Review rule: Record tier, restrictions, net price, evidence and individual response.

claims.Claim: A manufacturer rebate is a contractual payment and not by itself proof of unlawful steering, lower patient cost or higher total system cost.
claims.Review rule: Trace list price, rebate, plan payment, pharmacy reimbursement and patient cost.

claims.Claim: PBM affiliation with a pharmacy establishes common ownership, not automatic proof that every prescription was improperly steered or overpriced.
claims.Review rule: Identify formulary, network, channel policy, acquisition cost and alternative pharmacies.

claims.Claim: A Medicare maximum fair price applies within the statutory negotiation programme and is not a universal market price for every purchaser or transaction.
claims.Review rule: Record product, applicability year, programme and dispensing transaction.

claims.Claim: FDA approval establishes a regulatory benefit-risk decision for labelled use, not insurance coverage, affordability or superiority over every alternative.
claims.Review rule: Separate approval, label, comparative evidence, reimbursement and access.

claims.Claim: An Orange Book patent listing records submitted patent information but does not establish patent validity, infringement or the exact date of generic entry.
claims.Review rule: Track listed patent, certification, litigation, exclusivity and launch.

claims.Claim: Biosimilar approval establishes biosimilarity under the regulatory standard, not chemical identity, automatic interchangeability or market uptake.
claims.Review rule: Preserve biosimilar, interchangeable status, formulary and dispensing law.

claims.Claim: Accelerated approval provides earlier market access based on predictive evidence and leaves a confirmatory evidence obligation.
claims.Review rule: Track endpoint, approval condition, trial status and later regulatory action.

claims.Claim: Signed informed consent is evidence of a consent process, not proof of full understanding, voluntariness or absence of therapeutic misconception.
claims.Review rule: Review disclosure, discussion, capacity, language and recruitment conditions.

claims.Claim: IRB approval establishes institutional permission under research rules, not proof that a study is safe, scientifically valid or ethically conducted in practice.
claims.Review rule: Preserve protocol review, implementation, monitoring and adverse events.

claims.Claim: HIPAA applies to defined covered entities and business associates and should not be treated as a universal law governing every health-related dataset or application.
claims.Review rule: Identify actor status, information type and other applicable privacy law.

claims.Claim: A patient access right is not singular ownership of all health data, and custody, privacy, intellectual property and secondary-use permission remain distinct.
claims.Review rule: Record access, correction, export, custody and authorised uses separately.

claims.Claim: De-identified data may fall outside the HIPAA identifiability standard but are not guaranteed to be impossible to re-identify or unrestricted under every law.
claims.Review rule: Preserve method, residual risk, contract and other legal regimes.

claims.Claim: A nursing-home star rating or quality measure is an aggregate indicator, not a guarantee of the quality of a particular service or outcome for an individual.
claims.Review rule: Review component measures, date, staffing, inspection and resident needs.

claims.Claim: The strongest healthcare-power evidence combines coverage terms, network contracts, clinical records, prices, claims, drug-channel contracts, regulatory decisions, health-data logs and actual patient outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation before classifying access, denial, pricing abuse or clinical harm.

claims.Claim: Admission to an institution is distinct from enrolment, attendance, progression, completion and recognised qualification.
claims.Review rule: Preserve each state in the education lifecycle separately.

claims.Claim: A published tuition price is not the same as a student's net price, full cost of attendance or total debt-financed cost.
claims.Review rule: Record tuition, grants, living costs, borrowing and repayment separately.

claims.Claim: A grant award reduces price but does not establish that education is affordable or that the student can cover living costs.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile grant amount with complete cost of attendance and household resources.

claims.Claim: Student loan disbursement establishes a debt claim, not programme quality, completion, employability or positive financial return.
claims.Review rule: Track enrolment, completion, earnings, repayment and default separately.

claims.Claim: Accreditation is a periodic quality-assurance and eligibility process; it is not a government endorsement or guarantee of student outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Preserve accreditor status, government recognition, institutional eligibility and student outcomes separately.

claims.Claim: State authorisation, degree-awarding authority and accreditation are separate legal and institutional permissions.
claims.Review rule: Identify the authority, scope, period and consequence of each permission.

claims.Claim: Academic credits record workload or recognised study but do not by themselves prove mastery of the associated learning outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Preserve workload, assessment, grade and competence separately.

claims.Claim: A degree or micro-credential is an institutional attestation, not a complete measure of individual skill, productivity or character.
claims.Review rule: Record issuer, level, learning outcomes, assessment and recognition context.

claims.Claim: Qualification recognition can enable further study or employment consideration but does not automatically confer professional licensure or admission.
claims.Review rule: Separate recognition, admission, migration and occupational licensing.

claims.Claim: A university ranking is a methodology-dependent comparative product, not an objective total measure of educational or research quality.
claims.Review rule: Record indicators, weights, data sources, missing values and reputation inputs.

claims.Claim: A research grant funds a proposed programme of work; it does not establish the truth, social value or eventual reproducibility of the results.
claims.Review rule: Preserve proposal review, award, conduct, outputs and replication separately.

claims.Claim: Peer review is a gatekeeping and quality-control process, not a guarantee that a publication is correct or reproducible.
claims.Review rule: Track reviews, editorial decisions, conflicts, corrections and replication.

claims.Claim: Journal prestige and citation counts are signals shaped by field, network and visibility; they are not direct measures of truth or social value.
claims.Review rule: Normalise by field and preserve article-level evidence.

claims.Claim: Open access removes some reader barriers but does not mean publication, production, preservation or data stewardship is costless.
claims.Review rule: Track payer, licence, repository, preservation and access conditions.

claims.Claim: An article processing charge is a payment for a publishing service or model; it is not proof of acceptance, quality or legitimacy.
claims.Review rule: Separate editorial review from payment and publisher business model.

claims.Claim: Institutional repository deposit is distinct from public-domain status and can remain subject to copyright, embargo or access conditions.
claims.Review rule: Record version, licence, embargo and repository access.

claims.Claim: Institutional review board approval is a permission and oversight state, not proof that research is risk-free or ethically unproblematic.
claims.Review rule: Track protocol adherence, adverse events, consent and continuing review.

claims.Claim: Informed consent documents participation authority but does not eliminate power imbalance, misunderstanding or later harm.
claims.Review rule: Examine comprehension, voluntariness, dependency and withdrawal rights.

claims.Claim: A research misconduct allegation is not a finding; a retraction is not automatically proof that every author committed misconduct.
claims.Review rule: Preserve allegation, inquiry, investigation, finding, correction and sanction states.

claims.Claim: University ownership or patent management of an invention does not establish that the institution alone created its value or that commercialisation maximises public benefit.
claims.Review rule: Track funding, inventors, institutional rights, licensees and public obligations.

claims.Claim: FERPA or another student privacy regime conditions access and disclosure; it does not give the institution unrestricted ownership of student data.
claims.Review rule: Record legal basis, purpose, recipient, redisclosure and retention.

claims.Claim: A learning-analytics risk score is a prediction based on selected data, not a diagnosis of ability, motivation or inevitable dropout.
claims.Review rule: Track model validation, missing data, intervention and outcomes.

claims.Claim: A plagiarism similarity score or AI-detection output is not by itself proof of plagiarism, cheating or authorship.
claims.Review rule: Require human review, source comparison, student explanation and due process.

claims.Claim: Digital credentials can improve verification and portability but technical validity does not establish programme quality or labour-market recognition.
claims.Review rule: Separate cryptographic validity, issuer authority, learning outcomes and recognition.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of education power combines admission, price, aid, status, curriculum, assessment, credential, research, data and outcome records rather than treating one ranking, degree or score as decisive.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation before classifying quality, exclusion or value.

claims.Claim: Birth registration creates legal visibility and evidence of identity; it does not create the child's humanity, family bonds or full citizenship rights by itself.
claims.Review rule: Separate biological event, registration, certificate, nationality and service eligibility.

claims.Claim: Legal parentage, genetic parentage, gestational connection and day-to-day caregiving are distinct relationships that can coincide or diverge.
claims.Review rule: Record each basis of relationship and the authority determining it.

claims.Claim: Marriage or household membership does not establish equal access to money, shared preferences, safety or complete resource pooling.
claims.Review rule: Measure intra-household control and access rather than inferring unity.

claims.Claim: A custody, guardianship or foster-care order allocates protective responsibilities; it does not constitute ownership of a child or dependent adult.
claims.Review rule: Preserve rights-holder status, fiduciary duty and review mechanisms.

claims.Claim: A child-support or maintenance order establishes an obligation, not actual payment, full cost recovery or satisfactory caregiving.
claims.Review rule: Track assessment, order, withholding, payment, arrears and enforcement separately.

claims.Claim: Cross-border maintenance cooperation creates procedures for recognition and recovery; it does not guarantee prompt or complete collection.
claims.Review rule: Record treaty coverage, central-authority action, debtor location and actual recovery.

claims.Claim: Parental, maternity, paternity or carers' leave entitlement is distinct from income replacement, employer approval, uptake and return to work.
claims.Review rule: Track legal entitlement, benefit payment, leave taken and employment restoration.

claims.Claim: A right to request flexible working does not establish a right to the exact arrangement requested.
claims.Review rule: Record request, employer response, reason, appeal and actual arrangement.

claims.Claim: Unpaid care is economically productive and socially valuable, but time-use estimates do not measure care quality, consent or individual burden perfectly.
claims.Review rule: Preserve hours, tasks, intensity, choice and effect on paid work separately.

claims.Claim: Paid care does not automatically eliminate unpaid family care; formal and informal care often complement or substitute for each other.
claims.Review rule: Track service hours, unmet need and household time before and after formal care.

claims.Claim: Childcare eligibility, subsidy approval and provider enrolment are separate states; none guarantees a nearby, affordable or high-quality place.
claims.Review rule: Track capacity, waiting list, price, location, schedule and quality.

claims.Claim: A childcare licence or quality rating is a regulatory signal, not a guarantee of every daily interaction, developmental outcome or absence of harm.
claims.Review rule: Preserve inspection date, deficiencies, correction and ongoing monitoring.

claims.Claim: A family benefit or tax credit raises disposable resources but does not establish that the full cost of children, disability or care has been met.
claims.Review rule: Compare benefit value with household need, price and service availability.

claims.Claim: Benefit eligibility is distinct from application, approval, receipt, adequacy and continuity.
claims.Review rule: Build a state machine from legal coverage to realised payment.

claims.Claim: A survivor or dependent benefit is derived from legal and contribution rules; it is not evidence of household dependency, closeness or equal allocation.
claims.Review rule: Preserve contributor record, beneficiary status, family maximum and payment.

claims.Claim: A child-protection referral or risk score is not a finding of abuse, neglect or future harm.
claims.Review rule: Require investigation evidence, human judgment, notice and review.

claims.Claim: Emergency removal is a temporary protective state and does not settle permanent parental fitness, custody or adoption.
claims.Review rule: Preserve emergency basis, hearing, services, review and permanency decision.

claims.Claim: An adoption decree creates legal parentage but does not erase origin, identity, medical history or every prior relationship.
claims.Review rule: Track consent, origin records, recognition and post-adoption rights.

claims.Claim: Treaty-conforming intercountry adoption reduces defined risks but does not guarantee that no illicit practice, coercion or later harm occurred.
claims.Review rule: Preserve central-authority records, consents, payments and long-term outcomes.

claims.Claim: A will, trust or beneficiary designation transfers legal claims; it does not reveal the full family's economic contribution, need or moral entitlement.
claims.Review rule: Separate legal entitlement from contribution, control and beneficial enjoyment.

claims.Claim: Trust assets, trustee control and beneficiary interests are distinct; a beneficiary does not necessarily own or control underlying assets.
claims.Review rule: Record settlor, legal title, discretion, distribution rights and protectors.

claims.Claim: Assisted-reproduction consent, genetic connection, gestation, intent and legal parentage are separate states governed differently across jurisdictions.
claims.Review rule: Preserve each relationship, consent event and court or registry decision.

claims.Claim: A total fertility rate, dependency ratio or population projection is an aggregate scenario, not a measure of individual preference or deterministic destiny.
claims.Review rule: Record assumptions, intervals, migration and scenario revisions.

claims.Claim: Automated family-benefit or child-welfare systems can standardise processing, but their outputs are not neutral, infallible or self-executing legal findings.
claims.Review rule: Require validation, explainability, correction, human review and appeal.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of family and care power combines civil status, household resources, time use, service access, benefit payment, judicial orders and realised outcomes rather than treating one certificate, score or demographic indicator as decisive.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation before classifying dependency, support, neglect or family wellbeing.

claims.Claim: Registered agricultural title is not equivalent to possession, cultivation rights, water rights, beneficial control or customary legitimacy.
claims.Review rule: Review title, possession, use, water and customary records separately.

claims.Claim: A land investment or lease does not by itself establish displacement, dispossession or beneficial development.
claims.Review rule: Require transaction, consent, livelihood and outcome evidence.

claims.Claim: Genetic, deposited, protected, licensed, certified and farm-saved seed states are legally and operationally distinct.
claims.Related IDs: MECH-947; MECH-948; MECH-949; MECH-950; MECH-951; MECH-952; MECH-953; MECH-954
claims.Review rule: Track material identity, custody, legal right, licence and reproduction separately.

claims.Claim: Plant-variety protection or a commercial seed licence does not establish ownership of every farm, harvest or food product using that variety.
claims.Review rule: Retain universal ownership claims only as unsupported boundaries.

claims.Claim: Fertilizer production, physical supply, dealer inventory, farmer affordability and timely application are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile production, trade, retail, credit and farm-use data.

claims.Claim: Crop-protection authorization is not proof of zero health or ecological risk, and an allegation of harm is not proof of causation.
claims.Review rule: Track approved use, exposure, monitoring, finding and remedy.

claims.Claim: A formal water right or allocation is not equivalent to reliable physical delivery or safely managed drinking water.
claims.Review rule: Separate legal allocation, infrastructure delivery, availability, quality and affordability.

claims.Claim: Water scarcity can arise from hydrology, climate, infrastructure, demand, allocation and governance; it should not be attributed to one actor without specific evidence.
claims.Review rule: Test actor-specific conduct against physical and institutional alternatives.

claims.Claim: Agricultural loan approval, disbursement, productive use, repayment and restructuring are separate transaction states.
claims.Review rule: Build loan-level state transitions where data permit.

claims.Claim: A crop-insurance policy is not equivalent to coverage of the realized peril, a valid claim, a timely payment or full economic recovery.
claims.Review rule: Track peril, trigger, basis risk, claim, adjustment, payment and uncovered loss.

claims.Claim: Agricultural labour recruitment, legal status, payroll responsibility, workplace control and safety enforcement may be allocated across different actors.
claims.Review rule: Identify recruiter, employer, host, payer and inspector separately.

claims.Claim: Cooperative status does not prove democratic member control, equal benefit or freedom from managerial capture.
claims.Review rule: Review bylaws, voting, patronage, board control and realized distributions.

claims.Claim: A contract-farming agreement coordinates production but does not by itself prove guaranteed income, fair bargaining power or buyer control over every farm decision.
claims.Review rule: Separate written terms, input dependence, rejection risk and realized payment.

claims.Claim: A warehouse receipt is not equivalent to verified, unencumbered and immediately deliverable commodity inventory.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile receipt, registry, inspection, custody and physical stock.

claims.Claim: Reported strategic reserve volume is not equivalent to usable, rotated or immediately releasable food supply.
claims.Review rule: Audit stock quality, location, encumbrance, release authority and delivery.

claims.Claim: Agricultural futures notional, market position, hedge effectiveness and final physical exposure are distinct.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile derivatives positions with physical inventories and cash prices.

claims.Claim: Commodity futures are not established as the sole cause of food-price inflation.
claims.Review rule: Estimate trading effects alongside supply, energy, exchange-rate, trade and policy channels.

claims.Claim: Farm-gate, wholesale, import-parity, futures, administered and retail prices are different price states.
claims.Review rule: Use product-, place-, quality- and date-matched price reconciliation.

claims.Claim: SPS and phytosanitary measures can protect health and affect trade; neither protective purpose nor disguised restriction should be presumed without evidence.
claims.Review rule: Track risk assessment, standard, certificate, border action, review and trade effect.

claims.Claim: A food-safety licence, inspection or certificate is not proof of continuing compliance or absence of contamination.
claims.Review rule: Track inspections, testing, incidents, recalls and remediation over time.

claims.Claim: Food availability is not equivalent to household economic access, dietary quality, intra-household allocation or realized nutrition.
claims.Review rule: Combine supply, price, income, diet, health, sanitation and care evidence.

claims.Claim: School-meal or food-assistance eligibility is not equivalent to receipt, consumption, nutritional adequacy or downstream outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Track enrolment, delivery, redemption, consumption and outcome states.

claims.Claim: Humanitarian food assistance can create influence or conditionality in specific cases, but the claim that all food aid is covert geopolitical coercion is unsupported.
claims.Review rule: Require programme-specific mandate, condition, conduct and outcome evidence.

claims.Claim: Climate scenarios and remote-sensing classifications are probabilistic or model-based inputs, not deterministic harvest findings.
claims.Review rule: Require uncertainty, calibration and ground-truth disclosure.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of provisioning power combines tenure, water, inputs, finance, labour, inventory, trade, price, safety, assistance, nutrition and ecological outcomes rather than treating one title, certificate, price or score as decisive.
claims.Review rule: Apply cross-system reconciliation before classifying control, scarcity, access or wellbeing.

claims.Claim: Climate observations, reanalysis products, attribution studies, scenarios and policy commitments are distinct evidentiary states and should not be collapsed into one climate fact.
claims.Review rule: Verify the observation, method, uncertainty range, scenario assumptions and institutional use separately.

claims.Claim: International coordination, common assessments and treaty reporting do not establish one unified actor commanding all climate policy or environmental outcomes.
claims.Review rule: Retain as unsupported unless direct evidence of unified command, authority and execution is produced.

claims.Claim: Corporate inventories require an organizational boundary and scope classification; Scope 1, 2, 3 and financed emissions are not interchangeable measures.
claims.Review rule: Record the reporting boundary, consolidation approach, estimation method, denominator and reporting period.

claims.Claim: Disclosure, assurance and a transition plan do not establish physical emissions reduction or full value-chain coverage.
claims.Review rule: Trace assurance scope and subsequent realised emissions rather than inferring outcome from publication.

claims.Claim: Tax liability, allowance creation, allocation, trade, surrender and border adjustment are separate legal and market states.
claims.Related IDs: V30PRICE-001; V30PRICE-003; V30PRICE-008; MECH-1025; MECH-1028; MECH-1030
claims.Review rule: Audit the cap or rate, exemptions, allocation, registry state, surrender and enforcement separately.

claims.Claim: A carbon price does not possess complete control over technology, output, trade, distribution or realised emissions.
claims.Review rule: Retain as unsupported unless a causal design shows the price alone determines the claimed outcome.

claims.Claim: Methodology approval, host authorization, validation, verification, issuance, custody, transfer and retirement are separate carbon-credit states.
claims.Related IDs: V30CRED-001; V30CRED-002; V30CRED-005; MECH-1031; MECH-1033; MECH-1034
claims.Review rule: Require the project, methodology version, host decision, verifier, serial numbers and registry transaction.

claims.Claim: A carbon-credit purchase or retirement does not by itself establish additionality, permanence, ecological equivalence or neutralization of the buyer's emissions.
claims.Review rule: Separate credit quality, accounting treatment and public claim language.

claims.Claim: Emission permits, release reports, chemical listings, waste notifications and cleanup orders are different regulatory instruments.
claims.Related IDs: V30POLL-001; V30POLL-002; V30POLL-005; MECH-1037; MECH-1038; MECH-1039
claims.Review rule: Trace permit conditions, monitored releases, inspections, violations and remediation.

claims.Claim: Regulatory authorization or disclosed releases do not establish continuous compliance, safe cumulative exposure or completed remediation.
claims.Review rule: Compare reported data with monitoring, enforcement and health or ecological outcomes.

claims.Claim: Assessment scoping, impact assessment, consultation, consent, permit conditions and grievance review are separate procedural states.
claims.Related IDs: V30PERMIT-001; V30PERMIT-004; V30PERMIT-006; MECH-1043; MECH-1044; MECH-1045
claims.Review rule: Record timing, information access, decision authority, conditions, review and remedy.

claims.Claim: Consultation does not necessarily establish consent, equal bargaining power or protection from project harm.
claims.Review rule: Verify which rights-holders participated, what changed and whether commitments were enforceable.

claims.Claim: A biodiversity target, protected-area designation, OECM recognition and measured ecological condition are different states.
claims.Review rule: Track legal status, governance, rights, funding, ecological indicators and enforcement.

claims.Claim: Nature-related disclosure and biodiversity finance can improve visibility and funding without proving ecological recovery or equitable governance.
claims.Review rule: Trace use of funds, ecological baselines, additionality and rights-holder outcomes.

claims.Claim: Forest title, use permission, carbon authority, reference level, credit entitlement and community rights are non-equivalent claims.
claims.Review rule: Map the legal holder, land tenure, carbon right, benefit-sharing rule and registry state separately.

claims.Claim: A forest or nature credit does not itself prove avoided conversion, permanence, no leakage or fair benefit sharing.
claims.Review rule: Verify the counterfactual, monitoring period, reversal rules, tenure and distribution of proceeds.

claims.Claim: Fund accreditation, proposal approval, commitment, disbursement, project completion and climate outcome are separate financing states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile approved, committed and disbursed amounts with implementation and ex-post outcomes.

claims.Claim: A green label, transition framework or stress test does not by itself establish additional climate finance, solvency or emissions reduction.
claims.Review rule: Trace instrument terms, use of proceeds, external review and realised transition expenditure.

claims.Claim: Adaptation planning, warning issuance, service availability, protective action and reduced loss are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Audit who received the warning or service, acted, remained exposed and bore residual loss.

claims.Claim: Managed retreat or property acquisition must separate voluntary agreement, valuation, relocation support, tenure, community continuity and realised safety.
claims.Review rule: Record consent, compensation, debt treatment, destination risk and post-relocation outcomes.

claims.Claim: Disaster exposure, insured exposure, parametric trigger, payout, public expenditure and total economic loss are different quantities.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile the index, attachment, payout, timing, uncovered loss and final fiscal incidence.

claims.Claim: Contingent credit, insurance, catastrophe securities and loss-and-damage funds change liquidity and allocation but do not eliminate physical or social loss.
claims.Related IDs: V30LOSS-004; V30LOSS-005; V30LOSS-010; MECH-1072; MECH-1074; MECH-1075
claims.Review rule: Trace who receives cash, who repays debt, who remains uncovered and who ultimately absorbs the loss.

claims.Claim: A scientific assessment, attribution result or aggregate emissions estimate does not by itself prove that one defendant legally caused every component of one disaster.
claims.Review rule: Require separate evidence on contribution, exposure, vulnerability, duty, causation and remedy.

claims.Claim: Application, standing, jurisdiction, advisory interpretation, judgment, remedy, appeal and enforcement are separate climate-litigation states.
claims.Review rule: Record the procedural state, legal duty, remedy ordered and implementation status.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of climate and environmental power combines observations, inventories, permissions, prices, registries, participation, finance, realised impacts, final loss incidence and enforceable remedy rather than treating one model, price, credit, permit or judgment as decisive.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation and a reviewable record before classifying responsibility, protection, transition or remedy.

claims.Claim: Threat assessment, political claim, domestic authorization, international legal basis and operational order are separate institutional states.
claims.Review rule: Require exact authority, date, scope, legal basis and issuing institution.

claims.Claim: Alliance consultation, a collective-defence obligation, national assistance decision, force contribution and operational command are not equivalent.
claims.Review rule: Record treaty trigger, requested assistance, national decision, caveats and command chain.

claims.Claim: Defence authority, appropriation, obligation, contract, production, delivery, readiness and use are separate fiscal and operational states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile budgets, obligations, awards, accepted deliveries, inventory and readiness.

claims.Claim: A Foreign Military Sales notification or Letter of Offer and Acceptance is not identical to production, delivery, operational availability or use.
claims.Review rule: Track case status, financing, implementation agency, delivery and end-use monitoring.

claims.Claim: Export notification, licence, customs release, shipment, delivery, end-user possession, retransfer and lawful end use are separate arms-transfer states.
claims.Review rule: Require transaction-level licensing, logistics, custody and monitoring records.

claims.Claim: Industrial contract value and nominal capacity do not equal accepted output, usable stockpile, serviceability or sustained delivery to operational units.
claims.Review rule: Measure throughput, acceptance, storage condition, maintenance, transport and consumption.

claims.Claim: Intelligence collection, assessment, dissemination, political acceptance and operational use are distinct states with different authorities and uncertainty.
claims.Review rule: Preserve provenance, confidence, dissent, dissemination and decision records.

claims.Claim: Target nomination, validation, legal review, proportionality assessment, command authorization, execution and civilian-harm assessment are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Audit the complete target and command chain rather than one intelligence or strike record.

claims.Claim: International humanitarian law imposes limits on means and methods of warfare and protects civilians and persons no longer participating in hostilities.
claims.Review rule: Identify conflict classification, protected status, applicable rules and evidence of compliance.

claims.Claim: A civilian-harm report, condolence payment, administrative finding and criminal judgment establish different responsibility and remedy states.
claims.Review rule: Separate incident verification, administrative response, command accountability and adjudication.

claims.Claim: Treaty membership, declaration, safeguard, monitoring signal, inspection, compliance conclusion and enforcement response are separate WMD-control states.
claims.Review rule: Record access, data, technical finding, legal conclusion and institutional response.

claims.Claim: An emergency declaration is not a permanent suspension of law; trigger, scope, duration, derogation and review remain distinct.
claims.Review rule: Track legal basis, non-derogable rights, renewal, oversight and termination.

claims.Claim: Occupation authority is a legally constrained administrative relationship, not sovereign title or unrestricted ownership of occupied territory.
claims.Review rule: Separate effective control, temporary administration, property rules and final status.

claims.Claim: Detention classification, registration, custody, treatment, independent access, review, transfer and release are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Require person-level custody and review records.

claims.Claim: Humanitarian need, appeal, donor commitment, disbursement, access, shipment, receipt, coverage and adequacy are not equivalent.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile finance, access, logistics, beneficiary receipt and outcome data.

claims.Claim: Refugee registration, asylum status, internal-displacement recording, assistance and durable solution are separate protection states.
claims.Review rule: Preserve status, location, household composition, protection and solution history.

claims.Claim: Ceasefire signature, entry into force, monitoring, violation report, attribution, response and durable cessation of hostilities are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Audit text, maps, timelines, verified incidents and enforcement.

claims.Claim: A peacekeeping mandate, authorized strength, deployed personnel, freedom of movement and realized civilian protection are distinct states.
claims.Review rule: Track authorization, generation, deployment, mobility, action and outcome.

claims.Claim: Disarmament, demobilization, reinsertion, reintegration and security-sector reform are distinct processes whose sequencing affects recurrence risk.
claims.Review rule: Measure weapons custody, participant status, economic integration and institutional legitimacy.

claims.Claim: Damage assessment, recovery plan, pledge, commitment, disbursement, procurement, completion and maintained service are separate reconstruction states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile project, contract, cash-flow, delivery, audit and service records.

claims.Claim: Property claim, adjudication, restitution order, registry update, possession and compensation are separate post-conflict remedy states.
claims.Review rule: Require claimant identity, pre-conflict rights, decision, registry and physical implementation.

claims.Claim: The existence of monetary, debt or resource interests does not prove that those interests are the sole cause of every war.
claims.Review rule: Require conflict-specific evidence and compare strategic, ideological, territorial and domestic explanations.

claims.Claim: Funding, ownership, investment, licensing or supply does not by itself prove operational command over a military force or specific attack.
claims.Review rule: Require documented command authority, orders and operational control.

claims.Claim: An aggregate casualty or damage estimate does not by itself establish complete actor-specific legal liability for every recorded harm.
claims.Review rule: Require incident-level attribution, applicable law, due process and remedy analysis.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of conflict power combines legal authority, budgets, contracts, transfer records, intelligence provenance, command decisions, civilian outcomes, access, peace implementation, reconstruction and enforceable remedy.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation and reviewable provenance before classifying command, protection, responsibility or final loss.

claims.Claim: Nationality is a legal status produced by applicable law and evidence; birth, registration, certificate, passport and effective protection are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Require applicable nationality law, civil record, administrative decision and review history.

claims.Claim: Birth registration supports legal identity but does not by itself establish citizenship in every jurisdiction.
claims.Review rule: Separate registration, parentage, territory, descent and nationality attribution.

claims.Claim: Naturalization eligibility, application, approval, oath and effective enjoyment of citizenship rights are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Track each procedural state and post-decision documentation.

claims.Claim: Deprivation of nationality requires separate evidence of legal ground, notice, decision, review and statelessness consequences.
claims.Review rule: Require due process, proportionality and alternative nationality evidence.

claims.Claim: Passport possession establishes a travel-document state, not unconditional entry or complete proof of all nationality questions.
claims.Review rule: Separate document validity, visa, admissibility and nationality.

claims.Claim: Visa application, biometric collection, adjudication, issuance, boarding and admission are separate mobility states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile carrier, consular and port-of-entry records.

claims.Claim: A carrier boarding denial is not the same as a sovereign visa refusal or port-of-entry decision.
claims.Review rule: Identify delegated duty, legal basis, reason and remedy.

claims.Claim: Refugee claim registration, interview, recognition, complementary protection, appeal and durable solution are separate protection states.
claims.Review rule: Preserve claim and status history.

claims.Claim: Resettlement referral, selection, security screening, admission and integration are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Track each authority and transfer stage.

claims.Claim: API, PNR, watchlist and biometric matches are distinct data products; a match or risk score is not a final legal finding.
claims.Review rule: Require identity resolution, reason, human review and outcome.

claims.Claim: Recruitment licence, job offer, work authorization, employment contract, payroll and wage receipt are separate labour-migration states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile recruiter, sponsor, employer and worker records.

claims.Claim: Employer sponsorship can create lawful mobility while also concentrating bargaining and status power in the sponsor relationship.
claims.Review rule: Measure portability, exit rights, enforcement and actual worker alternatives.

claims.Claim: Recruitment fees, wage deductions and migration debt must be traced separately from contractual salary and remittance flows.
claims.Review rule: Require lender, recruiter, payroll, transfer and repayment records.

claims.Claim: Family relationship, sponsor capacity, best interests, visa decision and actual reunification are separate states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile family, civil-status, welfare and travel records.

claims.Claim: DNA evidence can support biological kinship but does not by itself establish legal parentage, caregiving history or the best interests of a child.
claims.Review rule: Preserve consent, chain of custody and non-biological evidence.

claims.Claim: Detention ground, custody, healthcare, judicial review, release and removal are separate liberty and enforcement states.
claims.Review rule: Require person-level custody chronology.

claims.Claim: A return decision does not establish lawful execution where non-refoulement, identity, travel-document or judicial-review questions remain.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile protection screening and final movement.

claims.Claim: Displacement registration, assistance, property claim, return, local integration and relocation are separate protection and remedy states.
claims.Review rule: Track household, location, property and solution history.

claims.Claim: Remittance initiation, FX conversion, settlement, cash-out and household receipt are separate payment states.
claims.Review rule: Reconcile provider, bank, agent and recipient records.

claims.Claim: Integration requires realized access to housing, health, education, work, language, social protection and political voice rather than formal status alone.
claims.Review rule: Measure service availability, take-up, quality and outcomes.

claims.Claim: A migration database, biometric match or algorithmic score does not by itself constitute a lawful, accurate or reviewable status decision.
claims.Review rule: Require provenance, model governance, human authority and correction.

claims.Claim: Possession or absence of one identity or travel document does not conclusively determine nationality, belonging or all legal rights.
claims.Review rule: Require underlying law, facts and review.

claims.Claim: Irregular migration status does not by itself establish criminality, dangerousness or loss of labour and human rights.
claims.Review rule: Separate administrative, labour, protection and criminal-law states.

claims.Claim: Remittances, diaspora investment or cross-border social ties do not by themselves establish foreign command, disloyalty or covert coordination.
claims.Review rule: Require transaction-specific and authority-specific evidence.

claims.Claim: The strongest evidence of mobility power combines civil status, nationality law, travel documents, visa and border records, protection decisions, labour and family states, detention and return review, payment flows, data provenance and realized access or remedy.
claims.Review rule: Require cross-system reconciliation before classifying status, exclusion, control, integration or final incidence.
